home_pitcher_note: Lohse's long winter of uncertainty came to an end when he hooked on with the Cardinals, and the club is delighted to have him. While the projections for his payday were fairly outlandish, Lohse has been a useful pitcher for most of his career. He has four seasons of at least 180 innings and five years with 30 or more starts. Lohse had been scheduled for one more tuneup in a simulated game, but thanks to the rainout, he'll go on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Wells signed a $3.1 million, one-year deal with the Rockies this winter and hoped to make the starting rotation, but his inefficiency early in camp led the club to put him in long relief. Wells disagreed with the decision, but pitched better in his last two spring appearances as the Rockies prepared him for bullpen work. Now, however, after Friday's opener was postponed and no rotation member was available, Wells gets a chance to do what he wanted all along.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer was a revelation for the Cardinals after they plucked him off waivers from the Royals. He still had some trouble keeping the ball in the park, but he did an excellent job of corralling his walk rate. It remains to be seen how Wellemeyer will fare as a full-time Major League starter, having made his first 11 career starts last season in St. Louis. But pitching coach Dave Duncan is a big believer, and that's a good ally to have.
away_pitcher_note: Cook was the Rockies' No. 1 starter last season and struggled to a 5-6, 4.68 ERA performance before the All-Star break. He turned hot in the second half, going 3-1, 2.41 in six starts before suffering an oblique injury.

home_pitcher_note: It seems like forever that Thompson has been a swingman trying to secure a starting job with the Cardinals, but he's been in the organization for fewer than three full seasons. Still, this is a new opportunity for Thompson, getting the call to join the starting rotation from the beginning of the year. His sinker is an exceptional pitch with serious movement, and when it's good, he can throw it a huge percentage of the time.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez gave the Rockies a lift in 16 games after being called up in August. But before being promoted, consistency was an issue, and fastball command was a problem throughout Spring Training.

home_pitcher_note: Considering the skepticism with which his transition was met, Looper's first year as a starter actually went pretty OK. He made 30 starts and pitched 175 innings, and for the most part he was reasonably effective. Looper's ground-ball rate dipped significantly, though, and that's something he'd like to see change. He doesn't have the kind of repertoire to succeed for long as a fly-ball pitcher.
away_pitcher_note: Perez will face the Cardinals for the 12th time in his career. He is 3-4 with an 8.46 ERA against them. Perez is looking for his first winning season since the 2004 season, when he was with the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: If Wainwright can pitch a full season like he did in the second half in 2007, he'll be a Cy Young Award contender. He believes he can. After a slow start in '07, Wainwright posted a 2.71 ERA with 77 strikeouts, 30 walks and only four homers allowed in 99 2/3 innings after the All-Star break. He pitched two excellent games against the Nationals last season, but got minimal help from his offense and bullpen, and the Cardinals lost both games. Wainwright's first '07 start was washed out after three innings.
away_pitcher_note: His new high-leg delivery is starting to impress teams. The Braves, for example, noticed that the new maneuver helped Chico add more miles to his fastball. In the past, the Braves knew Chico as a guy who threw in the low-to-mid 80s. But they were surprised to see that Chico was throwing in the 90s during Spring Training.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse did everything that was asked of him in his Cardinals debut, pitching five shutout innings against a good Rockies club. His limited work in spring contributed to his being removed without facing a batter in the sixth, but he should build up his innings and pitches quickly. Lohse had a rough time against Washington last year, allowing 15 earned runs in 16 2/3 innings over five outings (three starts).
away_pitcher_note: The Nationals placed closer Chad Cordero on the disabled list on Friday night and recalled left-hander John Lannan, who will pitch against the Cardinals on Sunday at Busch Stadium. The Nationals needed a fifth starter because they didn't want right-hander Tim Redding to throw on short rest. Lannan was the Nationals' best pitcher during Spring Training, going 2-0 with a 2.18 ERA in five games. He was the Nationals' Minor League pitcher of the year in 2007.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez will pitch the home opener looking for his first win of the season. The left-hander took a no-decision on April 2 against the Padres after yielding four runs over five frames. Rodriguez performs well at Minute Maid Park, as evidenced by his 6-3 record and 2.94 ERA at home last year. He made two starts against the Cardinals in '07, going 1-1 with a 2.40 ERA. He yielded four runs over a combined 15 innings. Lifetime versus St. Louis, Rodriguez is 1-4 with a 6.59 ERA over six games.
away_pitcher_note: The story for Wellemeyer remains the same: he's effective, but he needs to be more efficient. His first start of 2008 was much like a lot of his starts from 2007, as Wellemeyer tossed five good innings but threw too many pitches to be brought out for more than that. He's got the stuff to put hitters away, but his command is iffy at times. He's made three career relief appearances at Minute Maid Park, and the numbers aren't pretty -- a 14.54 ERA in 4 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Chacon had an impressive first game with the Astros, pitching six solid innings against the Padres and getting a no-decision. He gave up two runs on five hits. He gave up a two-run homer to Kevin Kouzmanoff in the first inning, but settled down. He did have a little trouble with his command, walking four, but he also struck out four and got stronger as the game went on. The right-hander went 4-3 with a 3.52 ERA over 60 relief appearances for the Pirates in 2007, and was 1-1 with a 5.59 ERA over four starts. He started last year in the bullpen, moved to the rotation in May and back to the bullpen to finish the season. It appears that he will be part of the Astros' starting rotation this season. As manager Cecil Cooper noted, "if he pitches like he did against the Padres, he's going to win a lot of games for us."
away_pitcher_note: Thompson showed just how good he can be in his first start. Now he just has to do it again. The right-hander has a wicked sinker, but at his best, he can mix in a quality changeup and breaking ball as well, just as he did on Thursday. The pressure is on Thompson, because Joel Pineiro could return from injury as soon as Thompson's next scheduled turn. Either Thompson or Todd Wellemeyer would likely be the odd man out once Pineiro comes back.

home_pitcher_note: Sampson took a no-decision but pitched brilliantly against the Cubs on April 4, holding them to two runs over 6 2/3 innings. Sampson retired 13 of the first 14 batters he faced and yielded three hits over the first six innings. The right-hander was 1-1 with a 4.26 ERA over two games against the Cardinals last year, allowing six runs over 12 2/3 innings. Lifetime versus St. Louis, Sampson is 1-1 with a 4.15 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: This is what the Cardinals hoped they would be getting when they moved Looper to the starting rotation last season. He was quite effective at times in '07, but often didn't resemble the groundball specialist he had been in previous years. But in his 2008 debut, Looper induced 12 groundball outs against just three in the air, a very encouraging sign as he moves into his second season of starting.

home_pitcher_note: Correia pitched relatively well last Saturday against Milwaukee, considering he had endured a stomach virus all week that caused him to drop 12 pounds, from 200 to 188. The weight loss diminished Correia's velocity slightly, but he managed to last six innings, allowing four runs and six hits. A San Diego native who still lives there in the offseason, Correia is 1-0 with a 4.44 ERA in 15 lifetime appearances (mostly in relief) against the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: After a slow start in 2007, Wainwright posted a 2.71 ERA with 77 strikeouts, 30 walks and only four homers allowed in 99 2/3 innings after the All-Star break. Wainwright's first start was washed out after three innings, but he was strong in his second start on Saturday against Washington. Wainwright allowed two runs on eight hits over eight innings, with four strikeouts and one walk, to help the Cardinals defeat the Nationals, 5-4.
summary: 2008-04-10 - St. Louis Cardinals (1) @ San Francisco Giants (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Zito has lasted five innings in each of his first two starts. Although he lost last Sunday at Milwaukee, he emerged from the game feeling more comfortable about his pitching repertoire, which now lacks a fastball that travels in the upper-80 mph range and thus complements his offspeed deliveries. This will be Zito's first start of the season at AT&T Park, where he was 4-5 with a 4.34 ERA last year.
away_pitcher_note: A free agent who signed a one-year deal with the Cardinals in March, Lohse is off to a strong start with his new club after splitting time between Cincinnati and Philadelphia in 2006. The right-hander did not allow a run in his first two starts, covering 12 innings, while allowing just seven hits, striking out five and walking four. Now, he'll have to try to keep it up on the road for his next start.
summary: 2008-04-11 - St. Louis Cardinals (8) @ San Francisco Giants (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Cain, who often has lamented his control, walked nine batters in 10 innings over his first two starts. He endured a rough outing in the Giants' home opener Monday against San Diego, allowing five runs (four earned) and seven hits in 4 1/3 innings. Interestingly, the Cardinals are the only team that Cain has not faced in his two-plus Major League seasons.
away_pitcher_note: For most of his tenure as a Cardinals starter, Wellemeyer has been puzzling. His superficial results have looked good, but his peripheral stats have been dicey, and he's been inefficient. On Monday, though, he looked like he'd turned a corner. Wellemeyer's command was excellent, and his stuff remained strong. He was in control for six innings against a good lineup in a tough ballpark. If he pitches that well at a friendlier ballpark against a less-intimidating lineup, he'll have a big day.
summary: 2008-04-12 - St. Louis Cardinals (8) @ San Francisco Giants (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum bequeathed a 2-1 lead to the bullpen last Tuesday against San Diego in his most recent outing, which lasted six innings. But closer Brian Wilson allowed a ninth-inning run to blow the save and Lincecum's victory. Lincecum struck out seven in that game and now has 11 in 10 innings. He defeated the Cardinals in his only career appearance against them, allowing three runs in six innings in a 7-6 Giants win last July 7.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro pitched well enough and felt good enough that he'll make his first regular season start after only one Minor League rehab appearance. He was extremely sharp in that game, recovering after a shaky first inning to put up a solid outing. The Cardinals have emphasized aggressiveness with the fastball for Pineiro, and in his first go-round in St. Louis, it worked beautifully. If he can repeat his '07 Cardinals performance in '08, he'll be a major asset.
summary: 2008-04-13 - St. Louis Cardinals (4) @ San Francisco Giants (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Things are going well for Looper thus far, which allows the Cardinals to give everyone an extra day of rest after the off-day Monday. He hit higher readings on the radar gun in his last start than he usually has managed as a starter, a very encouraging sign. If Looper can keep getting the ball low in the strike zone while also sitting in the low 90s, it will be a good year for the veteran right-hander.
away_pitcher_note: Bush has lost both of his starts, though he didn't get many breaks on Wednesday against the Reds. He's 1-3 with a 7.61 ERA in four career starts against the Cardinals, and he may need a solid outing to hold on to his spot in the starting rotation. The Brewers will have right-hander Yovani Gallardo back from the disabled list as early as this weekend, so Bush, Carlos Villanueva or Manny Parra must be bounced from the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright's last outing was a strange one, with some hard-hit balls but six strikeouts and no walks. It ended with a loss, but the total picture for the Cardinals' No. 1 starter is very good so far: 10 strikeouts, one walk, one home run and a solid groundball ratio. The Brewers are a good test for any pitcher, but he pitched solidly against them last year, going 1-1 with a 3.00 ERA in two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Villanueva had no trouble at all with the top half of the Reds' potent batting order in his last start. The bottom five hitters, however, gave him trouble. He worked three full turns through the Cincinnati order and the top four hitters combined to go 0-for-11 with a walk. But the Reds' bottom five hitters combined to go 7-for-12 with four RBIs against Villanueva, with all four of the runs charged to the Brewers right-hander. He is 2-1 with a 2.70 ERA in eight career appearances against the Cards.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse finally gave up a run in his third St. Louis start, but he still pitched well enough for his second win. The Cardinals could easily be 3-0 in his games, since Lohse handed a lead to the bullpen in his debut, only to see it fade away. The right-hander has yet to allow a home run this year, which is a good way to keep winning even if your strikeout rate is low -- which his is through just three starts.
away_pitcher_note: The young lefty stayed out of trouble through three innings at Shea Stadium on Friday, but then faltered in the fourth, when New York scored three runs on four hits, a walk and a sacrifice fly. He was only at the 72-pitch mark, but was lifted for a pinch-hitter in the fifth inning when the Brewers had a runner at second base with two outs. Parra was not as sharp Friday as in his season debut, when he limited the Giants to three hits for his first Major League win. With Yovani Gallardo set to return from a rehab assignment, the team faces a difficult decision, and Parra's is one of the spots in doubt.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer is starting to show a bit of a pattern: he may require a quick hook. In his first game, he went five strong innings. In his second, he was rolling through six, only to flag in the seventh. And most recently, he ran into trouble in the sixth after five excellent innings. He needs to keep the ball in the park, but Wellemeyer's strikeout rate this year is exceptional at 10 per nine innings. That's a great indicator of continued success.
away_pitcher_note: Cain took a no-hitter into the seventh inning in Saturday's game against the Cardinals, the first time he's faced them. Albert Pujols led off the seventh with a booming double. Cain ended up allowing two runs on three hits with three walks and five strikeouts. In 16 innings this year, Cain has 15 strikeouts, but has walked 12.
summary: 2008-04-18 - San Francisco Giants (1) @ St. Louis Cardinals (11) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Well, the results can't be much worse. Pineiro was betrayed by a defensive misplay, ruled a hit, that should have saved him several earned runs in his first start. Even so, he didn't look like somebody fully ready to pitch in regular season games. This will be his second start after missing the season's first two weeks with a lat strain. The hope -- and expectation -- is that he'll be improved the second time around.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum struck out 11 in his most recent outing last Sunday against St. Louis, tying a San Francisco Giants record for the most strikeouts in a six-inning outing. Lincecum matched Fred Breining (1982), Osvaldo Fernandez (1996), Russ Ortiz (2000) and Matt Cain (2006). The Giants are 3-0 when Lincecum goes to the mound, including his four-inning relief appearance April 2 at Los Angeles after the threat of inclement weather -- which came to pass -- prompted manager Bruce Bochy to scratch him from his scheduled start.
summary: 2008-04-19 - San Francisco Giants (3) @ St. Louis Cardinals (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Looper wasn't happy at all with his last start, but he still managed to dodge five walks and get out of it with only one run allowed. That's a good sign for a pitcher who was either very good or very bad last year. If he can turn less-than-sharp days into respectable results, he could have a significantly improved 2008. Looper was also much better in daylight in 2007; this is his first daytime start in '08.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez has sandwiched two mediocre outings around an outstanding one. He allowed seven runs in four innings at Milwaukee in his season debut and blanked San Diego for six innings in his next appearance but was erratic on Monday against Arizona, allowing four runs (three earned) in five innings. Sanchez, 25, still struggles to find a consistent release point. When he does, he can be devastating, as his 21 strikeouts in 15 innings demonstrate.
summary: 2008-04-20 - San Francisco Giants (8) @ St. Louis Cardinals (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: It's a rematch for Villanueva of Wednesday in St. Louis, where he lasted only 4 2/3 innings and allowed five runs. Albert Pujols jumped on a 3-and-0 pitch in the first inning for a two-run double, then Villanueva locked with Rick Ankiel in a 17-pitch battle that ended in a walk. He needed 45 pitches to escape the first inning, ensuring a short night. He dropped to 2-2 against St. Louis with the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright tired a bit at the end of his last start, but nonetheless was charged with only two runs -- one earned -- in 7 2/3 innings. He's getting quick groundball outs, throwing strikes and keeping the ball in the park, and those things add up to pitching deep into games. Wainwright has gone at least seven innings in each of his three starts, which has been a valuable asset to a team that has relied heavily on its bullpen at times.

home_pitcher_note: Parra has not pitched more than four innings since his first outing of the season. In his last start Thursday in St. Louis, Parra allowed three earned runs on five hits, including a two-run fourth-inning single by Cardinals pitcher Kyle Lohse. Parra also gave up a homer, and issued a season-high five walks in Thursday's game that was won by the Brewers on Prince Fielder's two-run home run in the 10th inning.
away_pitcher_note: When you drive in as many runs as you allow, and your ERA goes up, it's probably been a pretty good season thus far. Lohse turned in another solid game, and he's showing no signs of backsliding. Lohse is throwing strikes -- five walks allowed in 24 1/3 innings. And he has yet to allow a home run in a Cardinals uniform. As long as he keeps limiting the free passes and the long balls, it's going to be a nice year.

home_pitcher_note: Though Snell limited the Cubs to three runs in six innings of work (all the runs coming in the fourth) in his last start, he was ultimately hurt by the Pirates' lack of run support. After struggling in his previous start, Snell slowed himself down and said that he tried not to think as much about the location of his pitches. As a result, Snell's command was much shaper. Snell has faced the Cardinals eight times (seven starts) in his career, and has a 3-3 record and 3.40 ERA against the club.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer keeps getting better and keeps strengthening his case to stay in the rotation even when some of the Cardinals' injured starters begin coming back. He's averaging more than a strikeout per inning and he's totaled 20 innings over his past three starts. Wellemeyer has displayed a newfound efficiency this year, and his stuff is still impressive. It's early, but he's emerging as one of the surprise players of 2008.

home_pitcher_note: Expected to anchor the top of the rotation, Gorzelanny has had his command in just one of his four starts this year. In his previous outing, the lefty exited before finishing the third, marking the second time this season he's been chased that early in a game. Gorzelanny is consistently leaving his pitches up, and he has vowed to make sure he takes more time in between pitches. Gorzelanny is 1-2 with a 3.04 ERA in four career starts against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro seems to be healthy, but he still doesn't look very sharp. He hasn't struck a batter out yet, and he's not even missing bats with any kind of frequency. He'll never be a dominating strikeout pitcher, but Pineiro does need to get to a point where he can get at least a few swings and misses. Facing a Pirates team that strikes out quite a bit, maybe this will be the day for him to get going.

home_pitcher_note: It was ugly last time out for Looper, but that was somewhat in tune with what the Cardinals saw last year. Looper has rarely been so-so as a starter. When he's good, he gets deep into games and keeps the ball on the ground. When he's bad, he gets pounded. Looper must make the most of his rocky games while continuing to churn out the occasional gem. He has yet to go more than six innings in a start this season.
away_pitcher_note: Chacon has been Houston's hard-luck pitcher. He's pitched well enough to be 4-0, but has four no-decisions for his efforts despite going six innings or more and allowing three earned runs or less in each of his starts. His ERA for the season is 2.77. In his most recent outing, he gave up three runs on seven hits in six innings against his former team, Colorado, but was not involved in the decision. He pitched eight scoreless innings at Philadelphia on April 15, but didn't get the win because of a blown save by Jose Valverde. Chacon faced St. Louis at Minute Maid Park on April 8 and limited them to three runs on four hits in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright keeps churning out quality starts, keeping the Cardinals in games and giving the bullpen a breather. He's done a lot of good things this year, like allowing only one home run all season, but his calling card has been innings. In every start this season, Wainwright has pitched at least seven innings -- and yet only once has he gone past 107 pitches. Wainwright continues to establish himself as one of the NL's best.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt earned his second win of the year with a convincing performance against the Padres on Monday, holding San Diego to three runs over seven innings. Oswalt said he finally had a feel for his breaking stuff, which eluded him in his first three outings. The right-hander has allowed four runs over his last two outings after losing his first three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse gave up more than two runs for the first time in a game this season when he allowed four in four innings in a 9-8 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers on Tuesday. Lohse walked two batters and was constantly behind in the count. "I can't fall behind that many guys," said Lohse. He was tagged for four earned runs on eight hits.
away_pitcher_note: Backe pitched well enough to win in his last outing on Tuesday but had to settle for a no-decision when the bullpen blew a four-run lead against the Padres. Backe yielded three runs, all on one home run by Adrian Gonzalez during his seven-inning outing. The right-hander has held opponents to three or fewer runs in four of his five outings this year.

home_pitcher_note: The Cardinals' rotation has surprised so far, and Todd Wellemeyer has been a big reason why. He has been impressive in his first full season as a starting pitcher. In his last outing, a no decision in Pittsburgh on Wednesday, he tossed six innings and surrendered four runs on seven hits. Despite not having his best stuff he battled and gave the club a chance to win.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo is off to a rough start to his 2008 season and has yet to pitch six innings. His latest outing came in Wednesday's 9-3 loss to the Astros where he was pummeled for eight earned runs and a season-high 10 hits over 3 2/3 innings. Arroyo and pitching coach Dick Pole have poured over video to see where the right-hander has gone wrong but have yet to come up with any solutions.

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro continued his mastery of the Pirates, tossing seven innings and allowing one run on four hits in a 6-2 Cards win on Thursday. Pineiro, who didn't have a strikeout in his first two starts, recorded six against the Pirates and only allowed one walk.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto lacked velocity and didn't have good location during a 5-3 loss to the Astros on Thursday. The 22-year-old gave up five earned runs and eight hits with two walks and two strikeouts over seven innings. Both of Cueto's strikeouts came in the first inning.

home_pitcher_note: Looper is getting more groundballs this season, and that's what he needs to do. However, he's threatening to resume his up-and-down pattern of a year ago. He has pitched very well at times, such as in his most recent start against Houston. He's also struggled badly, as he did five days earlier against the Giants.
away_pitcher_note: Harang can't buy a win lately. He's allowed two or fewer earned runs in five of his six starts, and has one victory to show for it. He pitched 7 1/3 strong innings against the San Francisco Giants on Friday night, but left the game without run support. He's 5-6 lifetime against the Cardinals, but beat them twice last year.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright is the undisputed ace of the Cardinals staff until Chris Carpenter returns. That means, among other things, that he's being worked hard. He's been extremely effective thus far, but he's already been pushed pretty hard twice this year. Wainwright receives an extra day of rest thanks to an off day, but it will be interesting to see how he recovers from a career-high 126-pitch outing.
away_pitcher_note: Hill was skipped in the rotation to give him extra time for side work, to keep the other starters on a five-day rotation, and to avoid having him face the Brewers. The Cubs want the lefty to be aggressive in his approach, and he's shown improvement. He won his only start against the Cardinals last season, giving up one run in seven innings. Hill did spend some time in the bullpen as a backup this week in case of emergency

home_pitcher_note: Lohse's strikeout rate is way down in the early going, but he's keeping the walks and home runs down as well. If he continues to do the last two, he can get away with the first. The Cubs, who several batters who have hit him very well over the years, present a challenge for him.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly should've won his last start against the Nationals. He gave up two runs on four hits over six innings, and looked sharp. But the Cubs were shut out by Nationals phenom John Lannan. Lilly's velocity is still off, but he's not worried. If other pitchers can win without throwing 99 mph, why can't he? It's a matter of improved command, and that's what the lefty is working on.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer keeps striking out a batter per inning, and as long as he does that, he'll be just fine. He's shown marked improvement in one category recently: keeping the ball in the ballpark. Wellemeyer has allowed just one homer over his past three starts, after giving up five in his first three games. A former Cubs prospect and big leaguer, he'll surely be looking forward to the opportunity to face his first team.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis took the loss in his last outing against the Brewers, giving up five runs on 10 hits over five innings. He had trouble locating his pitches, and the Brewers took advantage of every mistake. Marquis was 3-1 with a 3.60 ERA last season against his former team, the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenesz's spot in the rotation was in jeopardy before he turned in an encouraging 5 1/3 innings during which he gave up three hits, including a home run, and finished with a no-decision in the Rockies' 3-2 loss to the Giants on Wednesday. By being able to repeat his delivery, Jimenez had his liveliest fastball of the year and was able to change speeds and throw his breaking ball.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro showed that he knows how to pitch with a big lead. After a rocky beginning to his last game, he came out firing once he got a seven-run lead. It led to a lot of hard contact, but only one walk over the final five innings. Control has been Pineiro's key since he's come to St. Louis. He's thrown strikes consistently, and it's worked out.

home_pitcher_note: The good thing for Redman in his last start was the six scoreless innings he threw against the Dodgers on Saturday. The bad thing was he gave 10 runs in the first inning. Redman became unnerved after walking in a run in the middle of the inning. He didn't have much of a fastball and his changeup wasn't fooling hitters. Poor beginnings are an issue for him. But the next start is a shot at redemption in a different venue -- Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Looper has one bad start this year, but a couple of times now he's done the one thing he wasn't able to do last year: He's showing an ability to get by when he doesn't have his best stuff or command. Last year, he alternated good outings with brutal ones, as he wasn't able to survive when he wasn't sharp. This time, in six games, he has only one true clunker. That's a perfectly fine ratio, and one he'll try to keep up.

home_pitcher_note: Francis had a 3-1 lead over the Dodgers with one out in the sixth inning on Friday, but he also had thrown 100 pitches and faced loaded bases when manager Clint Hurdle decided to pull him. The bullpen faltered during a seven-run inning and Francis took the loss. The lefty was not as effective as he had been in going seven innings in each of his previous three starts, but he was able to make big pitches when he was in the game.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright showed no ill effects on Friday from the heavy workload he shouldered in his previous start. Nonetheless, the Cards took no chances, getting him out after 6 1/3 innings. The fact that that was his shortest outing of the year tells you how things have been going for the right-hander. Wainwright is enjoying an excellent year, pitching well and getting deep into games.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa had a rough outing in his season debut Saturday against the Dodgers, equaling a career high with nine runs on nine hits and three walks in four plus innings. He got some bad breaks as he gave up six runs in the first two innings, but he struggled with fastball command, and his slider and curve were ineffective, leaving only his changeup as a go-to pitch. He retired nine of 10 batters after the first six runs, but he couldn't record an out in the fifth inning, departing after a three-run homer on a hanging slider.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse had his worst start of the season in his last outing on Saturday, when the Cubs tagged him for eight earned runs on nine hits in six innings. He walked two batters and did not strike out anyone. The right-hander's ERA jumped from 2.36 after his first six starts to 3.79, which ranks third among the Cardinals' five starters. On the season, Lohse has struck out 14 and walked 10 in 40 1/3 innings of work. He's allowed 41 hits and opponents are batting .315 against him.

home_pitcher_note: Parra has not pitched more than 5 1/3 innings in any of his six starts, and that fact is starting to upset him. He lasted only four-plus frames against the Astros on Saturday, taking a 1-1 tie into the fifth inning and then allowing a five-run outburst sparked by back-to-back homers by the opposing pitcher, Brandon Backe, and slumping leadoff man Michael Bourne. Parra has great pure stuff -- a 92-94 mph fastball and three serviceable offspeed pitches -- but he has been up in the strike zone way to often, manager Ned Yost said. He has already started twice against the Cardinals, taking a pair of no-decisions while allowing six earned runs in nine total innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer lasted just five innings in his last start, on Sunday against the Cubs, which matched his shortest start of the season. The right-hander allowed two runs on three hits, struck out four and walked four. He threw 95 pitches, with 57 for strikes. In his next start, Wellemeyer will have to find a way to be more efficient with his pitches and try to get through six or seven innings to give the bullpen a break.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers and Cardinals have already played series at Miller Park and at Busch Stadium, but Sheets managed to miss both matchups. He probably didn't mind; Sheets is 5-14 in 23 career starts against the Cardinals with a 4.30 ERA. Pittsburgh is the only other National League Central rival against whom Sheets has a losing record (he's 6-8 against the Pirates). Sheets worked 6 1/3 innings against the Astros in his last start and showed no signs of the triceps injury that dogged him last month. He's one strikeout shy of Teddy Higuera's franchise record (1,081).
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro lasted only three innings and three batters Monday in Colorado, leaving the game after failing to retire a hitters in the fourth, yielding three hits and two runs -- one earned -- that inning after already allowing five hits and two runs in the first three innings.  His problems were compounded by his fourth inning at bat, when he swung and missed at a pitch that struck his right forearm as he completed his swing.  He had trouble keeping his breaking pitches down in his first Coors Field start, and he left too many pitches over the middle of the plate.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan improved over a tough outing in Chicago when he matched up against the Marlins on Tuesday, but he still was not particularly sharp, allowing three runs on eight hits in five innings and needing help from the bullpen to escape a bases-loaded, no-out jam in the sixth inning. Suppan needed to be virtually perfect because he matched up against Marlins ace Scott Olsen, who twice was one strike away from a two-hit shutout before settling for an 8 2/3-inning win. The Brewers have already played a pair of series against the Cardinals, Suppan's former team, but he did not pitch either time. He's 5-2 with a 3.32 ERA in nine career starts against St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: Looper pitched a gem Tuesday night in Colorado, making it to the ninth inning for the first time in his professional career. He held the Rockies two runs through eight, then let two more slip in before leaving in the ninth, finishing with 8 1/3 innings and 114 pitches. His sinker and his splitter were both on, and he made the Rox put the ball in play, walking none and striking out one, keeping the ball from the fat of the barrel. He made a couple mistakes, but until the ninth, they were isolated, allowing him to minimize the damage.

home_pitcher_note: Bush keeps getting burned by a few poorly placed pitches. That was the case again on Wednesday in Miami, when he returned to the rotation to replace an injured Yovani Gallardo and was roughed up for six runs in six innings. The Brewers were only trailing, 3-2, entering the sixth inning, but Bush surrendered a two-run home run to Jorge Cantu followed by a Dan Uggla solo shot. "He just can't get away with a mistake right now," manager Ned Yost said. Bush lost to the Cardinals in St. Louis on April 15 in his only quality start (three or fewer earned runs in six or more innings) this season.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright was on his game in Colorado, throwing seven shutout innings and earning a no decision in a game the bullpen lost in the eighth.  He avoided his curve against the Rockies, pitching off his fastball and using a four-seam changeup effectively against righties.  Wainwright excelled at limiting traffic, keeping Colorado from having multiple men reach base in all but one inning.  He relished the chance to pitch at Coors Field - after the fact, anyway - noting that it forced him to tighten his attention to mechanics, staying out front on his pitches and keeping the ball down in the zone.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse struggled Thursday, yielding seven runs on eight hits and five walks in four innings against the Rockies.  Four of the runs came with two outs in the first inning after a hard grounder to third deflected off Brendan Ryan's glove, opening the door for four hits and two walks.  Lohse couldn't get strike calls on his inside pitches, and in an effort to counteract the Coors Field factor of pitching at altitude, he abandoned his curve and tried too hard to pitch low in the zone, frequently ending up in the dirt.  Ultimately, he had to come back over the plate, and the Rockies were able to sit on his pitches and hand him a lopsided loss.
away_pitcher_note: Dumatrait picked up his first win of the season his last time out, dominating the Giants with 5 2/3 scoreless innings. He allowed just five hits and struck out five in the outing. Dumatrait, who has made just two starts since being moved from the bullpen to the rotation, continues to show more confidence in his changeup and is using that as a complement to his fastball and slider. The key for the lefty will continue to be making sure his pitches are down.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer deserved better after allowing only a pair of unearned runs in six solid innings Friday in Milwaukee, but Jason Isringhausen blew his fifth save with two outs in the ninth, and Milwaukee rallied for a victory. Wellemeyer also had a hand in the offensive part of the game, driving in a run with a single. He was one of three runners on base with nobody out, however, and the Cardinals were unable to score more than two runs in a potentially explosive frame.
away_pitcher_note: If Maholm hadn't tried to make an unwise defensive play in his last start, he may well have finished six innings of work without giving up a run. But instead, his attempt to try and snag a grounder led to four Giants runs in and a no-decision for Maholm. The lefty ran up a high pitch count early, but retired the last seven hitters he faced and did well in keeping the ball down. Maholm is 1-2 with a 2.28 ERA in three starts against St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro's sinker was on fire Saturday in Milwaukee, and he left the game with a lead before earning a no-decision in the Cardinals' 5-3 win over the Brewers. Pineiro only allowed two hits -- both off the bat of Ryan Braun -- through six innings before he loaded the bases with one out in the seventh, a circumstance Pineiro said could have been related to fatigue. Though two of those runners ultimately scored, it was a great bounceback from the previous start, when he lasted only three frames.
away_pitcher_note: After allowing four runs in three consecutive outings, Snell allowed just one in a season-high seven innings his last time out. The right-hander has been struggling with his aggressiveness all season, but appeared to take a step forward in that department despite giving up a career-high six walks in the game. Snell needs to continue using both sides of the plate more effectively. The righty is 3-3 with a 3.71 ERA in nine appearances (eight starts) against St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: Looper skipped his side session after working 8 1/3 innings in the thin Colorado air the start before, but he said he felt physically fine when he allowed four runs in six innings against Milwaukee. He struggled keeping the ball down, and Ryan Braun took advantage by smacking two home runs in the Cardinals' 5-3 loss. Looper only walked one and hit another batter -- but both of those scored in the first inning to spot the Brewers an early lead.
away_pitcher_note: Sonnanstine had picked up wins in four consecutive starts prior to Sunday's outing against the Angels, when he allowed five runs on eight hits while walking two to take a no-decision. Sonnanstine's best pitch is the slider, but in order for him to pitch well, he needs to locate his fastball to set up the vast array of pitches he throws from all different angles. He is 3-0 with a 4.05 ERA in three road starts this season. This will be his first career start against the Cardinals.
summary: 2008-05-16 - Tampa Bay Rays (3) @ St. Louis Cardinals (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright wasn't sharp his last time out, but it had to happen at some point. Nobody goes through a flawless season. Being back home should suit the right-hander. He's 3-0 at Busch Stadium with a 3.5 to 1 strikeout-to-walk ratio and an average of 7.75 innings per start.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander is beginning to develop into the dominating pitcher the Rays had hoped for when they acquired Garza in an offseason trade with the Twins. He is coming off his best performance of the season -- his first scoreless appearance in a season-high seven innings vs. the Yankees. Garza held New York sluggers Bobby Abreu, Hideki Matsui and Jason Giambi to a combined 0-for-7 in his 108-pitch effort, and will look for his third win of the season vs. the Cardinals.
summary: 2008-05-17 - Tampa Bay Rays (8) @ St. Louis Cardinals (9) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Lohse showed some progress his last time out, but he faded late. The fact remains that he's allowed four runs or more in four out of five starts, and the Cardinals are hoping for more. He's been much better at home (3.55 ERA) than on the road (8.78), but on the other hand he's had more success at night (3.12) than in the daylight (5.82).
away_pitcher_note: The flamethrower was as good as has ever been this season, scattering five hits over seven scoreless innings in May 13 over the Yankees. Jackson -- who tossed 111 pitches -- has now topped 110 tosses in his last two starts and has thrown 15 scoreless innings without a decision. Jackson is a threatening pitcher who gets better over the course of the game. He will look for another dominating performance and a much-deserved "W" vs. St. Louis.
summary: 2008-05-18 - Tampa Bay Rays (4) @ St. Louis Cardinals (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Jake Peavy was the scheduled starter until Sunday, when he was scratched because of a sore right elbow. Ledezma will start in his place.
away_pitcher_note: By any measure, Wellemeyer has been one of the Cardinals' two best starting pitchers this year, a remarkable achievement for a man who entered the year with 11 career big league starts and a 4.98 lifetime ERA. The right-hander has solved his biggest problem from the early going, which was the long ball -- he's gone four straight starts without allowing a home run. Wellemeyer is one of the great stories of the season so far, and the peripheral numbers indicate that he's got a chance to keep it up.
summary: 2008-05-19 - St. Louis Cardinals (8) @ San Diego Padres (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: His last outing against the Cubs was the first time he failed to pitch at least five innings in a start this season. Maddux is 2-4 this year on the road with a 5.35 ERA in six starts as opposed to a 1.42 ERA in three starts in PETCO.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro is coming off a strange start in which he appeared to be cruising, only to endure a fifth-inning unraveling that ultimately cost the Cardinals greatly. Still, he's been effective for the most part since a rocky start to begin the year. He's walked only 10 batters in 38 1/3 innings this season, an encouraging number. If he keeps it up at PETCO Park, he should be fine, since it's a forgiving ballpark where it's especially good to let hitters put the ball in play.
summary: 2008-05-20 - St. Louis Cardinals (2) @ San Diego Padres (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Young was staked to a 4-0 lead in the second inning of his last start against the Mariners before nearly giving it all back as he struggled with keeping his slider down in the strike zone. Once he did, Young was hard to hit as he set down 12 of the last 14 hitters he faced in winning for the fourth time this season. The key wasn't so much his fastball, which had good life through the strike zone, but his ability to harness and get better tilt on his slider -- a pitch that gave him fits in that second inning, but one that he relied on later.
away_pitcher_note: Looper made it a priority for 2008 to be able to limit the damage in games where he's not all that sharp. And to his credit, he's been able to do that this year. However, he's had a few too many of those games recently. What the Cardinals would like to see now are a few more of those games where Looper is sharp, getting quick outs and ground balls.
summary: 2008-05-21 - St. Louis Cardinals (11) @ San Diego Padres (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Lowe volunteered to start on short rest when Brad Penny's arm tightened and it turned into a short start on Sunday. Lowe was victimized by a James Loney throwing error, then let things get completely out of hand with an 0-2 pitch that Mike Napoli hit for a three-run homer. He was charged with seven runs on 10 hits in five innings and spent most of that time fuming on the mound over all that went wrong. He's gone a month since his last win.
away_pitcher_note: For many pitchers, it would just be a blip, but for Wainwright, two rough starts in a row qualifies as a slump. He's throwing strikes but he's giving up a lot of contact. It's far too early to get worried, but Wainwright needs to be at his best for the Cardinals to keep challenging for the NL Central title.
summary: 2008-05-23 - St. Louis Cardinals (2) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Brad Penny's last start was pushed back a day because of tightness in his arm during a bullpen session. When he did take the mound, it turned into his third consecutive disappointing performance. He allowed five runs (20 in last three starts) and it took two innings before his velocity reached the mid-90s. On the other hand, he grinded out six innings to save the bullpen and the Dodgers came back to win the game. He already has as many losses as he did all last season.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse looked more like himself last time out, breaking a rough stretch in which he allowed 19 runs in three starts. He should be feeling fresh, with an extra day of rest following a start in which he threw only 78 pitches. Lohse was knocked around in his only previous start at Dodger Stadium.
summary: 2008-05-24 - St. Louis Cardinals (4) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The Dodgers' youth movement hit another milestone when 20-year-old left-hander Clayton Kershaw was promoted to the Major Leagues from Double-A. Kershaw was 0-3 with a 2.28 ERA, 47 strikeouts, 15 walks and 32 hits allowed in 43 1/3 innings at Double-A Jacksonville, where his erratic workload was designed to preserve his arm for a pennant-race run in Los Angeles.
away_pitcher_note: Throughout Wellemeyer's career, a lack of consistency has been a major problem. At times he's been excellent, at other times rough. This year, though, he's been impressively steady. And it's been especially true in May -- Wellemeyer has allowed two earned runs or fewer in four consecutive starts. He's gone five starts without giving up a home run.
summary: 2008-05-25 - St. Louis Cardinals (3) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The good news: Looper hasn't allowed more than four runs in any of his past six starts. The bad: he hasn't allowed fewer than three runs in any of his past four starts. Still, there were some positive indicators in his last start. He struck out five, more than he had in three previous May starts combined. And for the second game in a row, he kept the ball on the ground. He's been good at home, and his best start of the year came against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Chacon finally stopped a record he didn't want in the first place when he notched a win in the win column during his last start versus the Cubs. The right-hander previously had a nine-game streak of no-decisions, the most in history to start a season. Chacon was shaky in the first inning, yielding a two-run homer to Derrek Lee as part of a three-run frame, but he cruised through his final six innings, holding the Cubs scoreless on two hits.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright righted himself, just as he expected he would, on Friday at Dodger Stadium. Now he comes home, where he's pitched very well this year (3-0, 2.70 in five starts). And he goes up against a Houston team he held down in an impressive, gutty performance earlier this year. He's the Cards' ace, and he seems to be back on track.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez, who has been on the disabled list since April 20 due to a strained groin, will be activated for this start at Busch Stadium. The only lefty in the rotation, Rodriguez is 1-4 with a 5.25 ERA in 10 career appearances aginst St. Louis, but he beat the Cardinals on April 7 with 7 1/3 scoreless innings (three hits allowed) with no walks and six strikeouts in a start at Minute Maid Park.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse comes back home, where he's been pitching very well so far this year. He has a 3.48 ERA in seven starts at Busch Stadium, with 20 strikeouts against just eight walks. He turned in an excellent performance against the Astros at Busch Stadium earlier this year, and he'll be trying to do it again. He's coming off a pair of solid starts in a row.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt didn't fare well in his first start since suffering inflammation in his right hip, allowing five runs in a loss to the Phillies. Oswalt yielded 11 hits, the fourth time this year he's allowed double-digits in hits. The right-hander faced the Cardinals earlier this year on April 26, taking a no-decision after yielding three runs over six innings. He walked three and struck out five.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer has been as steady as any Cardinals starter this season. He's allowed more than four runs just once in 11 starts, and he's permitted three or fewer in five straight. He had a rough go in his first start against Pittsburgh this year, but in his second appearance he turned in an excellent game.
away_pitcher_note: Duke was pushed back one day in the rotation because of a callous on the middle finger of his pitching hand. Duke has battled the minor discomfort through his last two starts and the Pirates' hope is that one extra day of rest will allow it to fully heal. In his last start, on Friday against the Cubs, Duke surrendered 10 hits in four innings, giving up four earned runs. It was his shortest outing since April 20, when the same Cubs team chased Duke from the game after four innings and five earned runs. Duke is 2-2 with a 3.98 ERA in seven starts against the Cardinals, though he is winless with a 5.60 ERA in Busch Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Parisi will make his first career start for the Cardinals in place of the injured Joel Pineiro. Parisi has pitched impressively in his first year with the club, striking out 10 batters in 15 2/3 innings with a 2.87 ERA. Manager Tony La Russa has used Parisi in multiple inning situations because he is normally a starter, and now he will get a chance to go deep against Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm looked impressive at times against a powerful Cubs lineup in his last start on May 25. He pitched six scoreless innings, but surrendered five runs in two separate innings. An unlikely Pirates comeback gave Maholm a no-decision. He is 2-3 with a 4.46 ERA against the Reds in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Looper thought he was right on the doorstep of getting on a roll, but in his last start he instead took a big step backward. He hasn't been truly sharp in several starts, and the stats indicate it. In five May starts, Looper has just nine strikeouts against eight walks, with five home runs allowed in 29 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The success of 2007 continues to be missing, and Snell has gotten to the point where it is beginning to affect him mentally. The right-hander has changed his mechanics, deciding to rely on his four-seam fastball and eliminate his sinker, but that hasn't worked. He's tried to up his velocity, and that hasn't translated into success either. The consensus is that the righty needs to relax and stop worrying about throwing perfect pitches, something that likely won't happen until he gets some solid starts under his belt. Snell faced the Cardinals on May 15 and allowed five runs on 11 hits in a season-short four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright throws his second consecutive start at home, a place he has relished pitching this year. In six home starts, the Cardinals' ace has won four. Most recently, Wainwright turned in an eight-inning, eight-strikeout gem against the Astros on May 28. With two impressive starts against the Astros in the bag this year -- the other a complete game victory -- Wainwright will try to win his third start in a row against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny lasted a career-low two-thirds of an inning his last time out, leaving the lefty wondering what it's going to take for his command to come back. He has lacked consistency from one start to the next all season and his walk total has escalated to 37 in 46 1/3 innings. The key for Gorzelanny is easy: getting ahead of hitters with some consistency. He fell behind seven of the eight hitters he faced in his most recent start. Gorzelanny lost a decision to the Cardinals earlier this season when he gave up a career-high seven walks and three runs in five innings. The lefty is 1-1 with a 1.98 ERA in two career starts at Busch Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Perez was strong for the Nationals in the second game of their West Coast road trip. The veteran left-hander threw 99 pitches -- 60 of them for strikes -- scattering six hits and three runs over 6 1/3 innings. He walked three and struck out four, and got good run support in form of a Jesus Flores grand slam and later a Lastings Milledge solo home run, as the Nationals took a 6-4 win at PETCO Park.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse pitched one of his best outings of the season in his last start against the Astros and has now won two starts in a row. In his last three starts, Lohse has thrown 18 innings while only giving up three earned runs. Lohse is 1-1 against the Nationals for his career in seven appearances with a 5.76 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan registered what's turning into a typical result for the Nationals last Thursday against San Diego. He threw 86 pitches over six innings, allowing just two runs and striking out five. However, the Nationals offense could only muster two runs of support, and the Nationals' bullpen lost the lead late, as San Diego won, 5-2, to take the rubber match of the three-game series.
away_pitcher_note: The Cardinals found a treasure when they plugged Wellemeyer into the starting rotation at the beginning of the year. In 10 of 12 starts this year, Wellemeyer has lasted at least six innings, and he's picked up six wins on the year. He turned in one of his best performances five days ago against Pittsburgh, when he threw a one-run, six-hit gem.

home_pitcher_note: Redding lasted 5 1/3 innings and gave up three runs on four hits against the Diamondbacks last Friday. He cruised through the first three innings and didn't allow a hit. But he struggled through the next 2 1/3 innings because of mechanical issues.
away_pitcher_note: Parisi gets one more chance to show his stuff. In his first Major League start, he was roughed up, but with Pineiro still out, he gets another shot. The right-hander, who throws a fastball, a curveball and a changeup, pitched very well in eight relief appearances before he was slotted into the rotation. He hopes to benefit from having a regular five-day routine, as opposed to last time, when he pitched four days after a relief appearance.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler absorbed his second loss after yielding four runs to the Brewers over five innings. He yielded a two-run homer to Prince Fielder on a poorly-placed changeup that sealed the loss. Moehler has faced the Cardinals once this year, in a relief appearance. He allowed one run in one inning of work.
away_pitcher_note: Looper's been decent lately, but it's been a while since he enjoyed a really good start. He's allowed at least three runs in each of his past six starts, and hasn't gone more than six innings since May 6. Even so, the right-hander hasn't been bad; he's only gotten knocked around twice this year, and for the most part he's keeping the team in the game. Looper has faced the Astros three times already this year, with two solid starts and a very rocky one the last time he saw them.

home_pitcher_note: Chacon suffered his first loss of the season in abbreviated fashion, throwing 40 pitches over one inning during a landslide defeat by the Brewers. Chacon yielded four runs, walked two and hit two. The right-hander has faced the Cardinals twice this year. He took a no-decision on April 8 at home, yielding three runs over six innings. On May 27, Chacon allowed two runs over seven innings in a winning effort at Busch Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright was inconsolable after his last outing, in which he was brilliant through six innings only to fall apart in the seventh. Historically, that's been a good sign. When Wainwright is disappointed in his game, he tends to bounce back extremely strong. He also loves facing the rival Astros, against whom he's tossed two excellent games already this season.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez earned his first win since April 13 after shutting out the Pirates on five hits over six innings. He regained control of his curveball, which had given him problems in his prior outing, which was also his first start after a five-week stay on the DL. Rodriguez faced the Cardinals earlier this season at Minute Maid Park, throwing 7 1/3 shutout innings and taking a no-decision in an eventual Houston win.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse endured an early-May slump, but it's definitely in the past now. He's working on a hot streak these days. Over Lohse's past four starts, he's allowed a total of four earned runs, with one home run and one walk. He's also been very efficient, averaging 14 pitches per inning in that time. It will be interesting to see how he recovers from his last start, in which he pitched only five official innings but sat out two lengthy rain delays and threw a great deal on the side.

home_pitcher_note: Bailey pitched well but fell victim to errors in his 2008 debut with the Reds on Thursday. He pitched 6 1/3 innings and gave up five runs -- just two of them earned -- on four hits with four walks and a strikeout in a loss to the Phillies. The Reds committed three errors in the game. Bailey is 0-1 with one career start against the Cardinals, in which he gave up seven earned runs on seven hits in just 3 2/3 innings. It came last season during his nine-start stint with the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: This will be the first Major League start for Boggs, called up Friday from Triple-A Memphis. He made his first appearance in the majors Friday in Houston in relief. He pitched two innings and gave up three hits and one run, a homer by Geoff Blum. Boggs, 24, was 5-1 with a 3.28 in 12 starts for Memphis this year. He allowed only three home runs in Triple-A this year.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto was solid in his last outing, pitching six innings and giving up three runs on eight hits with three walks and eight strikeouts in a win over the Marlins on Friday. He gave up two home runs, but he had plenty of support from the Cincinnati offense. Of his 115 pitches -- the second-most he's thrown all season -- 73 went for strikes. He's thrown at least 100 pitches in each of his last four starts. Cueto's only career start against the Cardinals came on April 29, when he gave up seven runs on eight hits in just 1 2/3 innings in a losing effort. It was by far his shortest outing of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Looper gave up two earned runs in six innings of his last start, Friday at Houston. But the St. Louis defense let him down, with two errors allowing three more Astros runs to score and giving him the loss. Looper gave up eight hits, but tied his career high with seven strikeouts and walked none. He threw 107 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo was clearly disappointed with his control in his last game, when he gave up four runs in 4 2/3 innings Saturday in a no-decision against the Marlins. He threw only 58 of his 103 pitches for strikes and said that ratio doesn't work for him. Arroyo was particularly wild in the second inning, when he threw nine straight balls at one point and 11 of 12. That's when the Marlins scored their first two runs off him. Arroyo had a dismal start to this season, but seemed to right himself in May. But he had trouble at Philadelphia in his last start before Saturday, and now is likely to be in a period of soul-searching about getting his game together.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro will make his first start since going on to the 15-day disabled list with a strained groin May 21. He threw a bullpen session on Tuesday, and Cardinals manager Tony La Russa said Pineiro was "at 100 percent." Pineiro last faced the Reds on April 29, when he gave up no runs and just one hit through seven innings with four walks and three strikeouts in receiving the victory.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer sat out his last scheduled start with an inflamed right elbow, but he's back on track to start Saturday. In his last start, Wellemeyer pitched six scoreless innings and gave up just five hits with a walk and five strikeouts against the Nationals. The five hits tied a season high, but it was the second time he's held an opponent to no earned runs. He hasn't lost a start since April 28.
away_pitcher_note: Kyle Kendrick was effectively erratic for five innings on Saturday against the Braves, but he gave up a two-run homer in the sixth inning to spoil his opportunity for a sixth win. Kendrick pitched 5 1/3 innings, and his teammates said after the game that they wished the 23-year-old right-hander could pitch deeper into games. Still, the Phillies are 10-4 in games started by Kendrick this season, which has to help his confidence as he continues to learn on the fly. Kendrick is 2-0 lifetime against St. Louis. Both wins came last season. In his last start against the Cardinals, on Sept. 17, 2007, Kendrick allowed three runs on seven hits in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse gave up a long, long home run to Houston's Lance Berkman in his last start Sunday and not much else. He limited the Astros to five hits and three runs over six innings, striking out three and walking two. He has won his last four starts and hasn't lost since May 9. This will be Lohse's first appearance this year vs. Philadelphia.
away_pitcher_note: pitched six innings and threw 99 pitches in hot and humid conditions on Sunday, but didn't factor in the decision against Atlanta. He gave up three runs on six hits, and his only real mistake was a pitch up in the zone to Mark Teixeira that he hit for a two-run homer in the first inning. Eaton stranded seven baserunners, working in and out of jams in the second, third and fourth innings to keep the Phillies in the game. Eaton is 1-4 with a 6.82 ERA in seven career starts against St. Louis. He has allowed six earned runs in each of his past two starts against the Cardinals, both of which came last season. In his most recent start against them, on July 15, 2007, he surrendered six runs on 10 hits in four innings and got the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Boggs was solid in his first Major League start on Tuesday while filling in for Todd Wellemeyer, who was nursing an inflamed right elbow. He pitched five innings and gave up two runs on four hits with three walks in a 7-2 victory over the Reds. He made his professional debut June 6 against the Astros, when he pitched two innings in relief and allowed a solo home run.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies hope Myers' outing on Tuesday wasn't a regression to his early-season form. The right-hander was sloppy against the Marlins, allowing five runs on three home runs and fell behind in too many counts. He had a 2.35 ERA in his previous two outings, including a 7 1/3-inning, one-hit performance on June 4. If his location and breaking pitches continue to be poor, he'll continue to struggle.

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro gave up just two runs on three hits through five innings of work against the Reds on Thursday. It was his first start since returning from the 15-day disabled list, where he was nursing a strained right groin. He threw just 69 pitches -- 47 going for strikes -- with one walk and six strikeouts. One of his earned runs came on a sacrifice squeeze, while another came when Reds starter Bronson Arroyo hit his fourth career home run in the fifth.
away_pitcher_note: After winning his first two starts, Davies lapsed into control problems against the Rangers last Wednesday night. He walked five and gave up seven hits but still managed to get through six innings with one run across the plate. He left with a 5-1 lead but the bullpen coughed up 10 runs and lost the game, 11-5. Command of his fastball has plagued Davies in the past and he worked hard at Triple-A Omaha to remedy that. He had walked just one in his previous outing. Although Davies formerly pitched for the Braves, this will be his first appearance against the Cardinals.
summary: 2008-06-17 - Kansas City Royals (2) @ St. Louis Cardinals (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Looper pitched his first career shutout in his last start, a 10-0 victory over Cincinnati on Wednesday. He retired the first 11 and final 11 batters he faced and gave up just three hits while striking out four and walking none. Looper took a new approach in the shutout. He said he slowed his delivery and approach down substantially and that it helped him with his location.
away_pitcher_note: Bannister had one glitch last Thursday against the Rangers, giving up four runs on two homers in the second inning. But he hung on, giving up just one more hit in five subsequent scoreless innings, and put the Royals in a position to win, which they did in the ninth. There was no decision for Bannister, who is 2-6 since winning his first three starts of the season. Last year Bannister beat the Cardinals, 8-1, on June 12 by pitching seven shutout innings at Kansas City. This is his first St. Louis appearance.
summary: 2008-06-18 - Kansas City Royals (3) @ St. Louis Cardinals (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: With Anthony Reyes going on the DL due to elbow soreness, the Cardinals activate Thompson perhaps a bit more quickly than they anticipated. Thompson earned a rotation spot in Spring Training but was bumped when Joel Pineiro came off the DL. He struggled in relief, was placed on the injured list himself and has made two rehabilitation starts. Thompson's an extreme groundballer when things are going well, and he'll try to keep the ball down against a Kansas City team that has hit three homers the past two games.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke worked himself into tough jams on Friday night at Arizona but managed to wiggle free and pitch seven shutout innings before being relieved. Pitching carefully to the tough Diamondbacks, he walked a career-high seven but gave up just three hits. The no-decision meant he hasn't won in five straight starts after starting the season 5-1. Working in 100-plus degree heat, he threw 111 pitches and still looked strong. Against the Cardinals, he's 1-2 with a 7.04 ERA in four games.
summary: 2008-06-19 - Kansas City Royals (4) @ St. Louis Cardinals (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: After just missing his fifth win of the season in Cincinnati on Saturday when Jonathan Papelbon allowed a game-tying homer, Wakefield gets another chance to get over the .500 mark. Wakefield has thrown at least seven innings in each of his last starts, including last Saturday when he allowed just four hits and two solo home runs over seven, walking two and striking out six. He is 1-2 with a 5.29 ERA in five career starts against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse keeps throwing strikes and pitching deep into games. Not coincidentally, he keeps winning. He's gone at least six innings in six out of seven starts, with the only exception being a rain-interrupted affair in Washington. Lohse has issued a total of six walks in those seven games. That combination will typically add up to some solid results, and what do you know, Lohse has won five straight starts.
summary: 2008-06-20 - St. Louis Cardinals (5) @ Boston Red Sox (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander makes his first start since May 27 after suffering a mild strain of his rotator cuff. Matsuzaka did make a rehab outing for Triple-A Pawtucket on Monday, allowing three hits and two runs over five innings. He walked one and struck out five. Before the injury, Matsuzaka was off to a terrific start. Over 64 innings, he allowed just 45 hits while striking out 55. In Matsuzaka's first 43 Major League starts, he is 23-12 with a 3.95 ERA. This will be his first career appearance against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: In his first big league start, Boggs acquitted himself nicely, but in game No. 2 it was a bit rocky. Against a potent offense in its friendly home park, Boggs will be doing well if he simply keeps his team in the ballgame.
summary: 2008-06-21 - St. Louis Cardinals (9) @ Boston Red Sox (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Lester has been Boston's best pitcher over the last few weeks. He has won his last three starts, giving up a total of three runs in 20 1/3 innings. Lester is holding opponents to a .249 average on the season and has allowed three earned runs or fewer in 10 consecutive starts. Lester has thrived at Fenway this season, going 4-1 with a 2.55 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Exhibit 14,591 on why wins are a bad way to judge a pitcher: Pineiro hasn't won since April 29. In the interim, however, he's pitched well enough to win at least three times, most notably in his most recent start, when he allowed a single run over seven innings. Fenway Park probably isn't high on Pineiro's list of favorite places, but he's going well enough that he might be able to erase the bad memories of a frustrating '07 with the Red Sox.
summary: 2008-06-22 - St. Louis Cardinals (3) @ Boston Red Sox (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: It took five solid starts, but Rogers finally has a winning record after losing his first three outings this season. He has allowed just four earned runs on 25 hits over 36 innings in those last five starts, the latest being seven innings of one-run ball against the Giants last Tuesday. In the process, the command that marked his 17-win season in 2006 has made a comeback. He'll need to pound the strike zone carefully against a Cardinals lineup that ranks fifth in the Majors in on-base percentage and actually fares better in that regard against left-handers, despite hitting 10 points lower against them than versus right-handers.
away_pitcher_note: Looper has been rolling lately, and the formula is very simple. Throw strikes, and keep it in the ballpark. He's gone four straight starts without allowing a home run, and three straight without a walk. As a result, the right-hander has a 1.95 ERA in May. That's despite a couple of starts in the inhospitable environments of Minute Maid Park and Great American Ball Park. Now he gets another kind of challenge, pitching to a potent lineup that includes a designated hitter.

home_pitcher_note: The early-season phenomenon that Galarraga seemed to be upon his April callup keeps rolling, and he's quietly building a case for a spot on the American League All-Star pitching staff. Another victory against a quality club like the Cardinals would obviously further bolster his case. Not only has the former Rangers farmhand won his last three starts, but he hasn't allowed an earned run over 13 innings in his last two outings. He has allowed just 47 hits over 71 1/3 innings this season, which translates to a mere .184 batting average.
away_pitcher_note: No starter in the NL is hotter than Lohse, who is 6-0 with a 2.09 ERA over his past seven starts. Lohse has delivered desperately needed stability to a rotation reeling from injuries, and has done a huge part to keep the Cardinals in contention while they do without Adam Wainwright. He's throwing strikes (seven walks in seven starts) and letting his defense work, and it's going extremely well.

home_pitcher_note: The Tigers maneuvered their rotation for their homestand so that Robertson could start on his normal rest. The way he's been winning, it's hard to blame them. Robertson has won his last three starts, tying a career-best winning streak he set in 2004, his first full Major League season. The latest came Saturday at San Diego, where he gave up five runs on seven hits over six innings but somehow avoided further damage to let his offense pick him up for the victory. He's 6-3 for his career in Interleague Play, including one victory over the Cardinals last year at Comerica Park.
away_pitcher_note: This one is written in pencil, rather than ink, but it appears that Wellemeyer will get the start in the series finale in Detroit. He had been absolutely exceptional until coming down with some elbow soreness, and the injury resulted in an extremely rocky last start. A fairly intensive bullpen session told Wellemeyer that he's coming along well, though, and he expects to get the ball. If he's not ready, the assignment would probably fall to rookie Mitchell Boggs.

home_pitcher_note: Meche hurt himself in his last outing on Saturday against the Giants, making a throwing error on what should have been a double play. He didn't get out of the inning, but the bullpen preserved a 5-3 victory for him. Meche has been on the upswing. In his first eight starts, he was 2-5 with a 6.31 ERA. In his eight starts since then, he's gone 3-3 with a 3.62 ERA. Meche missed the Cardinals' series at St. Louis and he's faced them just once in his career with no decision. His career stats against the National League, though, are an impressive 12-4 with a 3.62 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro's last start was a big test, and he passed, turning in seven exceptional innings at Fenway Park. He'll get another Interleague appearance on Friday, coincidentally against old Seattle teammate Gil Meche. Pineiro has a winless streak that's closing in on two months, but it's absolutely not his fault. Since his last victory, on April 29, Pineiro has a 3.92 ERA, 25 strikeouts and eight walks in 39 innings.
summary: 2008-06-27 - St. Louis Cardinals (2) @ Kansas City Royals (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: After victories in three of four fine starts, Davies ran into big trouble on Sunday against the Giants. He lasted just 1 1/3 innings and gave up five runs on six hits and two walks, expending 52 pitches in the process. Fortunately, the Royals came from behind to outlast the Giants, 11-10, and Davies' record got a reprieve. Davies' earlier success came because of his much-improved command, but that lapsed in this outing. He did well against the Cardinals on June 17 in St. Louis, giving up just one run in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Boggs hasn't blown anybody away, and he hasn't missed a lot of bats. But he's found a way to survive, and every one of his starting assignments has been tough. Now he gets another challenge, against another hot team using a designated hitter. With Mark Mulder no longer knocking down the door for a starting job, Boggs may have a little breathing room. It will be interesting to see how he handles it.
summary: 2008-06-28 - St. Louis Cardinals (5) @ Kansas City Royals (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Bannister, in his previous six starts, had walked just six batters. So it was highly irregular when he walked six in the first five innings on Monday night against the Rockies. That matched his career high. He survived, however, and went seven innings for the victory. Bannister had trouble controlling his pitches on the third-base side of home plate, a glitch he'll surely be working on. On June 18 at St. Louis, he beat the Cardinals and held them to two runs in seven innings. He's 2-0 against them in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Looper found the going a bit tough against an extremely potent Tigers lineup, but he still almost came out of it with a quality start. He's going well, and he pitched an excellent game against this same Royals club in St. Louis earlier in June. Looper is 5-2 with a 3.91 ERA away from Busch Stadium, and he has walked just four batters in 46 road innings this year.
summary: 2008-06-29 - St. Louis Cardinals (9) @ Kansas City Royals (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Lohse's six-start winning streak came to an end with a no-decision, but he still hasn't been the losing pitcher in a game since May 8. He just didn't have anything his last time out. Upon his return home, and against a lineup that is a bit less daunting than Detroit's, there's good reason to expect a return to June form. Lohse may still have a shot at an All-Star berth if everything falls his way.
away_pitcher_note: Maine did what he always seems to do, pitching a solid six innings on Wednesday while only allowing two runs on five hits. But Maine is still searching for the second wind that will get him into the seventh, eighth and ninth innings, as he has only pitched more than 6 2/3 innings once, which was an 8 1/3 start on May 7 at the Dodgers. That isn't to say Maine doesn't chuck his share of pitches, as Wednesday's 102 pitches upped the number of times he's hit triple digits to 13 of his 16 starts this season.
summary: 2008-06-30 - New York Mets (1) @ St. Louis Cardinals (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer's return to action after missing time with a sore elbow was a success. He had a very good fastball and slider, and he believes his changeup won't be far behind. He was handled gently in his first start back, throwing only 76 pitches. Expect a longer leash this time around.
away_pitcher_note: Armas will probably get the call up from Triple-A for a fill-in start on Tuesday, and, depending on how he pitches, the 30-year-old veteran could potentially assume the long-relief role for the Mets in place of fellow callup Carlos Muniz. In 16 appearances with New Orleans, Armas is 5-6 with a 2.50 ERA, striking out 88 batters and walking 20 in 100 2/3 innings of work. If he were to face the Cardinals, he is a career 3-2 against them with a 3.98 ERA in nine meetings, seven of those being starts.
summary: 2008-07-01 - New York Mets (7) @ St. Louis Cardinals (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro's line from his last start wasn't pretty, but one good thing stands out about his last three: he's gone at least seven innings each time. Considering the load that the St. Louis bullpen has carried, that's a victory in itself. Still, Pineiro could really use some reinforcement in the form of a win. He hasn't recorded one since April, and this start will take place in July. That's too long.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez's start in the second game of Friday's Subway Series doubleheader was a struggle, as he surrendered six earned runs in 5 2/3 innings. For the second consecutive start, Martinez gave up six runs, and he has now permitted 12 runs in his last 10 innings. The 36-year-old came out of Friday's start saying he was tipping off some of his pitches, an issue he will look to correct heading into his next start vs. the Cardinals. He's an even 4-4 against St. Louis in his career, with a 3.27 ERA in 77 innings of work.
summary: 2008-07-02 - New York Mets (7) @ St. Louis Cardinals (8) (Final)
