home_pitcher_note: Manager Tony La Russa's mantra for choosing a rotation is "pick the best five," which surely means that Boggs has earned at least one more start. The rookie was outstanding in his most recent start, getting his fastball down and working off that to get swings and misses with his off-speed pitches. That's called pitching, and it's impressive how Boggs is learning the art as he goes along.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey gave up four earned runs in five innings of work vs. the Yankees on Friday, but it was enough for him to get his third straight win. The Yankees were able to scatter eight hits off of Pelfrey, but he never folded, doing just enough with plenty of run support working him through the Mets? 15-6 drubbing of the Bronx Bombers in Game 1 of the doubleheader. Pelfrey pitched the best month of his 2008 campaign in June, compiling a 3.52 ERA in 30 2/3 innings of work. He?ll face the Cardinals next, who he has never faced.
summary: 2008-07-03 - New York Mets (11) @ St. Louis Cardinals (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Looper was the victim of a strange start his last time out. Against the Royals, Looper lasted 3 1/3 innings and was given a quick hook from manager Tony La Russa. Rather than let things get out of hand on a windy day, La Russa took out Looper who was not sharp in his outing. Looper has a great deal of experience against the Cubs, facing them 36 times in his career. So far, that experience has led to success on the mound as Looper has produced a 2.37 ERA in 64 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano was expected to be activated from the disabled list for this game, which will be his first start since June 18. He had to come out of that game because of a strained right shoulder, and went on the disabled list for the first time in his career. The right-hander had a bullpen session on Sunday, and said he benefited from the time off. He felt great, especially his slider and sinker. He was 3-0 with a 1.69 ERA last year against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Over the offseason, several teams passed up on Lohse rather than take him off the free agent market. The Cardinals took a $4.25 million chance on him during Spring Training and their investment has more than paid off. At 10-2, Lohse has already won as many games as he did last season and has the fourth-highest win total of any Major League pitcher. Four wins short of a career high, Lohse has catapulted himself into All-Star consideration and looked sharp in his recent outing against the Mets. Lohse struck out four over seven innings and allowed an unearned run in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Continuing his streak of success on the road, Lilly went eight-plus innings in his last start in San Francisco and didn't allow any runs until the final frame. Lilly has allowed just four runs in his previous three road starts. Against the Giants, he was throwing three pitches -- fastball, curveball, changeup -- for strikes, and he allowed just seven hits while striking out five.

home_pitcher_note: Since he won May's Player of the Month award, Wellemeyer has turned into his old self. In his four starts since he won the award, Wellemeyer is 1-3 with a 6.52 ERA in 19 1/3 innings. Needless to say, Wellemeyer has not been overly sharp recently. In his most recent outing against the Mets, Wellemeyer missed his spots and suffered badly against an offense that can score runs in a heartbeat. Now he gets to face his first team, the Cubs, and should have a little extra incentive pitching against them.
away_pitcher_note: Because he pitched well against the White Sox last weekend, and since the Cardinals have a lineup that struggles against left-handers, Marshall will get another crack at the starting rotation. Subbing for Carlos Zambrano, Marshall kept the Cubs in the game vs. the White Sox, going seven innings and giving up three runs while striking out five. The left-hander said he feels more comfortable in the rotation, and he thinks he's proven himself as a Major League-quality starter.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels was one out away from recording his third complete game of the season on Thursday against the Braves. But with his pitch count already at 125, manager Charlie Manuel didn't risk keeping Hamels on the mound. His rationale was that Hamels has two more starts to make before the All-Star break and a whole second half of the season to pitch. So Hamels had to settle for one run on five hits in 8 2/3 innings. He has pitched at least six innings in each of his past six starts. Hamels is 2-0 with a 4.26 ERA in four career starts against the Cardinals. In his last start, Sept. 18, 2007, Hamels gave up three runs on five hits in three innings.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro has had a rough going for the past two months. In his last nine starts, Pineiro is winless with seven no-decisions. Over this time, Pineiro has pitched effectively for the Cardinals, but will be coming off a rather poor outing against the Mets on Wednesday. Over five innings, Pineiro gave up four runs and scattered 11 hits -- most of which were hit with authority. Pineiro said after the game that it was just one of those nights where he had shaky command and kept missing his spots.

home_pitcher_note: Happ made his first start of 2008 on Friday, lasting 4 2/3 innings, allowing two runs on three hits, striking out three and walking four. Manager Charlie Manuel was noncommittal regarding whether Happ's Friday outing had earned him another start, though he said he was pleased with Happ's command. The lefty was called up to fill in for Brett Myers, who was optioned to Triple-A Lehigh Valley.
away_pitcher_note: With the Cardinals sending rookie right-hander Mitchell Boggs down to Triple-A Memphis, Mulder will make his first start of the year and his first since Sept. 16. Thus far, Mulder has made two appearances out of the bullpen for the Cardinals and with mixed results. In his first trip out of the 'pen, Mulder threw one inning and gave up two hits. But in his most recent appearance, Mulder struggled and lasted only one-third of an inning while giving up two runs.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer earned his ninth quality start of 2008 on his way to a no-decision against the Mets Saturday. He lasted 6 2/3 innings, giving up three runs on seven hits. He did not start against the Cardinals the last time the Phillies faced St. Louis, but owns an all-time record of 4-1 against them in 10 starts. The Phillies started out the season 10-4 in Moyer's first 14 starts, but have lost his last four starts in a row.
away_pitcher_note: Looper could not have asked for a much better start against the Cubs on Friday. But Looper's two mistakes cost him and the Cardinals the game. While his team was unable to support him with a good deal of runs, Looper gave up two solo home runs to the Cubs and that was enough for the rivals to win. Looper is coming off throwing 120 pitches in seven innings, so it will be interesting to see how his arm rebounds after that kind of start. He said the arm felt fine and the day off between the Phillies series shouldn't hurt.

home_pitcher_note: Duke had his shortest outing of the season his last time out as he was pulled after allowing six runs (five earned) on seven hits and three walks in 2 1/3 innings against the Brewers. Duke struggled especially with his control, which was surprising considering the lefty had allowed just nine walks in his last 41 2/3 innings. There's little reason to believe, though, this was more than an anomaly, as he had thrown at least six innings in 10 of his last 13 starts before the outing. In one of his best outings of the year, Duke allowed just two runs in 7 2/3 innings in a start against the Astros in early June.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse continued his dominance in a career year when he faced the Cubs on Saturday at Busch Stadium. Though he got the no-decision, Lohse lasted seven innings and gave up only two runs, lowering his ERA to 3.61. In his last nine starts, Lohse is 7-0 and finished June with a perfect record. With the prolonged absences of Chris Carpenter and Adam Wainwright, Lohse has given the Cardinals a needed reliant arm out of the starting rotation.

home_pitcher_note: The Pirates recalled Herrera after Friday night's game. The 27-year-old Cuban defector will start for Phil Dumatrait, who was placed on the disabled list with continued shoulder problems. Herrera was signed by the Pirates on Dec. 18, 2006, as a non-drafted free agent from Cuba. He spent the 2001-04 seasons playing for the Cuban national team. He was 3-5 with a 3.43 ERA in 10 starts this season for Double-A Altoona.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer has had some fine moments since returning from an early-June elbow injury, but he hasn't quite looked like the same pitcher who was so good in the season's first two months. He's throwing strikes, and he's keeping the ball in the park, definitely two things to like. But he hasn't found the sharpness on his slider that was such a big part of his early success, and he just isn't controlling at-bats and handling hitters the way he was before.

home_pitcher_note: Snell's last start was his first since he was placed on the disabled list with right elbow soreness. Though his efficiency was subpar -- he threw 88 pitches in 3 2/3 innings -- Snell proved that his velocity is once again back. He opened the game with 20 straight fastballs -- a pitch he said he intends to throw often at the beginning of every start from now on -- all registering about three to five mph faster than they were before the injury was discovered. This will be Snell's fourth start of the season against the Cardinals. The righty has allowed 14 runs in the first 15 innings against St. Louis this year.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro finally got a win his last time out, but he's deserved a lot more W's than he's been credited with. He'll try to even his record in the last game of the first half, and he'll be pitching in a park where he turned in one of his best games of the year. Back in April, Pineiro pitched seven exceptional innings against the Pirates at PNC Park. Pineiro hasn't allowed a homer in either of his past two starts, and over his past four games, he has a ground-ball:fly-ball ratio of just under 2.5:1.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse won his eighth straight decision and his 11th in 13 games this year by holding Pittsburgh to six hits and no runs over seven innings as the Cards downed the Bucs, 6-0, on July 11. The Cards are 13-7 in games Lohse has started.
away_pitcher_note: Peavy had yet another masterful start as he went seven shutout innings in a 4-0 victory over the Atlanta Braves on July 11. Peavy struck out seven while only giving up four hits. His last four starts have all been quality starts (over six innings) and he's struck out at least six batters in each of those four starts. The Padres seem to be a different team with him on the mound, especially at home, and Peavy seems to be a different pitcher when on his home mound. He sports a 1.45 ERA at home but has a 4.41 ERA on the road.
summary: 2008-07-17 - San Diego Padres (3) @ St. Louis Cardinals (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Looper stacked 112 pitches in a 4-1 loss to the Phillies on July 10. Stack that total atop the 120 he threw in his previous start. Looper has not recorded a win since June 24, when he defeated the Detroit Tigers, 8-4.
away_pitcher_note: Maddux's last start was another of frustration for his supporters. Though the veteran righty says he would rather lose while pitching than not be pitching at all, those around him feel bad that his record doesn't show how well he has pitched this season. Maddux has a 3-8 record in 20 starts and hasn't had a victory in his last 12 times out. In seven of his last 10 starts, he's allowed two runs or less.
summary: 2008-07-18 - San Diego Padres (7) @ St. Louis Cardinals (11) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer who had dropped three of his last four starts, pitched 6 1/3 innings and allowed four runs on four hits at Pittsburgh on July 12. He left the game with a comfortable lead, but the right-hander picked up a no-decision as the bullpen imploded in a 12-11 Pirates victory in 10 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf, who has been rumored to be on the trading block leading up to the July 31 trade deadline, allowed six runs in five innings in his last start against the Braves on July 13, which came five days after he allowed one run in seven innings in a victory over the Marlins. Which Wolf will show up? It depends on his command. He made a mechanical change to get him more extension before the  Florida start. He then allowed three runs in the first inning in the loss to the Braves.
summary: 2008-07-19 - San Diego Padres (5) @ St. Louis Cardinals (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Garcia will be making his first career start. In his first Major League appearance, he tossed two scoreless frames in relief to close out a 6-0 Cardinals victory over Pittsburgh on July 11. Garcia was 4-4 at Triple-A Memphis with a 4.49 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Like Banks, Baek enters the second half with a fresh arm. He made his last start on July 9 against Florida, allowing three runs on six hits over five innings. Opponents are hitting .282 against him since he was traded to the Padres in June from Seattle. Baek might not be long for the starting rotation, though, if the Padres decide to hang on to veterans Greg Maddux and Randy Wolf through the July 31 non-waiver trading deadline.
summary: 2008-07-20 - San Diego Padres (5) @ St. Louis Cardinals (9) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro was staked to a 4-1 lead in his last start on July 13 at Pittsburgh, but wound up tossing 5 2/3 innings, allowing six runs on 10 hits. He received a no-decision. He lost a 3-2 decision to San Diego on April 20, allowing six hits and three runs in 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: McClung gets the nod as the Brewers begin a rare platoon of starting pitchers. McClung will get the nod when his spot in the rotation comes up on the road, and fellow right-hander Dave Bush will take the ball at home. The Brewers are going with the numbers here; McClung is 1-1 with a 3.28 ERA in 11 games, four starts, on the road and 4-4 with a 4.95 ERA in 10 games, six starts, at home. Bush is 4-2 with a 2.49 ERA in nine starts at home and 1-6 with a 6.95 ERA in nine games, eight of them starts, on the road. With the acquisition of CC Sabathia and with Jeff Suppan likely being activated from the disabled list on Tuesday, there was not room for both McClung and Bush in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse hit his stride in May and he continues to sprint to the finish. With Adam Wainwright and Chris Carpenter on the disabled list, Lohse has provided the Cardinals with a much needed boost in their starting rotation and he has delivered. Lohse has not lost a start since May 8 and has lost only two games in his last 32 starts, dating back to July 2007. While he did not pitch his best in his last outing and was aided by some spectacular defense, Lohse pitched effective enough to last seven innings and give up two runs. Attributing his success to his confidence in his entire arsenal, Lohse has morphed into one of the better pitchers this year.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers are expecting Suppan to return to the starting rotation. The veteran right-hander was bothered by joint irritation in the elbow on his throwing arm, forcing him to the disabled list. Before going on the DL, Suppan had been struggling. He allowed 18 earned runs on 30 hits over 15 2/3 innings in his last four starts. Both Suppan and manager Ned Yost downplayed the degree of the injury, but felt that rest would be good for the righty.

home_pitcher_note: It didn't take long for the Padres to knock Looper around in his last outing on July 18. In three-plus innings of work, Looper only threw 68 pitches but managed to give up six runs on eight hits. Looper kept serving up pitches over the heart of the plate so many times that he eventually became visibly frustrated. However, Looper has been much more consistent this year than in years past. In his other three poor starts, Looper has followed with quality starts, showing a strong ability to bounce back.
away_pitcher_note: So far, so good for Sabathia, who is 3-0 in his three Brewers starts since a trade from Cleveland. He has pitched all nine innings in each of his last two starts, including a four-hitter at San Francisco to begin the second half, becoming the first Brewers pitcher to toss complete games in consecutive starts since Scott Karl in 1995. Sabathia is also living up to his reputation as a tough out; he homered against the Reds on July 13 and then doubled and scored against the Giants on Friday.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer may have found something as he went on in his last outing, and the Cardinals certainly hope so. Since he sustained an elbow injury in early June, he hasn't looked like the same pitcher who was so effective in April and May. Wellemeyer relies heavily on two pitches, his fastball and his slider, so if either one is less than its best, he's going to have a hard time.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets was lifted for a pinch-hitter in the middle of a four-run Brewers rally on Saturday, so he pitched only five innings, snapping Milwaukee's streak of seven consecutive quality starts. He surrendered four runs in the fourth inning, and while only two were earned because of an error by shortstop J.J. Hardy, it marked the first time an opponent scored more than twice in a single frame against Sheets since the Dodgers' six-run seventh inning on May 15.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey's streak of consecutive starts won ended at six in Cincinnati on Sunday, but he didn't lose, and he provided what few of his starting colleagues provide -- length. He pitched seven innings and allowed only six hits and a walk. But three of the hits were solo home runs, a surprising development because he had surrendered merely four home runs in 108 2/3 innings before Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: Boggs, a rookie, won three of his first five Major League starts but then ran into a problem against the Mets on July 3: he allowed 11 runs -- 10 of them earned -- on 10 hits and six walks in six innings.
summary: 2008-07-25 - St. Louis Cardinals (2) @ New York Mets (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: A former pitching prospect in the Yankees system, Knight will make his first Major League start -- and his first big league appearance in six years -- against the Cardinals Saturday. Knight, the reigning Pacific Coast League Pitcher of the Week, was 5-1 with a 1.60 ERA for Triple-A New Orleans. He last pitched Saturday, striking out 12 batters over six scoreless innings to record the win. Knight briefly considered retiring from baseball this offseason before latching on with the Somerset (N.J.) Patriots of the Atlantic League, and, ultimately, with the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro must figure out how to avoid the big inning. Whether it's because of concentration lapses, mechanical flaws or something else, he's been extremely prone to "crooked numbers" lately. In four of his past five starts, he's had at least one inning in which he allowed at least three runs. The other start in that span? Six and a third shutout. You do the math.
summary: 2008-07-26 - St. Louis Cardinals (10) @ New York Mets (8) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Re-establishing himself after a five-run shelling in Cincinnati, Santana pitched well enough in Tuesday's game against the Phillies to win. But it didn't work out that way. He pitched eight innings, allowing eight hits and striking out four, holding Philadelphia to two runs. Regardless, a ninth-inning implosion by the Mets bullpen stained a potential victory and produced a no-decision for Santana. Next up, the Cardinals, whom Santana hasn't faced.
away_pitcher_note: For six innings, Lohse turned in a special performance against the Brewers on Tuesday. But as he admitted, it's a nine-inning game, not six. Perfect through four innings, Lohse unraveled in the seventh and eighth innings, allowing the Brewers to come back from a 3-0 deficit and eventually win the game in the ninth. Still, Lohse has been the Cardinals' most efficient pitcher this year possessing excellent stuff en route to a 12-2 record. Two wins short of tying a career-high for a season, Lohse has pitched into the seventh inning for five straight games.
summary: 2008-07-27 - St. Louis Cardinals (1) @ New York Mets (9) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Morton was recalled from Triple-A Richmond to start Monday's series opener against the Cardinals after lefty Jo-Jo Reyes, Monday's projected starter, was needed during Sunday's game. Morton was optioned to Richmond on Saturday to make room on the active roster for Mike Hampton. Since impressing while making his first three career Major League starts in June, Morton has battled rookie inconsistency. He is 1-2 with a 7.58 ERA in his past four starts. While facing the Marlins last week, a pair of walks hurt him when Mike Jacobs followed with a homer. The lanky 24-year-old right-hander has had trouble showing consistent command with his live fastball. This will be his first career appearance against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Though his line against the Brewers in his last start was very good -- five innings pitched, seven hits, one earned run -- Looper had to exit early because of a high pitch count. He also picked up the loss because the Brewers' CC Sabathia shut out the Cardinals. However, Looper rebounded from a poor start on July 18 and pitched a solid game against one of the better lineups in the Majors. Looper is winless since June 24 -- a statistic he would love to change against Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Tim Hudson has been placed on the disabled list, so the ongoing Atlanta shuffling means that Campillo will start. The right-hander started on Sunday, but he pitched only 1 2/3 innings before a lengthy rain delay in Philadelphia forced him out of the game.
away_pitcher_note: For a while on Thursday, it appeared Wellemeyer was going to win his second straight decision for the first time since June 5. After the Cardinals bullpen lost their 23rd game of the year, though, Wellemeyer received another no-decision. For four innings, Wellemeyer had excellent stuff but succumbed to two long innings that drove up his pitch count. It was a better showing from May's Pitcher of the Month, though, and Wellemeyer another solid start would seem to say he has regained his consistency.

home_pitcher_note: Jair Jurrjens tossed eight shutout innings and allowed just three hits Friday against the Phillies, helping the Braves claim a crucial series-opening win over their division rival. Jurrjens made a spectacular defensive play to end the eighth inning, knocking down a comebacker and making a strong throw to first to get the out. Jurrjens also didn't allow a runner to reach third base. The 22-year-old right-hander walked one and struck out six while becoming the second Braves pitcher to reach 10 wins this season; Tim Hudson has 11. Jurrjens trimmed his ERA to 3.02.
away_pitcher_note: This is the moment the Redbirds have awaited for more than a season and a half, the return of their ace to the mound after a lengthy battle with elbow troubles that culminated in Tommy John surgery last July. Carpenter probably won't go much past 90 pitches, and his usually exceptional command may still be less than perfect. But he's the man for the Redbirds, and his return is a very, very big deal.

home_pitcher_note: Hampton, making his first start since Aug. 19, 2005, allowed six runs on eight hits in four-plus innings Saturday against the Phillies, but did not factor in the decision. Staked to a 9-3 lead, Hampton exited with the bases loaded and no out in the fifth. All three baserunners scored in what became a demoralizing 10-9 loss. The oft-injured left-hander tossed 91 pitches -- 55 for strikes -- and threw first-pitch strikes to 12 of the 22 batters he faced. Hampton, who missed the first four months of the season with a strained left pectoral muscle, is 10-8 with a 3.59 ERA in 26 games (21 starts) against St. Louis. He hasn't faced the Cardinals since May 12, 2004, when he allowed four runs on eight hits in six innings and lost.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro has been getting leads, but not holding them. And that's a problem. He's been ahead at some point in 15 of his starts, and yet he has only picked up three wins. He can be excellent, but he can also be frustrating. With Adam Wainwright's return coming fairly soon, Pineiro is one of three conceivable candidates to be bumped from the rotation, so he needs to show something in his next couple of starts.

home_pitcher_note: As his manager is fond of saying, "even Sinatra cleared his throat once in a while." Lohse, who had been consistently excellent for the better part of three months, endured a clunker his last time out. He's still been the Cardinals' most dependable starter this year, and he's got a big assignment with the opener of a three-game series against the potent Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels endured his harshest outing of 2008 Saturday against the Braves, giving up nine runs -- four of them earned -- in one inning. He left after 3 2/3 innings on the hill, his shortest outing this season. The Phils' bats, however, exploded for seven runs in the fifth to give Hamels the no-decision. Hamels lost his only outing against St. Louis this season, when he gave up two runs in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Looper faces a tough task in the hard-hitting Phillies, a team that made him labor three weeks ago. In that start, at Citizens Bank Park, Looper needed 112 pitches to go six innings. However, he's coming off a very solid game in Atlanta, a game in which he righted a recent problem -- the long ball. He didn't allow a home run against the Braves, after serving up 10 in his previous six starts. If he keeps it in the park, he should be fine.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton's start against the Braves on Sunday was cut short when the game was halted for a two-hour rain delay. In two innings of work prior to the delay, the Phils' new addition surrendered two runs on three hits. Blanton will make his third start for the Phillies against the Cardinals, a team he has not yet faced, having just joined the National League after about 3 1/2 seasons with the Athletics. Before joining Philadelphia, the 27-year-old right-hander went 5-12 with a 4.96 ERA for Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer may be getting it back together after a rough stretch that followed his return from an elbow injury. His last time out he struck out five, his highest total since the injury and an indication that his offspeed offerings are coming around. The Cards have been careful with him; he hasn't gone more than 6 1/3 innings or 98 pitches since the injury.
away_pitcher_note: Myers allowed one unearned run in seven innings Tuesday night against the Nationals in securing his first win since May 30. The victory over Washington could signal a breakthrough for the 27-year-old, who was optioned to Triple-A after beginning his season with a 3-9 record and 5.84 ERA. In his second start since his return, he didn't try to overpower hitters, and he ended up walking one while scattering four hits through seven. In nine career starts against St. Louis, Myers is 3-2 with a 5.43 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter will try to stretch it past four innings in his first home start since undergoing Tommy John elbow ligament replacement surgery. He'll likely be on an increased, but still limited, pitch count. That means a major key for the right-hander will be getting off to a good start, so he doesn't use up all of his pitches in the first two or three innings. His pattern in rehab starts as well as his first regular-season start was a slow beginning, followed by significant improvement.
away_pitcher_note: You don't often see shutouts end with a play at the plate, but as Billingsley said, he'll take it. He beat the Giants with a five-hitter and is 7-2 since mid-June. He leads the rotation in all the pertinent categories: victories, strikeouts, innings, etc. He's become the latest staff ace, even though he just turned 24.
summary: 2008-08-05 - Los Angeles Dodgers (4) @ St. Louis Cardinals (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro struggled again Thursday, allowing 10 hits for the fourth consecutive start. The right-hander had no explanation for his recent struggles, other than saying that he was missing up in the zone with most of his pitches. Pineiro also failed to hold onto a lead for the 16th time in 18 chances this season. Thus, he only has three wins. Pineiro has only faced the Dodgers once, on June 20, 2006, when he allowed three runs on 10 hits in 6 1/3 innings and won.
away_pitcher_note: Derek Lowe played his familiar role of tough-luck loser against the D-backs, allowing two runs and losing, receiving only one run from his offense. In his nine losses, the Dodgers have scored 10 runs. On the other hand, he was given a lead to protect and immediately gave it up. The 3.70 ERA is a better indication of his season than the win-loss record.
summary: 2008-08-06 - Los Angeles Dodgers (6) @ St. Louis Cardinals (9) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Making a start against the Phillies, Lohse had to endure one of his toughest starts of the season against a team that had won six games in a row. But he shut them down through his first five innings, only to allow a three-run home run in the sixth inning. Now he has yet another tough assignment against the Dodgers and will have to face slugger Manny Ramirez if he wants to cash in on tying a career high in wins.
away_pitcher_note: Against the Diamondbacks, Kershaw duplicated the six scoreless innings of his previous start, allowing only four hits and pitching out of two jams with runners on third base. Although he settled for a no-decision, he now has given up three runs or fewer in eight of his 11 outings and seems to have secured a regular slot in the rotation.
summary: 2008-08-07 - Los Angeles Dodgers (4) @ St. Louis Cardinals (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Lilly has thrown four quality starts in a row since the All-Star Game. Before that, the veteran left-hander held the Cardinals to two runs in six innings on July 5 and got a no-decision. He has a 3.46 ERA against the Cardinals in two starts this year and enjoys a lifetime 3.06 ERA against the Cubs' NL Central rival. He battled in his last start, against Pittsburgh, tossing 6 1/3 innings of one-run ball en route to his 11th win.
away_pitcher_note: Even though he pitched one of his better outings of the year in his last start, Looper did not get enough help from his offense to earn his 11th win. Looper gave up two solo home runs to the Phillies and they did him in. Looper has given up 17 home runs over the year, which put him at the 14th most in the National League. He has not fared all that well against the Dodgers but has allowed two runs or less in each of his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: The hard-throwing Cubs ace lowered his ERA for the third start in a row on Sunday against the Pirates. He threw only 82 pitches in five innings and did not receive a decision, as skipper Lou Piniella played it safe after Zambrano had thrown 243 pitches in his previous two starts. That, along with a fifth day of rest, means Zambrano should be well rested for his start against the Cardinals. In his last start against St. Louis, Zambrano worked six scoreless innings for the win, striking out five while giving up four hits. He is 9-4 with a 2.26 ERA in 19 career starts against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Over his last three outings, Wellemeyer has begun to regain his form that made him May's Pitcher of the Month. Giving up two runs or less in each of his last three starts, however, Wellemeyer has received three straight no-decisions. Now he gets to carry his newfound momentum against the Cubs -- the team he entered the Majors with. He has made two starts against Chicago in his career, going 1-1 with a 4.09 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster should be well-rested for this start. He matched his shortest outing of the season, five innings, in Monday's loss to Houston, but it was Mother Nature's fault. The Cubs-Astros game on Monday was halted by a thunderstorm at the start of the sixth for two hours and 45 minutes. They played two more innings before it was called for good. Dempster gave up two runs against the Astros to fall to 10-2 at home in 2008. He has yet to face the Cardinals this season, but he is very familiar with winning at Wrigley Field.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Carpenter's third start since returning from the disabled list, where he had spent the entire season. He has allowed one run on eight hits in nine innings so far. He went deeper into the game -- completing five innings -- in his last start than he did the start prior, in which he lasted four innings.

home_pitcher_note: It was a rougher second start for the right-hander, who made his 2008 debut on July 31. In his last outing, on Wednesday in Philadelphia, the 24-year-old gave up four runs (three earned) in five innings. He was taken deep by Ryan Howard, and he didn't have his pinpoint command, which got him in trouble. One of his walks and one hit batter cost him two runs. Sanchez's error also led to a Phillies run. Considering he missed more than a season because of right shoulder surgery, Sanchez understandably will have some rough stretches. His fastball was routinely about 88 mph, and he reached 91 mph once.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro said he felt like "two different pitchers" during his last start. While he struggled in the first three innings against the Dodgers -- giving up a home run to Manny Ramirez in the process -- Pineiro settled down after catcher Yadier Molina convinced him to use the sinker more often. After that, he dominated and gave up only one run over the next four innings. His inconsistency this year has hurt him, he said, and he hopes to get that straightened out for his next outing.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad had the best start of his short Major League career in a critical win against the Phillies on Thursday. The 21-year-old tossed six shutout innings against a high-powered Philadelphia offense -- stacked with strong left-handed bats -- giving up just three hits and walking four while striking out three. It was a big win for Volstad, not only because it allowed his team to take the three-game series against the Phillies, but it was a bounce-back effort just five days removed from giving up a career-high five runs (four earned) in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse is in a little bit of a funk for the first time since May, with a 7.27 ERA and five homers allowed over his past three starts. It's not as though he's been awful, but he set the bar very high earlier in the year. With any kind of a decent finish, he has a chance to be the first Cardinals pitcher to rack up more than 15 wins since three pitchers did so in 2005.

home_pitcher_note: An otherwise impressive outing was marred by two home runs in Nolasco's last start. The end result was the right-hander suffered a loss to the Mets at Shea Stadium. For the most part, Nolasco was pretty good, although he was taken deep on a two-run homer by David Wright, and Carlos Delgado added a solo shot. Nolasco has yielded two home runs in two straight games. He did work 6 2/3 innings, and scattered seven hits.
away_pitcher_note: Looper's been an interesting study lately, throwing lots of strikes and giving up lots of home runs. It hasn't hurt him too badly, because the homers have tended to be solo shots. It's not a bad way to pitch if you can keep it up, and Looper has a 2.42 ERA over his past four starts with 15 strikeouts and five walks.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off a loss to the Mets, Olsen has now dropped three straight decisions. He seeks his first win since July 19 against the Phillies. Olsen gave up four runs in the first inning, including a two-run blast to Carlos Delgado. Olsen rebounded and went into the sixth inning, but he was lifted after Fernando Tatis' leadoff single. Tatis ended up scoring, putting Olsen in line for the loss. For his career, Olsen is 1-2 with a 7.00 ERA in three games against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Much to the relief of the Cardinals, Wellemeyer is back. The pitcher who was so effective in April and May didn't look like himself for much of June and July following his return from an elbow injury. But in his last three starts, he's had stuff and command, as shown by his 13 strikeouts against three walks. He's even making progress with his changeup, to complement his impressive fastball and slider.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo did everything in his start last Saturday but win. He crafted the kind of outing that manager Dusty Baker couldn't find much to fault with. OK, maybe the double Arroyo served up to the opposing pitcher could be faulted, but that's about all. By any measure, he pitched six innings of quality baseball. He held the Astros to five hits and two runs, one of them coming after the pitcher's double. Yet the outing was a continuation of what Arroyo had done lately, which is to pitch well enough to give the Reds a chance in every game.
away_pitcher_note: With Chris Carpenter unable to pitch with a right posterior muscle strain, the Cardinals turn to Thompson, who has three starts this season but hasn't served in that role since July 19. Still, his 2.87 ERA as a starter hints at his capability. He shut out Colorado in 6 2/3 innings early in the season and also held Kansas City to two runs over five innings. Thompson also has taken his lumps in recent games as a reliever, giving up two runs and three hits against both the Cubs and Dodgers. The Dodgers did that damage in one-third of an inning. Since Thompson hasn't started since mid-June, he likely won't throw more than 60 to 70 pitches, if that.

home_pitcher_note: He had hoped for better in his return from the disabled list, but Harang didn't pitch the kind of game he's been expected to produce in his first start back. The righty was hit hard early, and he didn't spare the bullpen from getting early work. That's atypical of Harang, who has built a reputation as an innings eater. Though he wasn't sharp, Harang said he felt fine, and Reds manager Dusty Baker said the righty had good velocity. That's a fine omen for the future, because Harang must play a starring role in whatever success the Reds will have this season.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro usually rises or falls on the effectiveness of his sinkerball. It is his trademark pitch, but the catch is that lately, it has taken him several innings to get it under control. That's what happened in his last outing against the Marlins. Pineiro was down, 2-1, in the game when the sinker began working for him, but the Cardinals rallied for a much-needed 4-2 victory. And overall, Pineiro pitched his best game in nearly a month. He allowed seven hits and two runs, one earned, over seven innings in getting the victory. He floated the idea afterward of working on his sinker more intensely before games, so as to have it ready on the first pitch.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez was solid for 6 1/3 innings and earned a 5-1 win over the Pirates on Tuesday. Working on two extra days of rest, he gave up one earned run and five hits with three walks and five strikeouts. The right-hander didn't think the rest helped much because he lacked power on his pitches. But he was able to keep the ball down and stay out of trouble. Manager Dusty Baker thought Volquez threw fewer  strikes than in recent starts and almost preferred it since the pitcher might have been more effectively wild.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse acknowledged after his last game, a 4-3 loss to the Marlins, that he's been having recent problems making bad pitches at the wrong time. He certainly was victimized by a too-sweet changeup to the Marlins' Hanley Ramirez, who parked it for a decisive three-run home run. That bad pitch turned what was otherwise a good effort into a bad memory for Lohse. Also, the game was halted for a 1-hour, 53-minute rain delay in the fifth inning, shortening Lohse's work night. He pitched 4 1/3 innings, giving up six hits and four runs. He struck out five and threw and unusually high 84 pitches for the limited number of innings.

home_pitcher_note: Looper has been brilliant lately, enjoying the finest stretch of his two seasons in the starting rotation. He's pitching deep into games and throwing strikes. He's been occasionally prone to the homer, but everything else is going so well that the solo shots haven't been a problem for the most part. Over his past eight starts, Looper has 29 strikeouts and eight walks.
away_pitcher_note: Snell was good (not great), but with the way things have gone this season, his last start has to at least be a small step in the right direction. The righty gave up five walks and six hits in six innings, but somehow managed to limit the damage to just two runs scored. He would, however, be pegged with his 10th loss of the season because of no run support. The key for Snell remains pounding the strike zone, something that he has looked hesitant doing all year. Snell is winless in four starts against St. Louis this year. He's allowed 19 runs in 19 total innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer has clearly regained his form after an injury-hampered June and a slump through much of July. He's allowed eight runs over his past five starts, and his stuff has been very sharp. He's got his slider back, and he's augmenting it with an improved changeup. The right-hander will be pitching on five days' rest thanks to the Cardinals' Monday off-day.
away_pitcher_note: With two starts under his belt, Davis has solidified himself in the rotation, at least for the time being. After allowing two first-inning runs on Friday, Davis settled down and kept the Mets scoreless through the final six frames of his seven-inning start. Davis has now allowed just two earned runs in 13 innings as a starter. The righty doesn't have overpowering stuff, but it continues to be effective because he is consistently throwing down in the strike zone. Davis has never faced St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright will be making his 14th start and first since June 7. He has been on the DL with a right middle finger sprain since June 8. Wainwright has pronounced himself fully ready to face Major League hitters and claims he is snapping off his curveball harder than he was prior to the injury. The jury is still out on whether Wainwright will remain in the starting rotation or go to closer when Chris Carpenter returns. For now, Wainwright is just happy to be on the mound again in any capacity.
away_pitcher_note: In his next start, Morton will be looking to avenge the worst start of his young career. In 3 2/3 innings against the Cardinals on July 28, he allowed eight earned runs and issued four walks. During the four starts that have followed, the 24-year-old rookie right-hander has gone 1-3 with 3.63 ERA. He showed better control while allowing three earned run and issuing two walks in a losing effort against the Giants on Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse will be making this start while appealing a five-game suspension handed down by Major League Baseball for throwing a pitch near the head of Cincinnati's Edinson Volquez last Sunday. Offering consistency in a year of pitching turbulence on the Cardinals' injury-riddled staff, Lohse has proven to be an astute free agent pickup. He has delivered a staff-high 162 innings and his 13 wins leave him tied for fifth place in the National League in that category.
away_pitcher_note: Campillo has struggled in the first inning of his last two starts, giving up four runs to the Cubs and three to the Giants. He needed 37 pitches to get out of the first against San Francisco before settling down and pitching well. Campillo retired 14 straight batters until Aaron Rowand hit his 12th home run leading off the sixth inning. Campillo has surrendered 15 earned runs in his past 18 innings. Prior to that, he had allowed no more than three runs in six consecutive starts.

home_pitcher_note: Looper pitched three-hit ball over seven innings in his last start and allowed just one run. But he emerged as a tough-luck loser against Pittsburgh, continuing a recent pattern. Looper has allowed just nine earned runs in his last six starts for a 2.03 ERA. But his record is only 2-3 over that span. The Cardinals have scored only a combined four runs in those three losses.
away_pitcher_note: Reyes worked on the rhythm of his delivery while with Triple-A Richmond earlier this month, and he showed improvement while limiting the Mets to two earned runs in six innings on Tuesday. The 23-year-old southpaw has battled control issues all season, and his three walks against the Mets proved he still has some room for improvement. Before Tuesday, he had gone 0-5 with an 8.74 ERA in his previous six big league appearances.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Wellemeyer didn't finish off hitters the way he wanted to, but he still picked up the win in an 11-2 victory over the Pirates. Wellemeyer needed 95 pitches to get through five innings, but he limited Pittsburgh's damage by making big pitches when he needed to. Wellemeyer has held opposing hitters to a .230 average over his past six starts, and his ERA is 2.48 over that span.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets continued a modest slump since the acquisition of CC Sabathia when he allowed five runs in six innings against Houston on Tuesday in a Brewers loss. Once the ace of the staff, Sheets worked at least seven innings in eight of his first 16 starts, but he has gone that far in just two of his past nine. He has won only once since the team brought Sabathia on board, and the team has lost five of those eight outings.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright returned from a 2 1/2-month absence with a flourish on Friday, when he worked six innings against the Braves and allowed just five hits and one run. After recovering from a right middle finger sprain, Wainwright claims he is snapping off his curve as hard or harder than he has all season. Wainwright delivered 72 pitches in his last start and figures that he should be able to build on that total in his next outing.
away_pitcher_note: Parra and the Brewers beat the Astros on Wednesday for Parra's first win in a month, but he still wasn't happy. He faced one batter more than the minimum through three innings, then allowed five hits, three walks and two runs over the next two frames. He escaped with the lead when left fielder Gabe Kapler threw out a runner at the plate to end the fifth inning. Still, it was Parra's first win since July 20, when he was riding an eight-game winning streak. Entering Wednesday's win, Parra was 0-4 with a 5.70 ERA and a .295 opponents' batting average in five starts prior.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf gave the Astros six solid innings against the Mets on Sunday, bouncing back from early struggles to settle into a rhythm. He gave up four earned runs, including two homers, and he walked in one run with the bases loaded. But Wolf went on to retire nine of the final 11 batters he faced to keep his team within striking distance. He surrendered seven hits, striking out four with three walks. Wolf has not faced the Cardinals as a member of the Astros staff, but in his last start against St. Louis with the Padres he gave up eight hits and six runs (four earned) in 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: After a great first half, Lohse has cooled off quite a bit. He's lost three straight decisions, and the Cardinals are 1-5 in his last six starts. Lohse has not allowed fewer than three runs in a start since July 17, his first start after the All-Star break. Over his past six games, he has a 6.42 ERA and has allowed six homers in 33 2/3 innings. It's also worth noting that he's struggled on the road, with a 5.31 ERA away from St. Louis (3.16 at Busch Stadium).

home_pitcher_note: Moehler was hit hard early against the Mets, allowing a three-run home run in the first inning, which doomed him to a loss in a game where the Astros' bats were silenced. He remained solid in the second through fifth innings, though, holding down the Mets' offense until he was pulled with runners on first and second in the sixth, and a sacrifice fly would surrender fourth run on Moehler's tab. The loss broke a streak of five-straight wins for Moehler. He'll now face the Cardinals, who he held scoreless in seven innings on June 6.
away_pitcher_note: It's a short list of pitchers who are going better than Looper. He's pitched seven innings in six straight starts, and has allowed three runs or fewer in seven in a row. His ERA over his past seven outings is 2.30, and he has 52 strikeouts against 17 walks since June 6. He's also fared well in Houston, posting a 2.92 ERA as a starter at Minute Maid Park.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez struck out a career-high 10 batters in his one-run, three-hit start against the Reds. The lefty moved the position of his glove from below his chest to in front of his face, which he said made him more comfortable. He's 0-2 in three starts against St. Louis this season, with a 1.45 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer deserved better his last time out. He could easily have finished with one or two runs in six innings. But his defense betrayed him, and then he was asked to give one more inning than he had in him. Either way, it's been a fine second half for Wellemeyer, who has made a full return after elbow problems bothered him in June and even into July.

home_pitcher_note: It was like deja vu all over again for the Big Unit the last time out. He handed the bullpen a one-run lead after seven strong innings against the Padres, but for the second time in as many starts, the bullpen blew the game, and Johnson was denied his 295th career win. With the way manager Bob Melvin has the starting rotation aligned, Johnson will make six more starts in 2008, meaning he would have to win the remainder of his games to reach the 300-wins club in 2008.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro returns to the rotation after a brief stint in the bullpen. He was bumped thanks to a strange schedule that provided four off days in less than two weeks. The right-hander was actually going well, with three wins and a 3.60 ERA over his last three starts, but Chase Field presents a challenge for a pitcher who has been much more effective at new Busch Stadium than on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Petit has been pitching like an ace the last few times out, but the right-hander hasn't pitched on a consistent basis, with several off-days for the D-backs down the stretch. Manager Bob Melvin has gone with a four-man rotation recently, which has given Petit starts about once every nine days or so. Petit allowed just one run on two hits in his last start against his former team, the Marlins, as he picked up his third win of the season. Petit is 2-0 with a 1.23 ERA in 7 1/3 innings against the Cardinals in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright has looked like almost the same pitcher since his return from a finger injury. In two starts since coming off the disabled list, he's allowed 12 earned runs in 12 innings, with six strikeouts, one walk and one home run allowed. The one thing he hasn't done is get a lot of swings-and-misses, but his command has been good enough that he hasn't needed them. When Wainwright starts getting fruitless swings, you'll know he's all the way back.

home_pitcher_note: Davis had a decent outing his last start, tossing five innings, allowing just two runs on eight hits and three walks, and he picked up the win against the Dodgers. Davis seems to be back on track after scuffling in three straight starts, allowing 16 runs in 11 innings. The left-hander is 4-5 with a 5.05 ERA in 13 career games against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse ended a string of so-so performances his last time out, but he still couldn't get a win. He was outstanding in Houston, allowing two runs over eight innings, but a late game-tying homer cost him the W. Still, there's reason to be at least somewhat concerned. Lohse has been much, much better at home (3.16 ERA) than on the road (4.97), and he has a lifetime 5.50 ERA at Chase Field.

home_pitcher_note: The Cardinals could still get clever with this spot, but it's unlikely. Looper had been pitching extremely well before his dud in Houston on Saturday, and since becoming a starter he's pitched very well against the Marlins. He'll be aiming for a career-best 13th win, though he'll also be trying to avoid falling back to .500. If Looper keeps the ball down, which he couldn't do against the Astros, he'll be fine.
away_pitcher_note: In a no-decision against the Mets on Saturday, Nolasco wasn't his usual, dominant self, but he was able to do just enough to keep his team in the ballgame, which led to an eventual walk-off win. The 25-year-old gave up two runs in the first inning but only scattered one more in his next five. What's most impressive is Nolasco struck out eight batters while issuing only one walk. Over his last seven starts, he's struck out 59 batters and walked just four.

home_pitcher_note: In Wellemeyer's last outing, he picked up the loss, despite allowing just one run on four hits in seven strong innings against the Astros, as they shut out the Cards, 3-0, at Minute Maid Park. Wellemeyer was hard on himself after the game because he couldn't put a bunt down, which could have led to a run. The right-hander is 2-1 with a 2.38 ERA in his career against the Marlins, spanning four outings, one start.
away_pitcher_note: The long ball plagued Olsen in a loss to the Mets on Sunday. That afternoon saw the 24-year-old give up three solo shots, which tied his season high, and exit after throwing 104 pitches in 6 1/3 innings. In the seventh, Olsen was charged with three more runs and threw 15 pitches to four batters before his outing ended. Over his past five starts, Olsen has given up 22 runs in 27 2/3 innings, posting a 6.67 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Plenty has gone wrong on the pitching side for the Cardinals this year, especially when it comes to injured hurlers. There's this good news, though: Wainwright looks like himself. In three games since he returned from the disabled list, Wainwright has 13 strikeouts, three walks and one homer allowed. He's still building back to full strength and sharpness, but if this is building mode, then clearly there's a lot to like.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson has logged six straight quality starts -- minimum of six innings and no more than three runs. The 24-year-old right-hander did struggle, however, in his last start -- a no-decision against the Braves. It was the second straight time Johnson faced Atlanta. On Aug. 27, he tossed a complete-game, four-hitter, and won, 4-1. He threw a season-high 113 pitches on that day. But in his Sept. 1 contest with Atlanta in Miami, Johnson gave up three runs in six innings. The Braves scratched out nine hits, but Johnson didn't issue a walk. The right-hander struck out eight.

home_pitcher_note: Ever wonder why statheads say wins don't matter? Take a look at Lohse's past four starts. He's pitched 26 innings, allowing eight runs for a 2.77 ERA. He's struck out 18 against eight walks, and given up exactly one home run. To top it off, three of those four starts have come in three of the most hitter-friendly parks in baseball, in Cincinnati, Houston and Phoenix. And yet he's 0-1 in those games. Can somebody please buy this guy a break?
away_pitcher_note: In his next start, Dempster will be vying for his career-high 16th win once again. The right-hander suffered a rare loss at home in his last start, against Houston. He gave up three runs on eight hits in seven innings, but the Cubs' offense continued to sputter. Since the All-Star break, Dempster is 5-2 with a 2.44 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Looper bounced back superbly from his first rocky start in months. And in fact, on Friday against Florida, he looked like he was as much in command as he has been all season. That makes eight very good starts out of nine for Looper, who may be earning himself a lot of money with this stretch drive. Looper likely isn't thinking about his first time in free agency as a starting pitcher, but you can bet other teams are taking notice of his very solid season.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly struggled in his last start, a brief two-inning outing against the Reds. He gave up five runs on four hits and three walks over two innings, his shortest stint of the year. Lilly struggled with location and offspeed pitches against the Reds, falling to 0-4 against them this year. As Cubs manager Lou Piniella said, it was not what they expected. Lilly has one win in three outings against St. Louis this year.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer is dealing lately. He started the year hot, hurt his elbow and struggled upon his return to action, but over the past six weeks, he's going as well as he has all year. In his past eight starts, Wellemeyer has a 2.75 ERA, 37 strikeouts and 12 walks in 52 1/3 innings. One thing worth watching is his durability, since he's coming off the longest start of his career -- eight innings and 119 pitches, both new personal highs.
away_pitcher_note: Harden should be well rested. Because of his history of right elbow problems, the Cubs chose to give the right-hander an extended breather. Harden's last start was on Aug. 29, against the Phillies, and he did not get a decision. Harden threw 100 pitches in five innings, giving up two runs (one earned) on three hits and four walks. He now has 167 strikeouts, matching his career high set in 2004, when he was a member of the A's. Harden finished August with a 3-0 record and a 1.82 ERA, giving up six earned runs in 29 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Coming back after his streak of 20 consecutive starts with six or more innings had bitten the dust, Maholm got back in that mode by lasting six full innings against the Giants. Maholm never looked fully comfortable, though, and he was helped by a double play that should have just been a forceout. Maholm said he's not fatigued, despite having thrown a career-high 185 1/3 innings to this point.

Scheduled starter Jeff Karstens will miss this start because of an abscessed tooth on the left side of his mouth The right-hander sat in the Pirates' clubhouse on Friday with a swollen left cheek, which didn't heal enough to allow him to take the mound tonight. Ian Snell will pitch in Karstens' place, but will have had a regular four days of rest because of the Pirates' move to a six-man rotation on Sept. 2.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright is dealing, and it's just like he never left. The right-hander has put to rest the only two lingering questions from his first couple of starts off the disabled list. He's missing bats again, to the tune of 13 strikeouts in his past two outings. And he lasted eight innings on Sunday, his longest start since before he injured his finger. It's a short list of better starters in the NL than a healthy Wainwright.

home_pitcher_note: Davis' bouncing in and out of the starting rotation continues. The right-hander will take the mound on Sunday for Ian Snell, who filled in for an injured Jeff Karstens on Saturday night. The start will be Davis' fourth with the Pirates this season. In those games, he's given up 12 runs in 16 2/3 innings pitched. Manager John Russell said Davis will be limited in his pitch count.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro, initially slated for Friday, started the series opener in Pittsburgh. Thompson, announced as Friday's starter on Thursday, will instead pitch the series finale on Sunday. Thompson is 5-2 with a 4.61 ERA this season in 23 games, four of which were starts.

home_pitcher_note: Despite saying that only his sinker was working for him, Arroyo pitched brilliantly but wasn't rewarded with a decision on Wednesday at Milwaukee. He gave up two unearned runs and five hits over seven innings with four walks and three strikeouts. Two Reds errors led to two Brewers runs while Arroyo was opposed by tough lefty CC Sabathia. Arroyo still left the game with a 3-1 lead before a two-run Brewers eighth cost him a victory in a 4-3 Cincinnati loss.
away_pitcher_note: Can somebody please buy this guy a break? Looper is pitching as well as almost anybody in the league, but he's not getting the wins to show it. The latest example came on Wednesday, when he allowed four runs, but just one earned. Over his past 10 starts, Looper has a 2.97 ERA, and he has eight games with two earned runs or fewer. Yet he's only 3-5 in that span.

home_pitcher_note: On Friday at Arizona, Harang gave up one unearned run and four hits with an intentional walk and four strikeouts over seven superbly pitched innings. He was saddled with the loss in a 3-2 defeat. He's had five-straight quality starts and a 2.45 ERA in those games but just one win to show for it. Harang last faced the Cardinals on Aug. 16 and tied a career high with eight earned runs allowed over 3 1/3 innings during a 9-3 loss at Great American Ball Park.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer has somewhat quietly put together an excellent season, to the point where you can make a case that he's been the Cardinals' second-best starter. He's a native of Louisville, Ky., so pitching in Cincinnati brings him close to home and puts him in front of plenty of family and friends. Wellemeyer has a 2.87 ERA away from Busch Stadium, but Great American Ball Park is not your average place to pitch on the road -- mistakes get punished, so he'll have to avoid them.

home_pitcher_note: Pitch count should be a concern for Volquez, who established his career high in each of his last two starts. On Saturday, during a 3-2 Reds win in 10 innings, the right-hander was foiled in his third attempt for a 17th victory when he gave up two earned runs and five hits over six-plus innings. He tied a season high with six walks and eight strikeouts and threw 120 pitches. Frequently showing frustration, Volquez made mistakes like issuing a four-pitch walk to pitcher Randy Johnson and hitting light hitter Augie Ojeda with an 0-2 pitch in the third inning. Volquez allowed the leadoff runner to reach in each of the first five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse returns from suspension, but not as quickly as he had hoped. He'll be pitching on eight full days' rest, which isn't Lohse's preference but which pitching coach Dave Duncan said might do him some good. Lohse has a 4.92 ERA over his past nine starts, though he has 41 strikeouts against 15 walks in that span. Lohse hasn't pitched at Wrigley Field this year, but he pitched brilliantly there in an April 2007 start -- eight shutout innings, 12 strikeouts and one walk.

home_pitcher_note: What did Zambrano do in his last start? Oh yeah, he threw a no-hitter against the Astros. In Milwaukee. After missing a turn in the rotation with rotator cuff tendinitis. Zambrano struck out 10, walked one and hit a batter en route to the first Cubs no-hitter in 36 years. Before that, he had gone more than six innings once since Aug. 1 and had to undergo an MRI to determine what was wrong. Well, problem fixed. In two starts against St. Louis this year, he's 1-1 with a 7.84 ERA. Zambrano is trying to become the third Cubs starter to reach 15 wins this season. Ryan Dempster has 16, and Ted Lilly has 15.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a shockingly subpar performance, Wainwright is hungry to redeem himself in what is sure to be a charged atmosphere at Wrigley Field. Wainwright just didn't feel strong on Saturday night in Pittsburgh and was clearly affected by the muggy conditions. Facing the Cubs won't be an easy task for him, and he's never beaten them, but never bet against Wainwright when he has extra motivation.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly nearly followed Carlos Zambrano to make it back-to-back no-hitters for the Cubs against the Astros on Monday. He settled for a combined one-hitter, giving up a single to Mark Loretta with no outs in the seventh. Lilly struck out nine and walked one in seven innings, throwing 88 pitches. That magnificent outing followed an eight-inning, one-run performance against St. Louis in his previous start. Lilly's ERA is at a season low, and he's 2-0 with a 2.54 ERA in four starts against the Cardinals this year.
away_pitcher_note: Nobody was happy with Pineiro's last outing, except perhaps the Pirates. He alternated outstanding innings with shaky ones, throwing just enough good pitches to make it that much more maddening when he got knocked around. Once again he'll be pitching on an unconventional schedule, this time going on seven days' rest. It will be his third start in 35 days.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster won his career-high 16th game of the season Tuesday, tossing six innings of two-run, seven-hit ball. After surrendering Prince Fielder's two-out double to center in the first, he retired the next 11 batters he faced. He struck out nine batters and is now 18 shy of 200 K's for the second time in his career. In two starts against St. Louis this season, Dempster is 1-0 with a 3.29 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Somehow, some way, things are going to break right for Looper to get a win. He was in control for five innings on Tuesday against the Reds, then he lost a handle in the sixth. Overall, Looper has been better than his record would indicate, and in recent weeks that difference is even starker. Over his last 11 starts, Looper has averaged more than 6 1/3 innings per game, he has a 3.18 ERA -- and his record is 3-6.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer was done in by one ugly inning on Wednesday in Cincinnati, pitching exceptionally well except for a three-homer fourth frame. He's looking to finish strong in his first full season as a Major League starter, and it's already fair to say the season has been a success. Wellemeyer leads the team in strikeouts and is going to top 180 innings -- likely with a sub-4.00 ERA. That's a pretty nice year.
away_pitcher_note: Webb picked up his National League-leading 21st win of the season the last time out against the Giants at Chase Field, throwing seven innings, allowing three runs -- two earned -- on eight hits. He didn't know it at the time, but his second-inning two-run double proved to be pretty decisive in a 7-6 win. With two more starts left, Webb can tie Curt Schilling for the second-highest season win total in a season in franchise history with 23.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse finally got a win to show for his solid efforts recently, giving him 14 victories to equal a career high. Over his last six starts he's averaged 6 1/3 innings per game with a 3.08 ERA, yet he only has one win. There's a lot to like about the way Lohse is pitching, though, with or without the victories. He's struck out 23 against seven walks in his past four starts. And on Thursday against the Reds, he did the one thing he hadn't been doing: he avoided the one big hit when he got in trouble.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson escaped a first-inning jam by allowing just one run after the first three hitters of the game got on base. That was all the Big Unit ended up allowing the entire game as he matched Giants ace Tim Lincecum pitch for pitch. He was in line for his 295th career win until Juan Cruz allowed a game-tying homer in the eighth. Johnson, who recently missed a start with shoulder fatigue, saw his velocity drop to the high 80's. He took an unconventional approach on Thursday, throwing several breaking balls to retire the Giants hitters, the most breaking balls manager Bob Melvin said he has ever seen Johnson throw in a game.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright bounced back from a subpar outing by beating the Cubs over the weekend, but he still didn't pitch up to his own standards. With one start left to make a mark on the season, he'll be looking to finish with an 11th win and a positive note to go into the winter. The Cardinals are 14-5 when Wainwright starts this year, making it clear just how much they missed him when he was out from early June to late August.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer is still looking for his first big-league win despite pitching well in all his starts. His last outing against the Rockies was typical of the way his year has gone. The right-hander scattered seven hits and allowed just three runs over six innings, but a lack of run support cost him in a 3-2 defeat. A hard thrower, Scherzer's fastball reaches the upper 90s. His secondary pitches -- slider and change -- have gotten better as the year has gone on.

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro's last opportunity to salvage an often-frustrating season comes at home against Arizona. He actually pitched better than his line (six innings, five runs, three earned) his last time out, limiting the damage after a number of defensive missteps behind him. He may be a tired hurler, since he headed home to Florida to be with his wife and newborn twins between starts.
away_pitcher_note: Davis deserved a better fate than he received in his last outing against the Rockies. The left-hander allowed just two runs over six innings and left with a 3-2 lead only to watch the bullpen give it up. Arizona eventually got the win, but it came too late for Davis, who has received no-decisions in each of his last four starts despite not allowing more than three runs in any of those games. This will be Davis' final start of the year and he will finish with a below .500 record for the first time 2003.

home_pitcher_note: It's Looper's last chance at a 13th win, a number he deserved to reach several starts ago. He has 21 strikeouts and three walks over his last four starts -- and four losses. Sometimes it's the defense, sometimes the offense, sometimes the bullpen, and sometimes a combination. But things just haven't broken right behind Looper lately.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo will be making his final start of the 2008 season. He has to hope its better than his penultimate start of the season, because it didn't go as well as he had expected. While his eight strikeouts in six innings suggested he was in good form, those strikeouts were deceiving. They masked three walks and six hits, which kept Arroyo under pressure. Throw in his inability to contain Brewers slugger Prince Fielder and Arroyo had cooked up a recipe for defeat.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer is coming off a solid outing against Arizona in which he allowed three runs on nine hits over six innings. The right-hander has put himself in position to be in the club's pitching staff mix for next season by delivering 185 1/3 innings over 31 starts and limiting opposing hitters to a .244 batting average.
away_pitcher_note: Harang has a 2.39 ERA over his last seven starts, including a complete-game shutout over St. Louis on Sept. 17 where he allowed only six hits. Harang was a 7-5 winner on Monday vs. the Marlins but needed some help after falling behind by a 4-0 score after three innings. He allowed four earned runs and eight hits, including two solo home runs, over seven innings with two walks and six strikeouts. He would like very much to end a down season on a high note during his final 2008 start.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse bids to become a 16-game winner before possibly testing his value as a free agent. Lohse has continually said he would like to return to St.Louis, where he burst into prominence after being a late-winter signee. Lohse gained some motivation to show teams his worth after he was basically an afterthought in last year's free agent pitching crop. He has six quality starts in his past seven outings and reached a three-ball count just once against the 26 hitters he faced in his last start against Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Pettyjohn is taking the place of Edinson Volquez, who was scratched as a precaution because of left knee tendinitis. The 31-year-old Pettyjohn led the International League in wins with a 15-6 record and 4.59 ERA in 28 starts this season for Triple-A Louisville. In two relief outings with the Reds, he is 0-0 with a 4.50 ERA, with one run allowed in two innings. His relief outing on Sept. 14 at Arizona was his first Major League appearance since Oct. 4, 2001, for the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note:
It was no slam dunk that Wainwright would get the call to start Opening Day for the Cardinals. Kyle Lohse had the most impact for the Cards in 2008, reaching 200 innings with a 3.78 ERA and challenging for an All-Star berth. And of course Chris Carpenter is the leader of the staff and has a Cy Young award on his mantel. But Wainwright has nonetheless earned the assignment with a pair of outstanding seasons.

Wainwright's 2008 was cut short by a finger injury that caused him to miss 2 1/2 months, so he made only 20 starts. Despite that, he was the clear front man on a surprising starting staff. He throws strikes, keeps the ball down, gets groundballs and can miss bats when he needs to.

Wainwright has a full four-pitch arsenal, with a quality fastball, a top-notch curveball, a changeup and a slider that he sometimes throws smaller, like a cutter.
away_pitcher_note:
Maholm begins the season as the Pirates' newfound ace, a label appropriately bestowed upon the left-hander after his breakout season in 2008. Maholm established career highs in starts (31), innings pitched (206 1/3) and strikeouts (139) last year on his way to a team-best nine win season. It was Maholm's efficiency and ability to avoid big innings last year that helped transform the lefty from a relatively unknown middle-of-the-rotation starter to a the Piratesmost dependable arm. At one point last year, Maholm pitched through the sixth inning in 20 consecutive starts.

In his first 19 2/3 innings in Grapefruit League play, Maholm allowed just one earned run and one walk. He had more strikeouts (11) than hits allowed (10).

Maholm made three starts against the Cardinals last season and went 2-1 with a 3.05 ERA. In two career starts at Busch Stadium, he is 1-1 with a 3.55 ERA. He also not alone in the fact that Albert Pujols has given him more fits at the plate than anyone else expected to be in St. Louis' Opening Day lineup. Pujols is 8-for-16 against Maholm with three doubles, one homer and three RBIs. Pujols has also drawn five walks.

home_pitcher_note:
Lohse was a revelation in 2008, signing in March then going on to anchor a Cardinals rotation that exceeded expectations. Before the year was out, he signed a new four-year deal, indicating his and the club's satisfaction with the match.

Lohse threw strikes, kept the ball in the park and totaled 200 innings for his new club. If he even approximates his 2008 performance, it will be a successful season.
away_pitcher_note:
Snell took a step back in 2008 after entering the year fresh off signing a five-year contract with the club. Though he did make 31 starts, he threw 43 2/3 fewer innings than he did in 2007 when he made 32 starts. Those numbers point to Snell biggest culprit last season, which was his inefficiency.

Snell has since admitted that he pressed early while trying to live up to his contract, and with Snell, channeling his mental side could be the biggest hurdle to overcome. With 25 wins combined in 2006 and 2007, Snell has shown he has the stuff. Now he just needs to reclaim it.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer was one of the biggest surprises in the National League in 2008, even if his breakout season was obscured by an even more noteworthy story on the other side of the ball, in Ryan Ludwick. At age 29, he thrived in his first full season as a Major League starter. Wellemeyer had a bit of a rough spring, never really getting going, but he'll have every opportunity to show that his 2008 season was reflective of the quality of pitcher he really is.
away_pitcher_note: Duke arguably has more to prove than any other Pirates starter this year. Memories of his sensational 2005 season seem long gone after the three subpar years that followed. But if anyone looks refreshed as Spring Training comes to a close, it's this left-hander. His results this spring were impressive, and Duke says that his arm strength is as good as it's ever been. If there was good news to come out of 2008, it was that Duke stayed healthy all season. Now, in a year in which his salary jumped to $2.2 million, he has to have the results to accompany that health.

home_pitcher_note: This will quite certainly be the biggest start made anywhere in baseball on the season's fourth day. Most clubs, after all, won't be trotting out a former Cy Young winner in the No. 4 spot in their rotations. But that's the case with the Cardinals and Carpenter, the '05 National League Cy Young and an exceptional pitcher as recently as 2006. He had an outstanding spring, allowing just four earned runs -- all of them in his final start. Assuming Carpenter stays healthy after missing nearly two full years due to elbow and shoulder problems, he's truly a top-flight starter.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf made just five appearances in Pittsburgh last season after coming over in a six-player trade in July. But by the time he pitched for the Pirates, it was obvious arm fatigue had set in. This spring, though, has provided a better glimpse of what the Pirates hope that Ohlendorf is capable of. He has shown no hesitancy to pitch inside, and an adjustment in his delivery has him more consistent. He has a power arm, and the Pirates love the fact that he has walked just two in 22 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro was angry after he was not chosen to start for Puerto Rico in the World Baseball Classic, but he may have found an outlet for that energy. He had an excellent spring, leading to hopes that he'll pitch more like he did late in 2007 than in a frustrating 2008. An effective Pineiro would make an enormous difference for the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Hampton will be attempting to log his first full season since 2004. The left-hander has dealt with a rash of injuries over the last four years, but his solid finish with the Braves in '08 -- he was 3-4 with a 4.85 ERA from July 26 through the end of the season -- was enough to convince the Astros he was worth a shot. Hampton is beginning his second tour with Houston. He posted a 69-40 record and  a 3.40 ERA from 1994-99 and played in three postseasons with the Astros (1997-99).

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright's first regular season start looked a lot like most of his games in the spring. There was plenty to like, starting with seven strikeouts. But there was also plenty to give pause, most notably five walks, tying a career high. Wainwright needed 94 pitches to get 16 outs, and that's not going to be good enough. He must be more efficient and get deeper into games.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt will stay on schedule to pitch every fifth day, which pushes the fifth starter, Russ Ortiz, out of the rotation the first time through. Oswalt was 0-1 with a 4.15 ERA over two starts vs. the Cardinals last year. He is 9-6 with a 2.90 ERA in his career against St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: It will be interesting to see how Lohse responds after a pretty tough assignment in his first start. He grinded out seven innings, with the last two being fairly eventful, and needed 108 pitches to do so. Those certainly aren't red-flag numbers, but Lohse did work hard on a chilly night early in the season. It's reasonable to expect him to show no ill effects, but if he does look a bit winded against Houston, his battle against the Pirates may partly explain it.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez will stay on his regular schedule despite Thursday's off day. The lefty was 1-2 with a 1.11 ERA over four starts against the Cardinals in 2008, allowing three runs over 24 1/3 innings. In his career, Rodriguez is 2-6 with a 4.08 ERA against St. Louis. He's allowed 24 earned runs over 53 innings.
