home_pitcher_note: Davis did not have one of his better outings on Wednesday as he allowed four runs on four hits in five innings and the D-backs lost to the Rockies, 9-2, at Chase Field. Things didn't start on a good note for the left-hander as he allowed a home run to Dexter Fowler on the game's first pitch. He settled in for a couple of innings after that, but the Rockies were able to put up a three spot against him in the fourth. Davis was limited to 146 innings last year, his lowest total since 2003, due to a battle with thyroid cancer. This spring, he was set back with some soreness in his left triceps, but by the end of spring seemed to be fine.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer hasn't really been quite right at any point this year, whether it be in Spring Training or his first start. He's identified a mechanical key that he believes will solve the issue, so the hope is that he'll be sorted out in time for Monday's game. He'll need to be, as he's pitching in one of the National League's most hitter-friendly ballparks.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer will be making his season debut. He was set back in January when his shoulder was a little stiff and he received a cortisone shot. Since that time he has not complained of any problems with the shoulder. The right-hander started for Class A Visalia on Thursday and allowed two runs (one earned) on one hit and four walks over 4 2/3 innings. He was dazzling in his Major League debut last year when he struck out seven in 4 1/3 hitless innings of relief. It was the longest debut outing in modern Major League history by a pitcher who retired every hitter he faced.
away_pitcher_note: It's hard to imagine how Carpenter can improve on his first start, which incidentally brought his first win since the 2006 World Series. He showed outstanding stuff and command with all of his repertoire, and he was efficient enough to get through seven innings on 92 pitches. Now he'll try to repeat that showing at a tough ballpark for pitchers.

home_pitcher_note: Garland won his first regular-season game in a D-backs uniform last Friday when he held the Dodgers to three runs on five hits over seven innings. The right-hander had allowed just one run over 6 1/3 innings before giving up a two-run homer to Casey Blake in the seventh on a sinker that stayed up a little more than he would have liked. Garland, who was signed as a free agent in January, also drew a key walk during a five-run third-inning rally.
away_pitcher_note: One down, 30 or so to go, but in the early going Pineiro looks very good. He pitched a fine game in his season debut on Friday night against Houston. However, he's often pitched very well at Busch Stadium. Now he'll have to do it on the road, at a tough park for pitchers, in Phoenix. Still, Pineiro has been excellent since the start of Spring Training, and he and the Cards are confident that he can enjoy a better year in 2009 than he posted in '08.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Marshall's first start of the season. The lefty won the fifth starter's spot this spring, but struggled a little in two Cactus League outings after he was named. Marshall was the swingman last year, making seven starts and posting a 4.15 ERA and appearing in 27 games in relief and compiling a 3.42 ERA. He is 2-1 with a 3.38 ERA lifetime against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: The Redbirds' Opening Day starter still hasn't quite found the groove that made him so good in 2008 and most of 2007. However, he has an ERA under 2.00 even while he's been searching for his form. That tells you something about how good Wainwright is capable of being. He's had some struggles at Wrigley and against the Cubs, but there's no hesitation to give him the ball in the opener of the first series of the year between the two old rivals.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Zambrano's first start at home this season. The right-hander was 7-2 at Wrigley last year. In his last start Saturday night at Miller Park, Zambrano gave up three runs on seven hits and three walks over six innings. He did strike out seven, but also threw 118 pitches. Prince Fielder connected on one of those for his first homer. The runs were the first off Zambrano at Miller Park in 20 innings. He was 1-2 with a 12.75 ERA against the Cardinals last year.
away_pitcher_note: Walters impressed the Major League staff in Spring Training, leapfrogging to the top of the sixth-starter chart. He throws strikes and keeps the ball on the ground, two traits that endear any young pitcher to manager Tony La Russa and pitching coach Dave Duncan. Still, Walters struggled somewhat last year in his first exposure to Triple-A, and it will be intriguing to see how he handles big league hitters in his first shot.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster got a little help from Reed Johnson to pick up the win in his last start. Johnson robbed Prince Fielder of a potential grand slam in the fifth. For the game, Dempster gave up four runs on six hits and three walks over six innings while striking out six. He said he didn't feel sharp and kept getting behind hitters. Dempster will be happy to be home. The right-hander was 14-3 last year at Wrigley.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse has been exceptional thus far, but he's worked hard. In each of his first two starts, he's stuck it out to get some extra outs when, ideally, he might have benefited from being relieved. Still, each time, he's been able to grind it out and get the job done. He's likely to benefit from the extra day of rest that he'll receive following a little bit of rotation shuffling in the wake of Chris Carpenter's injury.

home_pitcher_note: The left-handed Lilly ignored nasty weather in the Cubs' home opener and held the Rockies to one hit over 6 2/3 innings en route to a win. He struck out eight. This is the first time he's opened the season 2-0 since 2003. Last year, he was 3-0 with a 3.06 ERA against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer has simplified his delivery in between starts and it has paid dividends. In his most recent start, he went seven innings against the Diamondbacks on Monday, allowing seven hits, and one earned run. He struck out four and didn't walk a batter. In Wellemeyer's first start of the season, he gave up 12 hits and five runs in a loss to Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer has simplified his delivery in between starts and it has paid dividends. In his most recent start, he went seven innings against the Diamondbacks on Monday, allowing seven hits, and one earned run. He struck out four and didn't walk a batter. In Wellemeyer's first start of the season, he gave up 12 hits and five runs in a loss to Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Perez is coming off his first win of the season on Wednesday night, a six-inning, one-run performance against the Padres. Although the lefty admitted to not having his best fastball, Perez used his slider and changeup early and often to keep San Diego's batters off balance. He fanned four and walked two, allowing two of the Padres' three hits to Luis Rodriguez. For Perez, it's all about consistency and Wednesday night he used a methodical approach, throwing 57 of 90 pitches for strikes.
summary: 2009-04-21 - New York Mets (4) @ St. Louis Cardinals (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Between Sunday's rainout and Monday's off day, the Cardinals will buy Pineiro two extra days of rest. Pineiro has one good start and one so-so one to his name thus far, but St. Louis has won both games. One trend has held in each of the three seasons in which he's pitched for the Cardinals: He is much better at Busch Stadium than away from home.
away_pitcher_note: After cruising through the first two frames with barely a hiccup on Thursday, Maine opened the third inning with a walk to Henry Blanco. Three of the next four Padres connected for a base hit, as San Diego batted around the order and worked Maine for a 46-pitch, five run inning. The right-hander exited after allowing six earned runs in five innings, to mark his first loss of the year.  Maine is a solid pitcher who has been plagued by one or two bad innings. He is getting stronger and will try to harness a 95 mph fastball to his advantage.
summary: 2009-04-22 - New York Mets (2) @ St. Louis Cardinals (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Even with the rainout and off day, Lohse will stay on turn, pitching on four days' rest. He didn't fare so well against the Cubs, so he'll pitch against the Mets instead. Mind you, he had a little bit of trouble against New York last year as well, but either way it's not like Lohse will be defenseless. He's been very good at home since joining the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez isn't fancy, but in manager Jerry Manuel's words, the veteran "always gives us a chance to win." That was the case again on Friday night, when Hernandez allowed one run over the first four innings before surrendering a three-run homer to Milwaukee's Ryan Braun. The Mets went on to win, 5-4. As a No. 5 starter, Hernandez gives the Mets much-needed consistency and length, and he'll look to accomplish that same feat in St. Louis. In 16 career starts against the Cardinals, Hernandez is 5-5 with a 4.33 ERA.
summary: 2009-04-23 - New York Mets (8) @ St. Louis Cardinals (12) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: This start will put Wainwright on seven full days' rest, a decision the Cardinals chalk up to matchups -- they preferred Wainwright against the Cubs and Kyle Lohse against the Mets, rather than vice versa. Still, it should also allow Wainwright an extra bullpen session in which to get sorted out, since he still has yet to have a game in which he pitched up to his own standards.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster did not factor in the decision his last time out, when he took on the Cardinals. The Cubs eventually won, 7-5, in 11 innings, and Dempster helped keep Chicago in the game, even though he wasn't sharp early. In six innings, Dempster allowed four runs on four hits and retired nine of the final 10 hitters he faced.

home_pitcher_note: Boggs entered the spring as the primary candidate to get a start if anything happened to one of the regular starting five. Then he got hurt in Spring Training, and P.J. Walters passed him on the depth chart. But Boggs showed the Cardinals something they liked in his relief appearance last time out, and he'll get a look against Chicago. One thing that impressed the staff last season was that he didn't shrink from difficult or high-profile assignments, and a Saturday afternoon game in front of a big crowd against the Cubs certainly fits that description.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Marshall's second start of the season. He did not get a decision in his first outing against the Cardinals, giving up three runs on seven hits and two walks over five-plus innings. He also struck out four. Lou Piniella's concern was that Marshall had some trouble with the Cardinals' left-handed hitters, and threw too many pitches to them. The lefty, who won the fifth starter spot this spring, is 1-0 with a 2.12 ERA in six games in his career against the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: Just as it seemed Wellemeyer had gotten sorted out after an iffy spring and start of the season, he was a bit shaky again on Tuesday. As he pointed out, though, some of what happened against him on Tuesday was a matter of ground balls finding holes. Additionally, Wellemeyer hasn't historically done well on long rest, and he had seven days between starts last time out. He'll need to be better against a potent Cubs team, but he's pitched very well against his old team.
away_pitcher_note: Harden showed he's a hearty Canadian in his last start. He shrugged off 40-degree temperatures at Wrigley Field to strike out eight over six innings against the Reds. The right-hander wore short sleeves despite the cold and gave up three hits. It was a much improved outing from his previous start, when he lasted three innings. He's now fanned 26 in his three starts. Harden won his only start against the Cardinals last season.

home_pitcher_note: Since issuing five walks during his April 12 start, Jurrjens has been a man on a mission.  Some of his teammates said the finest start of his career occurred on April 17, when he limited the Pirates to one run in 6 2/3 innings and suffered his only loss of the season.  But the 23-year-old right-hander fared even better on Wednesday, when he tossed  7 2/3 scoreless innings against the Nationals and got a no-decision. While he won his first two starts, he has proven much more efficient during his past two outings.
away_pitcher_note: A couple of patterns don't seem to favor Pineiro, but don't write him off. In the early going, he's alternated quality, with an excellent start followed by an iffy one followed by an excellent one. Moreover, he's been much better at home than on the road since he became a Cardinal. Still, he looks like something of a different pitcher this year, pitching aggressively with a two-seam fastball. He'll be looking to make it four wins in four starts.

home_pitcher_note: While enduring a four-run sixth inning on April 18 in Pittsburgh, Reyes ruined what was an otherwise impressive season debut. His season debut for Triple-A Gwinnett was also soured by a three-run sixth inning.  The 23-year-old southpaw is 0-8 with a 7.82 ERA during his past 14  big league appearances (13 starts).  This year he has committed himself to pitching to contact and avoiding the temptation to overpower opponents with his fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse's last two starts haven't been as good as his first two, and it's fair to whether he's showing any ill effects from working hard in his first two games. The bigger question, though, is his right knee, which he turned in his last inning on Thursday. The Cardinals will watch him closely and make sure he's able to go before they send him to the mound on Tuesday.

home_pitcher_note: Since encountering bad luck during his first two starts, Vazquez has won his past two outings and kept himself among the Major League strikeout leaders.  The 32-year-old right-hander has allowed just one earned run over his past 12 innings. Since issuing an uncharacteristically high four walks during his season debut, he's gone 18 innings during which he's recorded 29 strikeouts and issued just three walks. Vazquez hasn't faced the Cardinals since 2006.
away_pitcher_note: It took four starts, but Wainwright really looked like himself in his last outing. He located his pitches, got ahead in counts, got swings and misses, and made it through the seventh inning. It's exactly the sort of thing one expects to see from right-hander, and there's no reason to think he won't be able to offer more of the same on Wednesday. Pitching against the Braves, the team that drafted him, has tended to bring out the best in Wainwright. He has a 1.12 ERA in 24 Major League innings against Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Mets, Cabrera retired the first two batters he faced. Then the problems started. After Carlos Beltran singled and Carlos Delgado walked, David Wright hit what looked like a routine fly ball to center fielder Elijah Dukes. But Dukes, who had his sunglasses on the top of his head, lost the ball in the sun as it dropped in for a two-base error, which allowed two runs to score. By the time he left the game in the third inning, Cabrera threw 86 pitches, and the Mets had a 5-0 lead. Cabrera said he was not rattled by Dukes' error. He felt he should have been able to give the Nationals a quality start.
away_pitcher_note: Boggs earned this start by pitching very well five days earlier. He showed against the Cubs just what he needs to be effective: keep his sinking fastball down in the strike zone, and get chases with his breaking ball. Those things won't always both be there for him, but when they are, he's well-equipped to get Major League hitters out. He won't blow many people away, but he has good enough stuff to get outs.

home_pitcher_note: Call Jordan Zimmermann the Nationals' stopper. The right-hander tossed another great game and helped the Nationals defeat the Mets, 8-1, on Sunday to snap a three-game losing streak. There were 40,023 at Citi Field, and Zimmerman had never pitched in front of a large crowd before. But there were no signs of nervousness on his part. Zimmermann pitched 5 1/3 innings and gave up just one run on six hits. He didn't go any further because he threw 103 pitches. But even more impressive was how he handled the heart of the Mets' order, as Carlos Beltran, Carlos Delgado and David Wright went a combined 2-for-9 with six strikeouts against the right-hander. The game plan was to mix his pitches against the trio.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer's season has been frustrating to him and the Cardinals. After it appeared that he was getting straightened out, he turned in two more disappointing starts his past two times out. Wellemeyer's mechanics remain a bit out of whack, and he's also given up more than his share of bloops, flares, rollers and the like for hits. He finally started missing bats in the last couple of innings on Sunday, an indication that maybe he found something.

home_pitcher_note: On Monday, the offense gave Martis a 6-2 lead after 4 1/2 innings against the Phillies. But the Phillies came back and tied the score in the bottom of the fifth. The bases were loaded when Ryan Howard drilled a 1-2 pitch for a grand slam to tie the score at 6-6. Martis pitched five-plus innings and gave up seven runs on eight hits.
away_pitcher_note: Statistically, it's been a very odd season for Pineiro. He has almost as many wins (four) as strikeouts (six), a ratio that it's just about impossible to keep up. Still, he's getting deep into games and throwing strikes, so as long as his defense keeps converting balls in play into outs, he has a chance to keep being effective. He really would do well to start getting at least a few strikeouts here and there, though.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse was scratched from his scheduled Sunday start even before the game was canceled due to rain. He is coming off six shutout innings against Atlanta on Tuesday, when the only real downside was four walks -- but three of those were semi-intentional to Chipper Jones. If the right-hander can pitch that well with a sore knee and a nasty stomach bug, think of what he'll be able to do if he's feeling good. He's been even better early in 2009 than he was in '08, and he'll be facing a team against which he pitched very well in '08, winning both his starts and giving up just one run in 12 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton has started four games, but is still looking for victory No. 1 of the 2009 regular season. The right-hander was ineffective in his last start against the Nationals, giving up eight hits and six earned runs in 4 1/3 innings. He threw 90 pitches, 51 for strikes, and served up three home runs -- two to Ryan Zimmerman and one to Elijah Dukes. Blanton's ERA spiked from 7.31 to 8.41. His command hasn't been consistent as evidenced by three walks and pitches being left up in the zone.

home_pitcher_note: It's hard to figure Wainwright. On one hand, he's only been really sharp in one start all year. On the other, he's gotten excellent results nearly every time, and the Cardinals have won his last four starts. He's capable of being simply outstanding, as he showed two starts ago against Chicago. He just hasn't been able to do that repeatedly this year. He'll have a tall task on Tuesday, facing a dangerous Phillies lineup.
away_pitcher_note: Myers is 1-2 with a 4.83 ERA, which makes him the most effective starter in the Phillies' rotation. That is not encouraging when speaking of the Phillies' rotation overall, but Myers has three successive quality starts and has not thrown fewer than six innings in any of his five starts this season. He also took a step forward Wednesday against Washington when he did not allow a home run for the first time this season.

home_pitcher_note: Just two starts into his 2009 Cardinals campaign, the rookie right-hander is already making a mighty big impression. After coming up from Triple-A Memphis on April 15 after former Cy Young Award winner Chris Carpenter went on the DL, Boggs made his first start against the Cubs April 26, allowing one unearned run in 5 2/3 innings and getting the nod from manager Tony La Russa to make at least one more start. He closed out the team's 16-7 April by striking out a career-high nine batters over six innings in an April 30 no-decision against Washington in an outing La Russa termed "outstanding."
away_pitcher_note: Duke has now made five starts in 2009 and four of them have been absolutely outstanding. Throw out the six-run outing against Atlanta on April 19 and the left-hander has given up just three earned runs over 30 2/3 innings in those four starts. That's an ERA of 0.88. Duke made three starts against the Brewers in 2008, losing one and finishing with a 5.87 ERA as he allowed 20 hits over 15 1/3 innings. This will be his 13th career start against Milwaukee and he'll look to improve on his 4.70 ERA against the NL Central rivals.

home_pitcher_note: No one is happier to celebrate the merry month of May than Wellemeyer, who rebounded from a 6.14 ERA in six April starts to get the win on May 1 with seven strong innings of work against Washington. Last year, Wellemeyer was the National League's Pitcher of the Month for May with a 4-0 record and 2.19 ERA. The Cards would be happy to see him replicate that stint, but are happy enough to have gotten the quality start and seen his consistency improve in this last outing.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf has four quality starts in five outings this season, a clear sign of how consistent he's been so far. He continues to focus on his early game tempo and rhythm, making sure not to start too slow, which he had been doing early in the season. A poor early tempo often leads to a lack of aggressiveness for Ohlendorf as the outing progresses. Still, he continues to show good control of his sinker and is working his off-speed pitches off of it. Ohlendorf lost in a pitchers' duel to the Cardinals earlier this year when he allowed two earned runs on seven hits in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto has been on some kind of roll lately. His career-high eight scoreless innings was the driving force behind a 5-0 shutout of the Pirates on Sunday at PNC Park. No Pirates hitters reached second base against Cueto, who gave up just four singles and a walk. He was one shy of a career high with nine strikeouts. Over his last three games, totaling 22 innings, the 23-year-old has given up one run and 15 hits. He's allowed no more than one walk in any of those starts.
away_pitcher_note: Though he suffered his first loss of the season after four wins, his May 2 outing against Washington was an overall success for Pineiro. He delivered seven strong innings, and while he gave up four runs, only one was earned, as he had his offspeed stuff working and was inducing mostly grounders. He walked just one and struck out a season-high four.

home_pitcher_note: Harang believed he tried to be too fine with his pitches last season, putting an inordinate amount of pressure on himself, and that's what led to a very forgettable and disappointing 2008 for him. From the ashes of that 6-17 season, he says he's back to just being himself, which appears very good news for the Reds. After a seven-inning, two-run effort in a no-decision against the Marlins on Monday night, Harang's earned run average sits at a highly respectable 3.00. He tied a season high with nine strikeouts against the Marlins in a game that wound up going 14 innings. Harang still is likely to be tested by the offensively explosive Cardinals in Cincinnati's hitter-friendly ballpark, but at the least he will enter the game feeling that all of his pitches are working and he has good command of them.
away_pitcher_note: Two ugly innings turned Lohse's ERA from spectacular to merely very good, but he's still having a fine season. He appeared to be affected in his last start by being hit on the left elbow while he was batting. He doesn't expect that to have any impact on his next start, however. Overall, Lohse has not fared as well on the road as a Cardinal as he has at Busch Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez has discovered that he can do more with less. Less speed, that is. The right-hander can reach 97 mph on the radar gun, but he often doesn't know where the ball is going. Manager Dusty Baker is convinced Volquez can achieve more with a 91-92 mph fastball that still moves and he can locate and save the most intense heat for selected situations. Volquez has been arguably the most difficult Major Leaguer for hitters to solve over his past three starts. He's allowed just five hits in his past 21 innings and no runs in his past two starts, covering 16 innings. His most recent effort resulted in a 7-0 victory over the Marlins on Tuesday. He struck out seven and yielded three hits. Of his 97 pitches, 60 went for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright's pattern of putting runners on base finally caught up to him in his last start, when he was knocked around for seven runs by the Phillies. He insists that he'll use the defeat as something of a wake-up call and get things sorted out quickly. Still, he's only really pitched up to his high standards once in six starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Duke wasn't at his sharpest his last time out, but with the way the left-hander has started the season, there's no reason to believe that he won't be just fine when he takes the mound on Tuesday. As has been noted since the start of Spring Training, Duke is very much a different pitcher this season, both mentally and with his command, and he's done a superb job at avoiding the big inning, which constantly plagued him last year. When he's getting groundballs with ease, that's when you know Duke is on.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer's ERA is headed in the right direction. He allowed just two earned runs on four hits in seven innings in a 5-2 victory Thursday afternoon over Pittsburgh, dropping his ERA to 4.75 from a season high of 6.14 just two starts prior. Wellemeyer was the National League's Pitcher of the Month for May in 2008 with a 4-0 record and 2.19 ERA. The Cards would be happy to see him replicate that stint, but are happy enough to have gotten the quality start and seen his consistency improve in his past two outings.

home_pitcher_note: One bad inning did Ohlendorf in his last time out, and again, it has to do with his tempo. The Pirates have been trying to emphasize to Ohlendorf the need to take less time in between pitches and when he does, he seems to be sharp. However, Ohlendorf often falls into a trap, usually early in the game, where his tempo slows. His control suffers as a result. Still, he's been fairly consistent all season and has rebounded from hiccups like he had his last time out pretty well.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro, who entered Friday's game 3-0 with a 2.22 ERA in four career starts vs. Cincinnati, allowed five runs, four earned, on eight hits in six innings. All of the runs and seven of the hits came in the first two innings. Pineiro recovered to retire 11 of the last 12 batters he faced. He struck out three and did not walk a batter in a 96-pitch outing.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens matched his season high with a six-inning outing his last time out. The right-hander's efficiency was much better than it had been in his previous two starts and he was able to not fall behind so often, which had been an issue in April. Karstens also kept the ball in the park, an achievement considering that he had given up five home runs in his first four starts. The right-hander hasn't been dominant at all this season, but he has shown flashes of being a capable fifth starter in the rotation when he establishes his command early. Karstens has never faced the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Boggs will be making his fifth start this season. He allowed two runs  on five hits in 4 1/3 innings Wednesday in a 5-2 win over the Pirates. The rookie right-hander has made a mighty big impression. After coming up from Triple-A Memphis on April 15 after former Cy Young Award winner Chris Carpenter went on the disabled list, Boggs made his first start against the Cubs April 26, allowing one unearned run in 5 2/3 innings. He closed out the team's 16-7 April by striking out a career-high nine batters over six innings in an April 30 no-decision against Washington in an outing La Russa termed "outstanding."

home_pitcher_note: Lohse pitched well for five innings Friday night but was doomed by a five-run sixth at Cincinnati. The big blow was delivered by Reds pitcher Aaron Harang, who snapped an 0-for-13 skid with a two-run bases-loaded single. Lohse finished with seven earned runs allowed on nine hits in six innings. He walked three and struck out four. Overall, Lohse has not fared as well on the road as a Cardinal as he has at Busch Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo either struggled with his command or with home-plate umpire Jerry Crawford's postage stamp-sized strike zone on Saturday against the Cubs, but he limited the damage to two runs in five workmanlike innings and nearly didn't allow a run at all. Gallardo's pitch count hit 60 before he recorded the final out of the third inning, and he crossed the 100-pitch barrier in the fifth, but the righty was one out away from a scoreless outing when Micah Hoffpauir belted a two-run home run with two outs in the fifth. Gallardo has faced the Cardinals twice without much success; he allowed four runs in five innings of a no-decision at Busch Stadium and seven runs in 5 2/3 innings of his only outing against the Cards at Miller Park, a loss.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright did not have a strong outing against the Reds on Sunday, going six innings and allowing four runs on seven hits. Still, he was in line to get the win until the Cardinals' bullpen lost the lead in the ninth inning. Wainwrighht did have speed and control, though, walking only one and saying that he felt strong in the fifth and sixth innings. The best news is that Wainwright feels that he knows what went wrong. "It's not a question of arm strength or stuff -- the ball just isn't sinking the way it normally does, and I'm throwing fly balls," Wainwright said. "It's just a matter of arm slot -- so now that we recognize the problem, I should be able to correct it."
away_pitcher_note: Suppan will face his former teammates for the sixth time since leaving via free agency following the 2006 season. In five previous starts as a member of the Brewers against the Cardinals, Suppan is 4-0 with a 1.93 ERA -- having allowed eight earned runs in 37 1/3 innings -- and he's 6-2 with a 3.18 ERA in 11 career appearances against St. Louis. Suppan is coming off his first loss since April 12, a 4-2 decision against the Cubs at Miller Park in which he surrendered all four runs, only three earned, in the fourth inning. Alfonso Soriano hit a two-run home run to tie the game, and that has been a problem for Suppan; he has allowed at least one homer in six of his seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer has been a puzzle this year, but one thing has been pretty much constant: He gets in trouble early. The first two innings have been a minefield for the right-hander, and he needs to navigate them more successfully. When he can do that, he can often fashion a pretty good game. But too many times, he's dug himself too deep a hole to be able to dig out.
away_pitcher_note: After losing his first four decisions, Parra suddenly has suddenly won two starts in a row. He beat the Marlins in Milwaukee on Tuesday despite a rocky first two innings, in which he hit one batter, walked another and surrendered three two-out, run-scoring singles. He settled down after that, allowing only one more hit through the end of the sixth and recording six of his final nine outs via strikeout. Parra finished with eight whiffs, matching his season high, and put together a "quality start" (defined as six or more innings with three or fewer earned runs) for the third consecutive outing. He's pitched against the Cardinals six times in his career, including five starts, and has pitched well, to the tune of a 3.77 ERA, but he has yet to record a decision against St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse finally had a game where no physical ailments plagued him. So instead, a massive rainstorm washed out what was looking like a nice start after just two innings. The Cubs aren't the best matchup for him, but he tends to pitch well at home, and the rainout left the Cardinals scrambling to sort out how their rotation will work out. Lohse will pitch on two days' rest, treating the Friday night game essentially as a bullpen session.
away_pitcher_note: This was originally an off-day, but a rainout Friday night that was re-scheduled for Monday prompted manager Ken Macha to shuffle the deck. He could have used Yovani Gallardo, but instead bumped up Braden Looper to start against his former team. He'll be on regular rest coming off a "salvage" start against the Marlins last week. The first four Marlins hitters went single, homer, double, single for a 3-0 lead before Looper had his first out, but he settled down after that and allowed only two more runs through the sixth to snap a personal two-game losing streak.

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro puts a great deal in the hands of his defense when he pitches, which means he needs them to make plays. They didn't make enough in his last game, and so he ended up allowing five runs. If they catch the ball behind him, turn the double plays and get the job done, he can be quite effective. If not, it can be a long night. Pineiro also tends to benefit greatly from pitching at Busch Stadium, where the spacious dimensions help him out.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly served up eight hits over 6 1/3 innings in his last start against the Padres, including two home runs by Adrian Gonzalez. That was the only damage against the lefty, who did not walk a batter and struck out seven. Lilly won his third straight start. He was 3-0 with a 3.06 ERA against the Cardinals last season. Lilly is ahead of last year's pace; he didn't win his fifth game then until his 10th game. He is now 3-1 with a 1.29 ERA at home with 27 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: This is a very big deal for St. Louis, getting its ace and former Cy Young winner back after he was on the shelf for five weeks. Carpenter was outstanding in both of his starts before he was felled by a left oblique strain. If he's even close to his ideal level of sharpness and strength, he'll help the Cardinals tremendously. Carpenter will likely be on a fairly tight pitch count in his first start, but he's capable of making a tight pitch count last quite a few innings.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster had thrown 121 pitches in his start prior to May 14 vs. the Padres, but showed no wear and tear. Against San Diego, he went seven innings, gave up two runs on three hits and struck out five. He picked up the win, and seems to be in a better groove. He has thrown six or more innings in each of his starts this year, and recorded four quality starts. He did not get a decision in back to back outings vs. the Cardinals last month.

home_pitcher_note: It appears that Wainwright is back. Despite taking a loss, he was brilliant in his last start, throwing eight innings of two-hit, one-run ball. He threw strikes, but more than that, he threw quality strikes. Wainwright believes he has fixed a delivery flaw that had his arm slot too high. He's also back to relying more heavily on his sinking fastball. The combination added up to an excellent game on Saturday, and it should continue to do so as he goes forward.
away_pitcher_note: Marshall was assigned to the bullpen over the weekend just in case another lefty was needed. He missed a turn in the rotation when last Friday's game against the Astros was rained out. This will be his sixth start of the year. In his last start May 10, he gave up two runs on five hits over five innings against the Brewers. He has thrown six or more innings in three of his five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer's struggles remain a puzzling problem for the Cardinals, who were counting on him to follow up his breakout 2008 with another good year. Instead, he's scuffled nearly all season, turning in only three really good starts in eight opportunities. The truly vexing thing is that it's been a variety of issues. Sometimes selection, sometimes command, sometimes stuff. He just hasn't put it all together, and he needs to start doing so.
away_pitcher_note: Davies got in manager Trey Hillman's doghouse by throwing too many fastballs in all the wrong places in the first inning last Saturday night against the Orioles. Davies allowed just one run in the inning, made the necessary adjustments and pleased Hillman by getting through seven innings. But he lost, 3-2, and tied a career high by throwing 119 pitches. Davies' problem this season has been inconsistency; he can't seem to put good starts back-to-back. Formerly with the Braves, oddly enough Davies didn't face the Cardinals until last year with the Royals. He split two decisions and had a 2.70 ERA in the two starts.
summary: 2009-05-22 - Kansas City Royals (0) @ St. Louis Cardinals (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Manager Tony La Russa blamed himself for Lohse's subpar start against the Brewers, and he may not be all wrong. Lohse just didn't have much, but it was understandable. He was starting three days after his previous outing, which was washed out after two innings due to rain. He ought to be much more successful on Saturday against Kansas City, pitching on a normal schedule with normal rest.
away_pitcher_note: After a superlative stay at Triple-A Omaha (5-0, 0.90 ERA), Hochevar has found rough sledding in his return to the Majors. He lasted just two innings in his first start at Oakland. In his next outing, last Sunday against Baltimore, he made it just 3 1/3 innings before being pulled. His problem was control. In that brief outing, he labored through 70 pitches and only 34 of them were strikes. He walked three, hit one and allowed a run-scoring wild pitch. Hochevar needs to return to his Triple-A style of throwing strikes and keeping his pitches low in the zone.
summary: 2009-05-23 - Kansas City Royals (0) @ St. Louis Cardinals (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Coming off one of the finest games of his career, Pineiro will be looking for a repeat. He benefits greatly from pitching at Busch Stadium, so that increases his chances. And if manager Tony La Russa once again backs him with a defense-oriented lineup, as he did on Tuesday, that will help as well. Pineiro is getting a ton of balls in play -- he's not striking out or walking many batters at all -- so a lot comes down to the defense behind him. When the Cardinals catch the ball, he'll be effective.
away_pitcher_note: Bannister, after giving up five runs in six innings against the Indians on Tuesday night, seemed headed for his second loss. Lo and behold, the Royals rallied in the ninth to win, 6-5. Bannister felt he left his team down but it wasn't like he was horrible. His biggest mistake was a home run pitch to Kelly Shoppach in a three-run sixth. Since returning from Omaha, Bannister has been a solid performer. In his previous start, he came out with a stiff shoulder but there was no apparent recurrence this time. Bannister faced the Cardinals twice last season, going 1-1 but with a 6.94 ERA.
summary: 2009-05-24 - Kansas City Royals (3) @ St. Louis Cardinals (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Because of a rainout in St. Louis, Gallardo threw only 30 pitches in the 10 days prior to his most recent start, and it showed. He struggled to corral his fastball through a five-plus inning stint in Houston and surrendered six earned runs, the most he'd allowed since an awful start against the Reds back on April 13. In his five starts after the Cincinnati outing Gallardo was 3-0 with a 1.80 ERA and a complete game, but he came back to Earth against the Astros and surrendered seven hits including Miguel Tejada's home run, plus a pair of walks. He actually pitched 1 1/3 innings against the Cardinals on May 15 and surrendered a two-run homer to Colby Rasmus, but those stats were washed away by the rain so this is his official season debut against St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter once again amazed with his ability to be sharp upon returning from injury. Now he'll try to make it two healthy starts in a row. There's no question about his effectiveness if he can avoid injury. Held to a pitch count of somewhere around 70-80 in his first game back from an oblique strain (he was removed after 67), chances are he'll have a longer leash next time out. Somewhere in the neighborhood of 80-90 pitches is a good guess, and when Carpenter is going well, he can make that many pitches cover plenty of innings.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan limited the damage on a shaky night in Houston on Thursday but was burned by a couple of home runs. Hunter Pence's two-run shot in the second inning and Miguel Tejada's solo shot in the fourth accounted for all the damage against Suppan, who matched Dave Bush in allowing a team-high nine homers this season. Still, Suppan has been steady, holding opponents to three or fewer runs in each of his last seven starts, including a gem in St. Louis on May 16 in which Suppan surrendered six hits but no runs in a 1-0 win. He pitched for the Cardinals from 2004-06, and in six starts against them since he signed a four-year, $42 million deal with the Brewers, Suppan is 5-0 with a 1.66 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: It took the Cardinals' Opening Day starter a while to find his groove, but he has assuredly found it with back-to-back outstanding starts. He has adjusted his arm slot, refined his command and maintained his excellent stuff. Moreover, he is back to relying on his fastball. There are few better starters in the National League than a healthy, rolling Wainwright, and the Cardinals are reaping the benefits right now.

home_pitcher_note: Parra appeared to have turned the corner after a difficult April in which he was 0-4 with a 6.52 ERA in four starts. Entering Friday's game against the Twins, Parra was 3-0 with a 3.00 ERA in four May starts and 3-1 with a 2.79 ERA in five starts since April 26. Parra's May resurgence hit a major snag on Friday, when he allowed nine runs -- eight earned -- on eight hits and three walks in 3 1/3 innings. The left-hander will look to right the ship immediately on Wednesday against the Cardinals. Parra has been successful against the Cardinals in his career, going 1-0 with a 3.63 ERA in six starts and one relief appearance over 34 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer has shown signs of progress a couple of times already this year, and he did so again his last time out. The key is not to take two steps back after a step forward. Wellemeyer insists that as much as anything, he needs to get out of his own head and stop thinking so much about his delivery. He also needs to have all of his pitches available to throw for strikes from the start of a game. When he's able to mix in his slider and changeup along with his fastball, Wellemeyer is much more effective.

home_pitcher_note: Cain will be working with an extra day's rest, which he won't need. He has maintained his strength throughout the season, lasting at least six innings in each of his nine starts -- including a complete game last Saturday at Seattle. Cain has thrived with runners in scoring position, limiting opponents to a .100 average (4-for-40) in those situations. He has faced St. Louis just twice in his career, losing his lone decision and posting a 9.58 ERA against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: The story remains the same for Pineiro. When his defense makes plays behind him, he thrives. When it doesn't catch the ball for him, he has a hard time winning. In his last outing, two plays that might have been made, weren't. And although they weren't errors, it was enough to sink him and the Redbirds. According to baseball-reference.com, he could become the first pitcher since Greg Maddux in 1995 to have five straight starts without allowing a walk or a home run.
summary: 2009-05-29 - St. Louis Cardinals (2) @ San Francisco Giants (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Zito's stretch of stingy performances ended last Sunday at Seattle, where he yielded five runs in 6 1/3 innings as the Giants lost, 5-4. Ken Griffey Jr.'s two-run homer in the first inning and Adrian Beltre's three-run drive in the fifth did in Zito, who has allowed six home runs this season and four in his last two starts. Zito has endured rough times against the Cardinals, posting an 0-2 mark with a 4.80 ERA and 22 hits allowed in 15 innings spanning three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Few stories in baseball this year have been more impressive than that of Carpenter, who has already twice returned in magnificent form from injury. He began the year with two excellent starts after missing nearly all of 2007 and 2008 with elbow and shoulder issues. After a return to the DL with a left oblique strain, he pitched two more brilliant games. He's looking to make it five starts without allowing an earned run, a stat that pretty much says it all.
summary: 2009-05-30 - St. Louis Cardinals (6) @ San Francisco Giants (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Jonathan Sanchez opened his eighth start of the season at home Monday with five scoreless innings against the Atlanta Braves, but he was pulled from the game before retiring a batter in the sixth. He was charged with two earned runs and struck out six. Sanchez has fared well at AT&T Park this season, posting an ERA of 2.42. In eight career innings against the Cardinals, the left-hander hasn't allowed a run and is 2-0.
away_pitcher_note: Another sign that Wainwright is back: even when he was a little off in his last start, he was still very, very effective. It's three straight excellent starts for the big righty, and he's a critical part of the Redbirds' rotation. He's throwing strikes, and he's getting swings and misses. In Wainwright's last start, he struck out a career-high nine. In his last three starts, he has 23 Ks. And now he faces a low-wattage offense in a pitcher-friendly ballpark. It could be a fun day for Wainwright.
summary: 2009-05-31 - St. Louis Cardinals (3) @ San Francisco Giants (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: This start remains written in pencil, rather than pen, as it's still unclear exactly when Kyle Lohse will slot back into the St. Louis rotation. But for now, figure Wellemeyer on Monday with Lohse simply missing a turn and returning after the rest of the Redbirds pitch following Thursday's off day. That means that Wellemeyer, who has two solid starts in a row, would be going for a third at home against Cincinnati. He has yet to assemble three straight good starts this year, so keep an eye on this one to see whether he's truly turned a corner.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez will be activated from the disabled list to make the start vs. the Cardinals. On May 16 at San Diego, the right-hander left his previous start early because of back spasms and later went on the DL when he was unable to make his next turn in the rotation. On Wednesday, Volquez had a successful bullpen session where he declared himself pain-free while able to throw all of his pitches. "I think I'm ready to go right now," Volquez said after the session.

home_pitcher_note: Thompson, the Cardinals' do-everything pitcher, once again gets a tough assignment. The right-hander has not appeared in a game since May 17, yet he'll get the call to start against Cincinnati on Tuesday due to Joel Pineiro's back spasms. Thompson was starting at Triple-A Memphis in late April, but since his recall from the Minors, he has faced all of 31 batters in 29 days. For his career, the Cardinals are 17-7 when Thompson starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his first complete game of the season and seventh of his career, Arroyo gave up five hits -- four singles and a double -- with one walk and three strikeouts for an easy 6-1 win over the Astros on Wednesday. He had only 79 pitches through eight innings and finished with 92 pitches. In the start before that vs. Cleveland, he gave up one earned run over eight innings. Arroyo has yet to get a no-decision. He's figured in the outcome of all 10 of his starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse finally returns after being pushed back twice due to soreness in his right forearm. In his last start, on May 23, he was lifted after eight innings because he was hit on the right forearm by a pitch. Since then, Lohse cut short two bullpen sessions, and thus twice had his return postponed. But he successfully threw a side session on Sunday, getting on track to start on Wednesday against Cincinnati.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto gave up three earned runs on only three hits over seven innings, but two of the hits were home runs in a 3-2 loss to the Brewers on Friday. The right-hander was erratic early with all four of his walks over the first two innings. After a two-out, four-pitch walk in the Milwaukee first inning, Prince Fielder hit a two-run home run. Cueto later retired 13 of 14 batters until a hanging slider to Corey Hart went for the game-losing home run. Cueto has definitely been a model of consistency overall, however, having pitched seven innings over his last eight outings in a row.

home_pitcher_note: The Cardinals' ace finally gave up an earned run on Saturday, but he was still outstanding. It's a tribute to how good Carpenter has been that his line against the Giants -- six innings, two runs, five strikeouts, one walk -- was a step back. Carpenter for the most part has looked as good as ever this year, with vintage stuff and command as well as his imposing mound presence.
away_pitcher_note: In a 9-5 loss to the Brewers on Saturday, Harang had eight earned runs and 12 hits allowed -- including three home runs -- over 4 1/3 innings pitched, with five strikeouts. His fastball was his only quality pitch, and once he established that he had no off-speed command, the Brewers jumped all over him. Over his past two starts, Harang has allowed 11 earned runs, 22 hits and four homers over just 9 1/3 innings. On May 9 vs. the Cardinals at Great American Ball Park, the right-hander gave up three runs (two earned) and seven hits over seven innings for an 8-3 victory.

home_pitcher_note: After three consecutive superb outings, Wainwright was merely pretty good his last time out, and that won't sit well with him. One of Wainwright's best attributes is his unwillingness to settle for anything short of outstanding. Wainwright has pitched at least seven innings in four consecutive starts, and after issuing 18 walks in his first five games, he has handed out only 10 free passes in his past six.
away_pitcher_note: Interim manager Jim Tracy said De La Rosa is as talented as any starter on the squad but that he lacks one attribute -- the ability to get out of trouble. That was lacking again in his last start as he allowed a three-run homer on a 0-2 fastball with two outs to Padres slugger Adrian Gonzalez. De La Rosa pitched five innings and gave up four runs, but it could have been worse if Gonzalez wasn't gunned down at the plate to end the fifth.

home_pitcher_note: Monday brought another frustrating start for Wellemeyer, who just can't seem to build any momentum. He has yet to string together three consecutive good starts, and that's discouraging not only to him but to a team that was hoping he'd build on an excellent 2008 season. He does seem to have conquered the early-innings problem he had in April and part of May. Now, he just needs to do a better job of keeping it together when things start to turn against him.
away_pitcher_note: In a 4-1 loss at Houston in his last start, Cook kept the Rockies close until the sixth inning, when Carlos Lee lined a sinker over the left-field wall for a big two-run homer. Cook's best inning may have been the fourth, when he gave up just one run with runners on first and third and no outs. All but one of the outs in play and many of the nine hits were on the ground.

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro was scratched from his Tuesday start due to back spasms, but the Cardinals continue to hope that he'll miss only one appearance. That would put him on track to slot back into the rotation on Sunday at home against Colorado, and pitching at home tends to be a very good thing for Pineiro. He has a 2.05 ERA at Busch Stadium this year (5.45 on the road), and he's 9-3 with a 3.34 ERA at home since joining the Cardinals at the non-waiver Trade Deadline in 2007.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez went six innings in the Rockies' 3-2, 11-inning loss to the Astros on Tuesday night. It wasn't the easiest time on the mound, as Jimenez pitched around seven hits and four walks but forced 11 ground-ball outs. Included were two double plays. It wasn't the most efficient performance (112 pitches), but Jimenez's resourcefulness is one reason he is considered an up-and-coming star. The Cards know about him. Manager Tony La Russa was highly complimentary of him after he had a strong performance for the Dominican Republic against the Cards during a World Baseball Classic exhibition game.

home_pitcher_note: This would be Kyle Lohse's turn in the rotation, but Lohse was placed on the disabled list after he aggravated a right forearm injury on Wednesday night. Thompson will be almost exactly on turn, with five days' rest after he filled in for Joel Pineiro, who had back spasms. The Cardinals are 18-7 when Thompson starts a game.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis has to be happy not to be facing the Astros. In his start on Wednesday night, he gave up three first-inning runs, mostly on soft hits, settled down for five scoreless innings, then gave up two in the seventh. One run in the seventh was on a leadoff homer by Hunter Pence, who dominates Marquis (11-for-22). But the homer was a hanging slider that any good hitter should have a good chance at, and that's the kind of pitch Marquis was kicking himself for throwing. A onetime Cardinal, Marquis is 4-2 with a 3.99 ERA in eight games against the Cards but gave up five runs in 5 2/3 innings while losing his lone start against them last year.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson was impressive in his last outing holding the Brewers to two runs on five hits over 7 2/3 innings while striking out eight. The power pitcher was always a power hitter taking a Dave Bush pitch out for a three-run homer. Johnson has had one start against the Cardinals in his career.  In September 2008, he allowed three runs on seven hits over 6 2/3 innings. Albert Pujols, Ryan Ludwick and Rick ankiel are a combined 2-for-8 with a home run against Johnson.
away_pitcher_note: After dominating hitters in some of his earlier starts, Carpenter resorted to frustrating them his last time out. He can do nearly anything, be it racking up a high strikeout total and overwhelming his opponent, or pounding the bottom of the strike zone to induce a steady stream of ground balls. Nobody in the National League is pitching better than Carpenter, who has a ridiculous 0.71 ERA and is averaging fewer than 13 pitches per inning.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad had another quality start, allowing two runs over six innings, but made one mistake in his last outing and it was a costly one. The right-hander gave up a two-run homer to Pablo Sandoval that gave Volstad his fifth loss of the year. He has surrendered 64 hits on the year with 12 being long balls. Despite a losing record, the 22-year old has pitched well in 2009 going six or more innings in nine straight starts and 10 of his 12 this season. Volstad has faced the Cardinals once in his career, allowing three runs over five innings while picking up the win on Aug. 12, 2008.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright's efficiency was down and his walks were up in his last time out, but he was still very good. That's been a hallmark of his this season, that even when he's not extremely sharp he can be quite effective. But mostly, he's been plenty sharp for the past four weeks or so. Since the start of May, Wainwright has 42 strikeouts and 13 walks in 48 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Miller threw four innings of perfect baseball before the Giants were able to figure him out. The left-hander pitched well, allowing two runs (one earned) on four hits over 5 2/3 innings while striking out five. Miller found trouble in the fifth and sixth innings and was lifted with the bases loaded and two outs in the sixth, but the 24-year-old still managed to have a solid outing and pick up his second victory of the season. He's started against the Cardinals once before and won. Miller threw six shutout innings in an Interleague game against the Redbirds on May 18, 2007.
away_pitcher_note: So often, Wellemeyer finds himself one pitch away. So often, he can't make that one pitch. Wellemeyer has surrendered big innings again and again, turning otherwise fine games into disappointments. If he can pitch with runners on base as well as he does with the bases empty, he'll be just fine. It's actually making that adjustment that's the trick.

home_pitcher_note: Huff earned his first career Major League win in Chicago on Sunday by grinding through five innings in which he held the White Sox to three runs on four hits with three walks and three strikeouts. He worked his way out of several jams. The damage came on a three-run homer from Alexei Ramirez in the fifth. Huff, one of the more highly touted arms in the Indians' farm system at the start of the year, has shown continual improvement in his five Major League starts, and he finally has a win to show for it.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro's last start was a great example of the perils facing pitchers who allow lots of balls in play. He was beaten by a string of singles, one ball after another that found a hole. When the defense catches the ball behind him, he tends to have a good night. When those balls in play don't turn into outs, things can get ugly.

home_pitcher_note: Ohka is taking over the rotation spot that opened up when the Indians optioned Fausto Carmona to rookie ball. How long Ohka holds this spot will depend on his performance. He has given up six runs on 11 hits in 10 innings over two appearances of long relief work, both of which came on days Carmona started. Ohka hasn't started a Major League game since June 6, 2007, while with the Blue Jays. He is 3-4 with a 5.74 ERA in seven career appearances against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Thompson found a quick hook waiting for him in his last start, but ultimately fared pretty well and he's likely to get another chance to fill in for Kyle Lohse. At this point, the right-hander is what he is. When he keeps his sinking fastball down and throws strikes, he's effective. When he leaves the sinker up and/or misses the strike zone, he gets in trouble. Thompson can be very efficient when he's pitching well.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander gave up four runs in six innings against the Royals, but pitched better than his line showed. A sloppy sixth inning in which K.C. scored two runs thanks in part to two infield hits and a throwing error by catcher Kelly Shoppach didn't help his cause. As he has for most of the season, Lee did what every starter hopes to do -- keep his team in the game. The Indians rallied for eight runs in the sixth and seventh innings to pull out a win, even though Lee didn't figure in the decision. He threw 105 pitches, the 12th time in his last 13 starts he has topped the 100-pitch mark. Lee threw 98 pitches against the Reds on May 24, the only time he hasn't topped 100 in that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Tuesday's game against the Marlins offered a bit of a rarity for the Cardinals -- their ace, Carpenter, was spotted a three-run lead, and the club still lost. The 34-year-old, who came in with a 0.71 ERA -- a franchise low spanning the first six starts of the season -- gave up three runs in six innings to get a no-decision, walking one while striking out three and surrendering six hits. The three runs allowed, however, came on a two-run blooper to left field and a two-out infield single off Carpenter's glove -- both by Emilio Bonifacio. He ended up throwing 89 pitches (59 strikes). For his career, Carpenter is 2-2 with a 5.96 ERA in nine games (seven starts) against the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright got some nice run support and was victorious against the Marlins on Wednesday despite throwing 121 pitches (75 strikes) -- his highest mark since April 26, 2008. Wainwright gave up four runs on 11 hits while walking three and striking out four to help St. Louis snap its five-game losing streak. It was the 27-year-old's sixth straight decision -- a stretch that has him 3-3 with a 2.68 ERA. Wainwright gave up a run in two innings during his only career appearance against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Wednesday's complete-game victory over the White Sox continued the Detroit ace's roll through opposing hitters over the past month and a half. His 7-0 record and 1.10 ERA over his past nine starts is the best stretch by a Tigers starter since Doyle Alexander in 1987. His 81 strikeouts in that stretch gave him 106 over 13 starts this season, making him the quickest Tigers starter to fan 100 since Mickey Lolich in 1969. Now it's the National League's turn to face him, which has never been a fair challenge -- he's 8-0 with a 2.30 ERA over 10 career starts in Interleague Play.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer's fastball hovered in the 90-91 mph range in his last game, against the Marlins. That's about five mph slower than he was accustomed to averaging last season. Add the fact that Wellemeyer had significant trouble against the Marlins and you have a situation worth monitoring, in the least. Wellemeyer struck out just one Marlin in six innings and gave up five runs and 11 hits. The little-used Ross Gload got to him for two home runs, accounting for three runs. But Wellemeyer came away thinking he kept the damage to a minimum, especially considering his velocity woes. The Tigers, with a better-than-average offense, figure to be a significant test for him.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson's no-decision Thursday against the White Sox ended his string of quality starts at six over the past month, but it also showed another sign of progress from previous inconsistencies in Tampa Bay. His struggles getting into sync and Chicago hitters' patience cost him 99 pitches over five innings, but with two runs allowed, he avoided the kind of big innings that plagued him in years past. He's 1-3 with a 6.80 ERA over 13 games in Interleague Play, nine of them starts.

home_pitcher_note: Quietly, Pineiro continues to turn in one solid start after another. His strikeout totals are coming up a bit, while his walk and home run numbers stay down. That's a formula for success, one that's worked very well for Pineiro thus far in 2009. Another thing that's worked well is pitching at home, which he will do on Thursday. Pineiro has a 2.52 ERA at Busch Stadium in 2009 (5.27 on the road).
away_pitcher_note: Porcello gets another chance to help his own cause at the plate after becoming the first Tigers pitcher since 1972 to drive in multiple runs in a game Friday at Pittsburgh. More important were his seven innings of one-run ball in 99 pitches, showing some efficient execution for a 20-year-old.

home_pitcher_note: Davies wasn't spectacular in his last start, but he didn't need to be, and the Kansas City right-hander earned a much-needed win. Davies threw five innings against the Reds and allowed three runs on two hits. But Davies' command gave him fits at times. He walked five batters and struck out one. Davies hadn't picked up a win since April 30 at Toronto, and the victory snapped a five-game losing streak. But Davies has been better than his record indicates. He pitched seven innings and gave up three runs in a loss at Baltimore on May 16, and he allowed two earned runs in six innings in a loss at St. Louis on May 22.
away_pitcher_note: The equation has been pretty simple over the years: when Thompson starts, the Cardinals win. In his 27 career big league starts, the Cards are 19-8. Thompson jokes that it's because his teammates know they have to bring the big bats when he pitches, but nonetheless he does prefer starting and at times has done it very well. He's coming off an excellent game in Cleveland and will once again pitch on the road in Interleague Play, adding the challenge of a designated hitter to the opposing lineup.
summary: 2009-06-19 - St. Louis Cardinals (10) @ Kansas City Royals (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Bannister tossed up another solid outing in his last start. The Royals right-hander threw eight innings and allowed just one run on four hits against the Reds. It was Bannister's fifth quality start of the season, and the loss snapped a string of three straight  starts without a victory. Bannister struck out four and allowed just five baserunners. He improved to 6-3 in Interleague Play in his career, and he's already posted one victory against the Cardinals this season. Bannister lasted six innings and allowed two runs in a 3-2 victory on May 24 in St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: After considering going with Carpenter on regular rest on Friday, the Cardinals elected to use Monday's off-day to give him and Adam Wainwright a little breather. So both right-handers will pitch on five days' rest over the weekend in Kansas City. Carpenter is coming off a fine game in which a couple of mistakes cost him a loss. His record in Interleague road games since coming to St. Louis is spotty.
summary: 2009-06-20 - St. Louis Cardinals (7) @ Kansas City Royals (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Meche withstood the 85-degree heat and the Diamondbacks very nicely last Tuesday night as he pitched a complete-game 5-0 victory. He finished with a career-high 132 pitches, including 22 in the ninth inning, and firmly put to rest earlier concerns over his cranky back and his flagging stamina. Meche gave up just four hits and walked two, extending a personal shutout streak to 16 innings. In Interleague play, Meche has a 14-4 record. He didn't face the Cardinals this year in St. Louis, but he beat them, 7-2, last year at Kauffman Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: After a three-start lull, Wainwright looked like himself once again his last time out. The Cardinals would love to see him keep it up for a while. One thing they can count on from Wainwright is innings. Wainwright has gone at least six innings in 12 consecutive starts, and he's lasted seven or more in six of his last seven. The Cardinals are 9-5 in his starts. However, his ERA is 4.38 on the road, versus 2.55 at home.
summary: 2009-06-21 - St. Louis Cardinals (12) @ Kansas City Royals (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Despite allowing baserunners in every inning and serving up Matt Wieters' first career home run, Redding escaped with a no-decision in 5 1/3 innings last Wednesday in Baltimore. It was the worst outing of the month for a pitcher who had produced a 2.77 ERA in his previous two starts. Redding's next outing comes against the Cardinals, a team that tagged him for six runs in 5 2/3 innings in a start last season. Redding hasn't beaten the Cardinals since 2004.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer, in dire need of a good showing, got one his last time out. Now the trick is doing it again. It's not like he's been awful all year. He's put together a good start or two here and there throughout the season. What he hasn't been able to do is sustain it. If he can limit the damage in potential big innings like he did against Detroit on Wednesday, that's an excellent first step.
summary: 2009-06-22 - St. Louis Cardinals (4) @ New York Mets (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez he would have beaten the Orioles last Thursday if not for a blown save, and he still has not lost any of his last 10 starts, dating back to April 23 -- and that from a pitcher who wasn't even projected to make the Opening Day rotation. He is not walking batters -- just 2.5 per nine innings -- and he is stranding men on base. With runners in scoring position, opponents are batting just .183 off Hernandez this season. He'll look to continue that trend against the Cardinals, a team that thumped him for seven runs in 4 1/3 innings earlier this year.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro retired 16 straight Tigers on Thursday after giving up four runs in the first inning. He then fell to the ground in pain after striking out Josh Anderson to end the seventh and had to be carried from the field with cramps. Only one of his four runs were earned, and he took the tough-luck loss, sayhing that he was just a little dehydrated and would be fine for his start in New York. Pineiro has lost five straight starts and eight of his last nine after starting the season 4-0.
summary: 2009-06-23 - St. Louis Cardinals (3) @ New York Mets (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Nieve proved his first outing of the season-a 6-2 victory over the Yankees-was no fluke by shutting down the Rays for six innings on Friday. Nieve allowed just one run on three hits while striking out four to get his second win in as many starts. In that time, he has given up just seven hits in 12 2/3 innings. Nieve has never started against the Cardinals, posting a 5.79 ERA in three career relief appearances against St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: Thompson wasn't unhittable in his last start against the Royals, but thanks to a wave of run support from the Cardinals' offense, Thompson earned his second win of the year. And at times, Thompson was pretty good. After giving up a leadoff homer in the first, Thompson allowed just one run through the next five innings. He gave up another homer in the seventh and left after allowing four runs and five hits in seven innings. It was good enough for the Cardinals, and it may be good enough to give Thompson, who has spent a portion of 2009 in the bullpen, a few more opportunities to start.
summary: 2009-06-24 - St. Louis Cardinals (0) @ New York Mets (11) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Santana rebounded from one of the worst performances of his career with his longest outing of the season against the Rays on Saturday. Santana allowed just two runs on three hits in 7 1/3 innings, but a Carlos Pena solo homer in the seventh was the game-winner in a rain-interrupted 3-1 Rays victory. Santana has now lost three of his last four starts after beginning the season 7-2. He has started against the Cardinals once in his career -- a complete game last July 27. Santana limited the Cardinals to a run on six hits in the 9-1 Mets win.
away_pitcher_note: Despite missing nearly a month with a strained rib cage muscle earlier this season, Carpenter is making a case to be on the mound on July 14 in the All-Star Game at Busch Stadium. Carpenter was nearly flawless in his last start on Saturday against the Royals. He pitched seven scoreless innings before allowing a run across in the eighth. Carpenter exited after allowing one run on three hits in 7 2/3 innings. Carpenter's fifth victory of the season came one start after he suffered his first loss on June 14 against Cleveland, and the Cardinals' staff leader has allowed just 10 earned runs in nine starts.
summary: 2009-06-25 - St. Louis Cardinals (2) @ New York Mets (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright threw six innings and allowed five runs against the Royals in his last start. The Cardinals' offense piled up the runs, so Wainwright scored another victory, his third in a row. But it wasn't exactly easy. Wainwright surrendered three runs in the first inning and a solo homer in the second. But after the early trouble, Wainwright settled down and pitched scoreless frames in innings three, four and five. He allowed another homer in the sixth and exited after throwing 90 pitches. Wainwright has been an innings eater in 2009 -- he's lasted at least six innings in 12 consecutive starts. And lately, he's been the beneficiary of some great run support. The Cardinals have averaged 12 runs per game in his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Some early trouble in the first inning proved costly for Perkins in his last start. Three runs by the Astros was all that Houston needed as the Twins suffered a 4-1 loss. Perkins wasn't helped by the fact that his defense missed a couple of plays in the inning, but the left-hander settled in after the trouble. He allowed just one run on five hits after that first inning as he went seven innings on the day. He walked one and struck out one in earning his fourth loss of the season. Next up for Perkins will be his first career start vs. the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer's getting frustrated, and so are the Cardinals. Neither manager Tony La Russa nor pitching coach Dave Duncan will actually say that Wellemeyer is on thin ice, but once Kyle Lohse returns to the rotation, they'll surely have to at least consider bumping Wellemeyer rather than Brad Thompson. He's got at least one more chance to get sorted out, though, and Saturday's home game against the Twins is it.
away_pitcher_note: Even on a night when Slowey clearly didn't have his best stuff, he limited the Astros to just one run over six innings. He scattered just three hits and struck out six but walked four, tying his career high set on June 17, 2007 vs. Milwaukee. He also battled some stiffness in his right side (soreness in his ribs) that caused the Twins to push back his start to the end of the rotation. The 25-year-old is now tied with Roy Halladay for the Major League lead in wins (10). With Halladay on the DL, Slowey will try to take the lead on his own when he faces the Cardinals in his next start. It will be his first career appearance vs. St. Louis

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro lost five straight starts before his last one, but he was much better than that. It's still remarkable that he's sitting on eight losses, as he's been consistently solid. He's throwing his fastball, and more specifically his sinking fastball, more than ever before. And it's working out nicely. Pineiro loves pitching at home, so this could be another good one.
away_pitcher_note: It had been six weeks since his last win but Liriano picked up a "W" for the first time since May 9 in his last start vs. the Brewers. The win wasn't the easiest as Liriano labored through five innings, allowing three runs on seven hits and walking five. He threw a career-high 117 pitches in the outing and barely did enough to earn the win. But still, a win is a win and the Twins will see if Liriano can earn his second in a row when he faces the Cardinals for the first time in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Thompson was better than his line might have indicated his last time out, but this still might be his last start for a while. Kyle Lohse is due back from the disabled list in short order, so Thompson needs to state his case to stay in the rotation, and he needs to do it soon. He's filled a lot of roles, from long man to late-inning reliever to starter, but it's pitching in the rotation that he enjoys most. If he wants to keep doing it, he'd be well advised to turn in a strong showing on Monday.
away_pitcher_note: If not for Jason Giambi's solo home run, Tim Lincecum would have tallied his second shutout of the season Tuesday against the Oakland Athletics. That doesn't mean he had an easy go of it, though. Twice Lincecum evaded bases-loaded situations by inducing groundball double plays. He's won three of his last four starts. The right-hander went 2-0 with a 1.38 ERA against the St. Louis Cardinals last season.
summary: 2009-06-29 - San Francisco Giants (10) @ St. Louis Cardinals (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: One rocky inning on Thursday sent Carpenter's ERA soaring ... all the way to 1.78. With only one more start before All-Stars are chosen, the loss may have cost him a chance to pitch in the Midsummer Classic, but few in the National League have been better this year. Carpenter is throwing everything he's got and throwing it all for quality strikes -- fastball, cutter, curveball and changeup. He's a handful, though once again it appears that he'll be facing off against a fellow former Cy Young Award winner -- for fourth time this year.
away_pitcher_note: Randy Johnson pitched seven strong innings for the fourth time this season Wednesday against the Oakland Athletics. Johnson allowed one run on six hits and struck out six. He's now won three starts in a row and five of his last six. In two games against the St. Louis Cardinals last season, the Big Unit went 0-1 with an ERA of 9.31.
summary: 2009-06-30 - San Francisco Giants (6) @ St. Louis Cardinals (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright has settled into something of a pattern this year. He hasn't been efficient, getting into trouble far too often and running up high pitch counts. But he's shown an ability to limit the damage, locking down with men on base. It's added up to a lot of good-but-not-great starts. The problem is that Wainwright and the team expect closer to great from Wainwright, who was the Opening Day starter at Busch Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Cain allowed all five runs, matching his season-worst, in last Friday's 5-1 loss at Milwaukee. But he still managed to look mostly effective, allowing six hits in seven innings and striking out nine. The decision ended his personal seven-game winning streak over a span of nine starts. Cain, who appears bound for the National League All-Star squad, has worked at least six innings in every start and has recorded 10 quality starts in 15 outings. He's living up to his workhorse reputation by averaging 105 pitches per game.
summary: 2009-07-01 - San Francisco Giants (1) @ St. Louis Cardinals (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Manager Tony La Russa declined to comment on Wellemeyer's status in the rotation after another rough start on Saturday, but it's clear the right-hander needs to turn it around. For now, the Cardinals don't feel like they have any other really viable options, so the chances are very good that Wellemeyer will make this start. However, also on Thursday, Kyle Lohse will make a Minor League rehabilitation start as he tries to recover from a right forearm injury. It may not be a coincidence that the two starts occur on the same day.
away_pitcher_note: Despite his record and ERA, Zito has improved visibly this season. He's averaging four walks per nine innings, down from 5.1 last year, and he leads the staff with 11 double-play grounders induced. Zito's coming off an encouraging start in which he shut out Milwaukee for five innings at Miller Park, where he had lost his previous three outings and recorded a 10.05 ERA. Zito's night ended when Prince Fielder belted a three-run homer in the sixth inning. But it still represented a significant improvement for Zito, who lost to St. Louis on May 30 when he allowed three runs and 10 hits in 6 2/3 innings.
summary: 2009-07-02 - San Francisco Giants (2) @ St. Louis Cardinals (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Bailey struggled to find the strike zone in a 7-3 win over the Indians on Saturday. He pitched five innings, giving up three hits, three runs while striking out two and walking a career-high seven hitters. The 23-year-old right-hander has now walked 13 batters in 9 1/3 innings. Bailey will try to find the strike zone more often against the Cardinals, against whom he is 0-2 with a 14.73 ERA in two career starts.
away_pitcher_note: If there's a hard-luck pitcher anywhere in baseball this year, it's Pineiro, who has been far better than his nine losses would suggest. He's allowed three earned runs or fewer in five straight starts but has gone 1-4 in that span.
