home_pitcher_note: It's the last chance for Lohse to show his stuff before the playoffs. There are no guarantees for him, as John Smoltz has pitched well and he has yet to really find his form. Lohse has felt good for two starts in a row, though, and that's encouraging. Things would seem to work better if Lohse can secure a rotation spot, because Smoltz has experience as a late-inning reliever while Lohse has pitched very little out of the bullpen in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Villanueva is likely to make a spot start in place of Dave Bush, who decided to shut it down for the year because of arm fatigue. Earlier this season, the Brewers hoped Villanueva could bolster a rotation beset by injuries to Bush and others, but he went 0-3 with a 6.38 ERA and was bounced back to the bullpen. Villanueva has been better of late, posting a 2.31 ERA over his last 15 appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro gets one more chance to go into October on a positive note. He's been less effective in September than earlier in the year, and his last time out he got rocked. Pineiro needs to keep the ball in the park, and he didn't do that well his last time out. He's been much better at home than on the road, which would actually be the one upside if the Cardinals begin the playoffs on the road: Pineiro would pitch Game 3 at Busch Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan will work on short rest to reach the 30-start milestone for the 11th consecutive season. Among active pitchers, only Livan Hernandez (12 seasons) has a longer streak. Trouble is, Suppan has surrendered 15 earned runs and 22 hits in 10 1/3 innings over his past two starts. He'll probably pitch only a couple of innings before the Brewers turn to former Cardinal Chris Narveson.

home_pitcher_note: Not only will Wolf make his first career playoff appearance Wednesday against the Cardinals, but he'll do so as the Dodgers' No. 1 starter. Wolf went 11-7 for the Dodgers this season, but the low win number hides the fact that he was the Dodgers' most consistent pitcher. His 214 1/3 innings led the team, and Wolf could always be counted on to come through in a big game. Before his last start, Wolf had a streak of 17 consecutive starts in which he lasted at least six innings, and Los Angeles is 22-12 in his starts this season. In his only start against the Cardinals this year, on July 27, Wolf gave up two runs on seven hits in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: If Carpenter hadn't missed several weeks early in the season due to a strained oblique muscle, he'd probably be the favorite for the National League Cy Young Award. The only thing separating him, in truth, is a relative lack of innings, compared to teammate Adam Wainwright and the Giants' Tim Lincecum. Even so, it was a brilliant year. Carpenter paced the league in ERA and was a tremendous story as he came back from nearly two full missed seasons due to elbow injuries and a nerve condition behind his right shoulder. There's nobody the Cardinals would rather have on the mound in a big game.
summary: 2009-10-07 - St. Louis Cardinals (3) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The 21-year-old lefty turned in one of his more impressive outings of the season during Saturday's NL West clincher against the Rockies. Kershaw struck out the first five batters he faced and K'd seven the first time through the Rockies' batting order. In all, he finished with 10 strikeouts and pitched six scoreless innings in his final start of the year. Kershaw started two games against the Cardinals this season -- one was great and one was bad. On July 29, Kershaw threw eight scoreless innings and struck out seven but earned a no-decision. On Aug. 19 he gave up two runs and walked four in only 3 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright is a leading contender, maybe the leading contender, for the National League Cy Young Award despite a frustrating outcome to his final start. He pitched very well in that game, though, and that was the most important thing. Although a bullpen and defense meltdowns cost Wainwright his 20th win, he showed no ill effects of having to work very hard in his previous start, when he threw 130 pitches to help the Cardinals clinch the Central division. He's a proven October performer, having closed out all three series in the Cards' run to the 2006 World Series championship.
summary: 2009-10-08 - St. Louis Cardinals (2) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro is not coming into the playoffs on a roll. He hasn't been bad, at least not usually, but he hasn't been nearly as good over the past five weeks as he was earlier in the year. Pineiro allowed four or more runs in five of his final seven starts, as his walk rate regressed from microscopic to merely impressive. One benefit, however, of the Cardinals opening on the road is that Pineiro will pitch at home. He's been quite a bit more impressive at Busch Stadium than on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Sometimes you get more than you pay for. Vicente Padilla came to the Dodgers almost for free and maybe all he needed was a change of scenery. Released by the Rangers with a reputation for being a bad apple, he's been a model citizen in the Dodgers clubhouse. More importantly, he went 4-0 with a 3.20 ERA in seven starts and finished up with 10 strikeouts in five innings against the Rockies. He throws hard, has a variety of pitches and attacks hitters with confidence. And despite a reputation as a head hunter, he didn't hit any opposing batters in 39 1/3 innings after hitting eight in 108 innings with Texas and 99 in his career.
summary: 2009-10-10 - Los Angeles Dodgers (5) @ St. Louis Cardinals (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Slowey has showed he's plenty healthy, not to mention effective, by pitching 21 innings with a 1.71 ERA. He has 17 strikeouts against three walks on the spring.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia will make his first game appearance since being notified that he had won the competition to be the Cardinals' fifth starter. Garcia was excellent all spring, pitching at least as well as any other Cardinals hurler -- not just the other contenders for the fifth job.

home_pitcher_note: Harang will tie a Reds record by making his fifth consecutive Opening Day start, but unlike the previous four, there was some debate over the assignment. While Bronson Arroyo posted back-to-back 15-win seasons in 2008-09, Harang had a combined 12-31 record and a 4.52 ERA and battled with injuries. This, after he was a 16-game winner in 2006 and '07. Last season, Harang was more often a victim of hard luck and poor run support than bad outings. He also had season-ending surgery to remove his appendix in August, just as he showed signs of getting back on track. On Opening Day, Harang is 1-3 with a 3.52 ERA. He's made a few mechanical tweaks this winter that he hopes will return him to being the ace he was.
away_pitcher_note: If Opening Day should simply go to the best pitcher, it's an open question as to who should receive the assignment. If the honor should also factor in matters like standing with the team and esteem in the clubhouse, Carpenter is a no-brainer. He was the Cy Young runner-up last year and is the unquestioned leader of the Cardinals' pitching staff. Carpenter features the same arsenal as always: heavy fastball, sharp cutter, curveball and changeup, and he's also toyed with a split-finger offering this spring. This will be Carpenter's fifth career Opening Day start, and his fourth with the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto had an up-and-down 2009 season but appeared to take steps forward with his young career. He was 8-4 with a 2.69 ERA over his first 16 starts, then went 0-6 with a 10.64 ERA over the next eight outings before a trip to the disabled list in late August for right shoulder inflammation. It appeared that a full season as a big league rookie, followed by winter ball and the World Baseball Classic weakened his arm. But he still finished strong with at 3-1 with a 3.63 ERA over his final six starts. This past winter, Cueto did not participate in the full grind of winter ball, and he came to camp with zip in his pitches this spring.
away_pitcher_note: Chris Carpenter got the nod over Wainwright for Opening Day, but Wainwright certainly would have been a worthy candidate as well. He came into his own last season, finishing third in the Cy Young voting and leading the National League in starts, wins and innings. Wainwright is the complete package on the mound. He's big and durable, with excellent stuff and command and a widely varied four-pitch assortment. He even complements his pitching by faring well in other parts of the game: he won his first Gold Glove last season and is an accomplished hitter to boot.

home_pitcher_note: After a slow start last season, when he was bothered by carpal tunnel soreness in his right hand that required two cortisone shots, Arroyo had a Major League best 2.07 ERA over his final 16 starts after July 10. He no longer plays guitar during the season but the soreness issue will be something to watch. Arroyo said he was willing to get another shot, if needed, to get through the season. Over four of his last five seasons with the Reds and Red Sox, Arroyo has won at least 14 games. He's won 15 games the last two seasons for Cincinnati.
away_pitcher_note: The Cardinals signed Penny to a one-year deal this winter with the hope and expectation that the stars would align just right and he would regain the form that made him a star in the last decade with the Marlins and Dodgers. There are a number of reasons to think it might happen. Penny pitched better upon signing with the Giants than he did when he was with the Red Sox in 2009, and he has the kind of power arm that pitching coach Dave Duncan loves to work with. Penny had a so-so spring in terms of results, but his stuff appears to be very much intact.

home_pitcher_note: Bush entered Spring Training in something of a tenuous situation because of his $4.215 million salary, which wasn't guaranteed until Opening Day. But he pitched his way into the Brewers' mix, going 1-1 with a 4.34 ERA in four Cactus League appearances. That ERA is a bit deceiving because Bush surrendered six earned runs in his final Arizona start; before that he had allowed only one run in each of his three outings. When Bush is hitting his spots he is extremely effective; he took a no-hitter into the eighth inning in each of the past two seasons. His 2009 season was marred by an elbow injury -- the result of a line drive off Hanley Ramirez's bat in Florida that caused Bush trouble throughout the summer. He says he's 100 percent healthy this year.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse will be looking to put a frustrating and at times painful 2009 season in the rear-view mirror as quickly as possible. His performance didn't live up to what he managed in an outstanding 2008, and he was beset by one malady after another. Lohse dealt with a string of injuries and even a nasty stomach illness in one start. He's stayed healthy this spring, though, and looks poised to put together a better season in '10. He may not repeat his '08 success, but he should be better than he was last year, and that would be a good start for the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers briefly considered bringing a fifth starter into the mix here, but instead will go back to Gallardo on regular rest. He was the team's pick to pitch Opening Day against the Rockies after winning the team's pitcher of the year honor in 2009, and he should be on a longer leash this season with a full Major League season under his belt. Gallardo has struggled against the Cardinals in his career, going 0-2 with a 5.70 ERA in four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia entered camp as the longest shot of three candidates to make the Cardinals' rotation, but he pitched so well that the club simply didn't have any choice. The lefty was the clear winner of the competition with Kyle McClellan, who will go to the Cardinals bullpen, and Rich Hill, who will go to Triple-A Memphis. He has good stuff, developing but already decent command and a solid mound presence. He's also still pretty inexperienced as a professional pitcher and is less than two years removed from Tommy John surgery. That means the club will handle him gently, with hopes of keeping him healthy by limiting his innings and pitches.

home_pitcher_note: The prime-time assignment goes to Wolf, who could have his hands full with Cardinals hitters like former Brewer Felipe Lopez (7-for-21, .333 lifetime against Wolf), Albert Pujols (5-for-16, .313) and Matt Holliday (5-for-16, four extra-base hits). Wolf surrendered nine hits in his Brewers debut but won after allowing four runs in 6 2/3 innings thanks to an offense that scored seven times. He may spend some time between starts working on some ideas against left-handed hitters; Wolf is traditionally tough on them but gave up six hits to lefties on Tuesday night.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter had one frustrating inning in Monday's win over the Reds but otherwise looked a lot like the guy who steamrolled the National League Central in 2009. Of all the things Carpenter accomplished in '09, one of the most impressive was his dominance within his own division. In 15 starts within the Central, Carpenter went 11-0 with a 1.58 ERA. He's already off to a good start in that regard this year, so you can expect to see him pitching an awful lot in division games in 2010. He was especially brilliant in two starts at Miller Park last year, allowing no runs, three hits and two walks over 17 innings -- with 20 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Chris Carpenter got the Opening Day start, so Wainwright gets the home opener. As manager Tony La Russa said when he announced the decision, "It's not our first rodeo." Two aces, two Cy Young finalists, two honors. Wainwright was outstanding in his first start, and pronounced himself a good six weeks ahead of where he was at this point last season. His results were mostly good early last year, but he was walking far too many batters. This time around, he seems to be in a groove right away.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a solid first start of the season in taking a loss to the Giants on Tuesday, left-hander Wandy Rodriguez gets the ball in the series opener in St. Louis. Rodriguez held the Giants to three runs on seven hits and four walks and struck out four batters. He's 3-9 with a 3.95 ERA in 15 career appearances against the Cardinals, including 14 starts. He made five starts against St. Louis last year and was 1-3 with a 3.72 ERA. Rodriguez has held Albert Pujols in check. The Cardinals slugger is a career .161 hitter with no home runs and one RBI in 31 at-bats against Pujols.

home_pitcher_note: If one game is any indication -- and it isn't necessarily -- Penny is poised for a rebound. He turned in an excellent Cardinals debut, throwing strikes and keeping the ball down. Efficiency has been an issue for Penny in the past, but on Thursday he was efficient as well as effective. Penny has pretty much always been good when he's been healthy and pitching in the National League. He's back in the NL, and he looks healthy, so don't rule out the possibility of a very good year from the 31-year-old righty.
away_pitcher_note: Myers makes his second start for the Astros after giving up a career-high 12 hits in his Houston debut April 7. Myers allowed four runs, one walk and struck out three batters in a 10-4 loss to the Giants in his first start since May 27, 2009. He faced the Cardinals once last year at Busch Stadium and was rocked for nine hits and five runs in 5 1/3 innings. He's 4-2 with a 5.45 ERA in 13 career games against the Cardinals, including 11 starts, and is 2-1 with a 7.27 ERA lifetime in six appearances at Busch Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Wildness was the issue in Lohse's first start on Friday in Milwaukee. He walked three and gave up six hits and four runs in six innings against the Brewers in a game the Cardinals won on Nick Stavinoha's two-out, ninth-inning home run off Trevor Hoffman. "I got in trouble and I walked guys," Lohse said. "You can't walk yourself into trouble like that." Lohse is 6-5 with a 2.99 ERA in 12 games against Houston, but has been especially strong against the Astros the past two years. Since 2008, he is 5-1 with a 2.44 ERA in seven starts against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Norris, who burst onto the scene as a rookie last year and went 6-3 in 11 games, struggled in his first start in his sophomore season April 9 against the Phillies at Minute Maid Park. Norris gave up six hits, three runs and four walks in 2 2/3 innings, but he can take satisfaction that he's had good success against the Cardinals, having not allowed a run against them in 13 career innings. He threw seven scoreless innings in his first win in his first Major League start Aug. 2 at Busch Stadium, holding the Cardinals hitless through the first five innings. He beat them again Sept. 23 in Houston, throwing six scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: It's far, far too early to be alarmed about Carpenter, but it's not too early to be aware. Carpenter, who allowed seven home runs in the entire 2009 season, has allowed five in two starts. And it could very easily be six, except that Colby Rasmus reached over the wall to rob Scott Rolen in Cincinnati on Opening Day. Carpenter's history suggests he'll get right very quickly, but being susceptible to the long ball is a very unusual trait for the former Cy Young Award winner. He gets the call in the series opener on regular rest, allowing him to pitch five days later in Arizona before the off day.
away_pitcher_note: There was some discussion of skipping Perez's second start of the season, but that would have accomplished little: without an off-day during their road trip to Denver and St. Louis, the Mets would simply be flipping Perez and Johan Santana in the rotation -- not skipping their erratic left-hander altogether. So they are sticking with Perez at Busch Stadium, where he has struggled in the past. In his lone start there last season, Perez allowed four runs in 4 2/3 innings, escaping with a no-decision.
summary: 2010-04-16 - New York Mets (3) @ St. Louis Cardinals (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: There was a lot to like when Garcia last pitched, as the rookie left-hander showed impressive stuff and pretty good command. He looks a great deal different from his first stint in the Majors, back in 2008. The key for Garcia will be to stay healthy, because he's been consistently effective at just about every level. Garcia goes on six days' rest after his first start as the Cardinals take steps to protect him in his first full big league season. He also once again is spared the Sunday night ESPN assignment.
away_pitcher_note: Though Santana didn't pitch particularly poorly in his last start against the Nationals, he complained of a lack of fastball command in the first inning. And he made one bad pitch at precisely the wrong time, resulting in a Josh Willingham grand slam from which he and the Mets never recovered. Though Santana will be pitching at Busch Stadium for the first time in his career, he does have one unenviable piece of history against the Cardinals: Albert Pujols is 6-for-12 with two home runs in his career off Santana.
summary: 2010-04-17 - New York Mets (2) @ St. Louis Cardinals (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: If Wainwright had gotten off to this kind of start last season, he very likely would have won the Cy Young Award rather than finishing third. He's been absolutely outstanding through two starts, quite a turnaround from a somewhat slow beginning to '09. Wainwright is pounding the strike zone, pitching deep into games, getting groundballs and strikeouts -- in short, doing all the things he does when he's at his best. He'll get the call in the Sunday night game, an assignment which shouldn't faze him in the slightest.
away_pitcher_note: Three walks, a hit batsman and a throwing error -- his own throwing error -- led to six runs and an early exit for Maine on Wednesday in Denver. Maine walked two of the three leadoff batters he faced, served up an RBI double to pitcher Greg Smith and allowed eight runs in total, tying his career high. He also vented his frustration with some revealing body language on the mound. Maine will look to improve against the Cardinals, who battered him for five runs (and drew five walks) in 5 2/3 innings in their lone meeting last season.
summary: 2010-04-18 - New York Mets (3) @ St. Louis Cardinals (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Lopez scuffled a bit in his last outing against the Dodgers in their home opener. The right-hander allowed five runs on 11 hits over five innings. The blow that really hurt him was a two-run homer by Matt Kemp in the fourth after the D-backs had rallied to tie the game in the top half of the frame. The start was in contrast to his outstanding Arizona debut against the Pirates, when he allowed just one run on six hits over six innings. He even got into the action at the plate when he led off what would turn out to be a six-run third inning with a single to right off Charlie Morton. While not overpowering, Lopez has a good feel for pitching and manages a game well. Lopez came to Spring Training as a non-roster invitee and pitched his way into the No. 4 spot in the rotation, besting Billy Buckner and Kevin Mulvey. The right-hander has battled arm troubles since being the ace of the Orioles' staff earlier in the decade. He throws a fastball, cutter, curveball, slider and change. Lopez appeared in seven games (five starts) for the Phillies last year and also started 18 games for Triple-A Lehigh Valley.
away_pitcher_note: Nobody on the Cardinals staff is pitching better than Penny, who has surely exceeded even optimistic expectations through two starts. He's throwing tons of strikes, pounding the bottom of the zone and getting quick outs. It's a far cry from the pitcher who once averaged more than 17 pitches per inning over a full season. Penny has shut down the Diamondbacks over his career, going 9-3 with a 1.96 ERA against Arizona, including 2-1 with a 1.88 ERA in five starts at Chase Field.

home_pitcher_note: Haren gave the D-backs all he had in his last outing against the Dodgers, throwing a career-high 121 pitches. The right-hander left the game in the seventh with one on and one out and Arizona leading, 3-1. His hopes of a win were quickly dashed when reliever Aaron Heilman allowed a home run to the first batter he faced, Matt Kemp, to tie the game. In his start prior to that against the Pirates, Haren was not his usual self. He got too many pitches up in the zone and wound up allowing six runs (five earned) on nine hits over 6 2/3 innings. Haren fanned nine and walked two. It was quite a contrast from his Opening Day start, when he dominated the Padres. Haren allowed just three hits and one run over seven innings while being aggressive in the strike zone, throwing first-pitch strikes to 20 of the 24 hitters he faced. Haren only went to three balls on one of those 24 hitters in the opener. He throws a fastball, cut fastball, curve and split.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse was much better in his second start than his first, increasing the hope that he might be able to regain his 2008 form. He's one of the bigger variables on the '10 Cardinals. If Lohse pitches like he did in '08, it adds significant depth to an already good rotation. If he looks more like the man who had a hard time in '09, the St. Louis starting five is less of an asset. In fairness to Lohse, he dealt with physical maladies for nearly all of '09. If the true, healthy Lohse is the '08 version, it's good news for the Cardinals indeed.

St. Louis jiggered its rotation over the previous weekend in order to get Carpenter on this game. That's in part because it's before the off-day, and perhaps in part because Phoenix can be an unforgiving place to pitch. Carpenter has fared well there, though, going 3-0 in five games with a 3.13 ERA in the homer-happy yard. He's coming off a reassuring game for fans in which he struck out 10 and didn't allow a home run. That's quite a turnaround from a five-inning, seven-run, three-homer showing five days earlier.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum is off to a 3-0 start for the first time in his career. Though his velocity has diminished slightly, he still has enough on his fastball to set up an improving slider, an effective curveball and his devastating changeup. Lincecum has started only once at home thus far, allowing Brian McCann's two-run homer and nothing else in seven innings while striking out 10 as the Giants defeated Atlanta, 6-3. Lincecum has thrived against St. Louis, winning each of his four starts while posting a 1.61 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Lots of guys perform well in Spring Training, especially in the late innings against Minor Leaguers. They don't all carry it over, but Garcia assuredly has. He's turned in two excellent starts since winning the Cardinals' fifth starter job coming out of camp. He'll be going up against a stud opponent, but that hasn't fazed the rookie thus far. Garcia's two starts have found him opposing Yovani Gallardo and Johan Santana, so it shouldn't be an issue. Garcia has kept his poise despite limited experience, and there's little doubt about his stuff.
summary: 2010-04-23 - St. Louis Cardinals (1) @ San Francisco Giants (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The second-half Zito might have shown up early this year. Zito, who typically struggles before the All-Star break and excels afterward, has limited opponents to a .176 batting average. Zito has struck out just nine batters but has walked only five in 19 1/3 innings. He's coming off a no-decision last Sunday at Los Angeles, where he lasted 7 1/3 innings and left with a 1-0 lead after walking Garret Anderson. Manny Ramirez's pinch-hit homer off Sergio Romo then changed everything. Zito has struggled against St. Louis, going 0-4 with a 5.54 ERA in five lifetime starts.
away_pitcher_note: When his team needed him to help rest the bullpen, Wainwright delivered an outstanding game. But it's getting to the point where all he does is deliver outstanding games. Wainwright pitches deep into games, gets groundballs and strikeouts and even plays a complete game to boot. He's the reigning Gold Glover at his position and a viable candidate to win a Silver Slugger as well. He does it all, and there's no reason to think he'll stop this weekend at AT&T Park. Over his last 30 starts, dating back to mid-May of last season, Wainwright is 19-7 with a 2.17 ERA.
summary: 2010-04-24 - St. Louis Cardinals (0) @ San Francisco Giants (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Cain's lack of decisions obscures the fact that each of his outings has been a "quality" start. He owns an excellent strikeout-to-walk ratio of 4 to 1, reflecting his annual goal of cutting down on his walks. Cain issued 91 free passes in 217 2/3 innings in 2008, then walked 73 in the same number of innings last year. Cain picked up his first career victory against the Cardinals last year, yielding two runs (one earned) in 6 1/3 innings on May 29 at AT&T Park. He pitched even better but received no decision on July 1 at St. Louis, surrendering one run in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Penny keeps cruising. It looked like he might hit a bump in the road early in his last start, but instead he turned in another solid, seven-inning, two-run performance. He's throwing strikes, and more than that, he's throwing good strikes. He's working very efficiently, averaging almost exactly 14 pitches per inning. Since Penny was let go by the Red Sox and joined the Giants last summer, he's gone at least seven innings with two or fewer earned runs in eight of his nine starts. Penny also loves pitching at AT&T Park,  where he has a lifetime 3.05 ERA in 14 starts.
summary: 2010-04-25 - St. Louis Cardinals (2) @ San Francisco Giants (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Very little went right for Lohse in his last start, and he'll be looking to correct not only location mistakes, but some questionable pitch selections from that game. Lohse typically pitches off his fastball, but in Arizona he did what's often called "pitching backward" -- working off his other pitches and then going to the fastball as a change of pace, as it were. His best start this year was at Busch Stadium, and he's consistently been a good bit better at home than on the road since joining the Cardinals in 2008, so there's reason to think he'll be just fine his next time out.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson returns to the scene of his only career home run with the hope of bouncing back from the tough-luck loss he suffered on Wednesday against Roy Halladay and the Phillies. En route to his first loss of the season, the 34-year-old right-hander compiled a high early pitch count (61 pitches through three innings) and was damaged by the two Jayson Werth doubles that led to the only two runs he surrendered in six innings. Hudson's past two outings haven't been as impressive as his season debut against the Giants. But his velocity and crispness of his breaking pitches appear to back up his belief that his surgically-repaired right arm is as strong as its been in the past five years. He is 2-1 with a 5.96 ERA in his past four starts against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: As long as nobody hits Carpenter with a pitch, he should have an excellent game. He's pitched well his past two starts after an ugly one at the end of the season's first week. The only real hiccup occurred in his last outing when he let his anger over being hit affect his concentration. Carpenter's focus is one of his most critical attributes on the mound, and when it's compromised, he's a lesser pitcher. That very rarely happens, and it's not likely to happen again in this game. Carpenter has a 6.31 ERA in seven career starts against Atlanta, but that's a much better-looking 4.20 when you only count his tenure as a Cardinal.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe has struggled to find the consistency he expected after refining his delivery and encountering some success in Spring Training. Still, with the help of strong offensive support, he did not suffer his first loss until Thursday, when he allowed the Phillies five runs -- four earned -- and six hits in five innings. Lowe has issued 14 walks and allowed opponents to post a .268 batting average in the first 22 1/3 innings he has completed this season.  Lowe is 1-6 in seven career starts against the Cardinals, and during his most recent outing against them -- on Aug. 6, 2008 -- he allowed 13 hits and eight runs in just 3 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia might not have been as sharp as his first two outings, and still pitched effectively enough to earn a win, if the opposing pitcher wasn't two-time reigning Cy Young Award winner Tim Lincecum. Garcia allowed seven hits, more than he allowed through his first two appearances combined, and allowed just two earned runs. Put to the test when errors were made behind him, Garcia remained composed and was able to avoid the big inning. That bodes well for the young pitcher in the future. The Giants scored two runs on errors and another on a wild pitch. The fourth scored on a dribbler to first base where the runner just beat Albert Pujols to the bag. Twice he induced double-play grounders to end innings with runners in scoring position.
away_pitcher_note: Kawakami has pitched effectively in two of his first three starts, but still finds himself in search of his first win of the year. He hasn't pitched into the seventh inning yet and during his two good outings he was undone by two-run, sixth innings. Regarded as a serviceable back-of-the-rotation starter, the 34-year-old right-hander allowed three earned runs and six hits in six innings against the Mets on Friday night. This will be the first career appearance against the Cardinals for the Japanese right-hander, who has allowed opponents to hit .284 this year.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright pitched brilliantly in his last start, against the Giants, but that's been true of all four of his previous starts this year. He took a shutout into the eighth inning before giving up a couple of runs and losing to Barry Zito. He's been feeling good all year, and even without a good offspeed pitch, he was able to shut down the Giants. He hasn't allowed a home run in his past three starts and has pitched deep into all of them, going at least seven innings. He's 4-0 with a 1.50 ERA in seven appearances (four starts) against the Braves, with a .216 batting average against.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start of the regular season, Jurrjens allowed two unearned runs on three hits over five innings against the Chicago Cubs. In the three starts since, the righty has struggled mightily, allowing 14 earned runs in 18 innings while picking up two losses. Jurrjens has fared well against the Cardinals in his career, despite a 1-2 record, with a 2.14 ERA in 21 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Penny is 7-1 in his past 10 Major League starts, with an ERA of 1.92, dating to last year. That's on the heels of a dreadful 2-7 record in his final 15 starts with the Boston Red Sox. Penny seems much more comfortable pitching in the National League, and you won't hear many arguments from the four teams he's faced this year. He's been a workhorse for the Cardinals and saved them from getting swept in their final series on the road in San Francisco in his last outing. This is the Penny a lot of people were talking about when he pitched for the Florida Marlins and Los Angeles Dodgers. Penny has allowed as many earned runs (three) as batters he's walked this year. With that kind of control, it's possible for Penny to push both Chris Carpenter and Adam Wainwright for top-of-the-rotation honors.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto was pushed back one day in the rotation to give him extra rest. Bronson Arroyo took Cueto's normal turn in the rotation on April 23. Reds manager Dusty Baker wanted to spell Cueto to his abundance of pitches. In three starts, Cueto had thrown 322 pitches. In his start on Saturday, Cueto was a bit more efficient, throwing 92 pitches in six innings. But the results were largely the same. Cueto allowed five earned runs and seven hits, walked one and struck out five. But he was outdueled by San Diego's Wade LeBlanc, who gave up just three hits in helping lead the Padres to a 5-0 victory to hand Cueto his first loss of the season.

home_pitcher_note: In a Cardinals rotation that has been superb, Lohse has been the one who hasn't really found his groove. He did seem to find something over the final few innings of his most recent start, and he said it had to do with reverting to the delivery he used in his excellent 2008 campaign. He's had great success at home as a Cardinal, and he's pitched well against the Astros, so this should be a good matchup for the veteran right-hander. Lohse has a 2.95 ERA in 13 career appearances (12 starts) against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey is still looking for more consistency in his outings. On Sunday afternoon in the series finale against San Diego, Bailey breezed through three innings, giving up just one hit while striking out four. He kept his pitch count manageable, with the exception of two rough innings. He allowed a two-run home run to Adrian Gonzalez in the fourth. In the sixth, he managed to escape with no runs allowed, but he gave up two hits, one walk and saw his pitch count elevate. Bailey finished with 105 pitches, 70 for strikes, over six innings. He allowed four earned runs and seven hits. Bailey walked just one and tied a career high with eight strikeouts in taking a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter has been a little less efficient, a little less crisp, than he is when he's at his absolute best. He's needing more pitches than usual and walking a few more batters than usual. And yet, overall, he's still been excellent. Carpenter has better than a 3-to-1 strikeout-to-walk ratio, a perfectly solid 3.48 ERA and quality starts in four of his five outings. It's a sign of how brilliant he's been over the past several years that there's any fault at all to be found in such an effective start to the season.
away_pitcher_note: In a 6-2 Reds win over the Astros on Tuesday, Harang was aggressive. He was ahead of hitters. And for the first time this season and only the second time since Aug. 9, 2009, he was a winning pitcher. Harang pitched six innings and allowed two earned runs and eight hits with one walk and six strikeouts. He did most of his work with the fastball and despite having no 1-2-3 innings, limited any serious damage -- something he wasn't able to do in previous outings this season.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton makes his 2010 season debut after spending the first month of the season on the disabled list with a strained left oblique. The Phillies don't expect Blanton to have perfect command in his first start of the season, but they certainly hope he performs better than most of the rest of the rotation this season. Phillies starters not named Roy Halladay entered Sunday with a 5.19 ERA, which has put a strain on the bullpen and the offense. The Phillies like to call Blanton an innings eater. Six-plus innings would be welcomed Monday.
away_pitcher_note: It's another tough test for Garcia, who's seen plenty of them already this year. This time it's not so much the opposing starter -- no Tim Lincecum or Johan Santana -- as it is the opposing lineup and the ballpark. Garcia will be facing the National League's best lineup, and a team that last year was also as good as any against left-handed pitching. And he'll be doing it in the claustrophobic confines of Citizens Bank Park, one of the toughest parks on pitchers in the league. Good luck, kid.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels is coming off another so-so outing against San Francisco, in which he struck out a season-high 10, but allowed another four earned runs in six innings with four walks and nine hits. His velocity worked its way up to 93, which is a good sign for the Phillies left-hander. But April wasn't a strong month, and Hamels carries a 5.28 ERA and 1.47 WHIP into his first start in May. The Phillies may bump Hamels to Tuesday if they decide to activate Joe Blanton off the 15-day disabled list to start Monday. That would split up the left-handers Hamels and Jamie Moyer in the Phils' rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright is coming off his least-impressive start of the year, but that just tells you how good he's been in 2010. When three runs in six innings counts as not-up-to-snuff, you're going pretty well. Over Wainwright's last 32 starts, dating back to mid-May of last season, he's 20-8 with a 2.23 ERA, 209 strikeouts, 53 walks and 13 home runs allowed in 229 2/3 innings. Wainwright has held his own nicely at Citizens Bank Park, with eight shutout innings over two career appearances (one start).

home_pitcher_note: Many Phillies fans wondered if Kendrick would get another chance to start, carrying a 7.61 ERA after five starts. But the Phillies have little choice but to stick with him with left-hander J.A. Happ still on the disabled list. "We need Kyle to step up," pitching coach Rich Dubee said. "We need him to be more efficient. We need him to pitch down in the strike zone. We need his temp to pick up so we have energy playing behind him. And he's aware of those things. Now he has to put them in play."
away_pitcher_note: Penny looked a bit shaky for the first time as a Cardinal his last time out, and he still turned in an effective outing. He wasn't helped by brutal weather conditions, and he came out of the game with a quality start, but he walked five in six innings. He's one of a pretty short list of pitchers with a history of success at Philadelphia's tough Citizens Bank Park. Penny is 2-0 in three starts at the Phillies' home stadium, with a 1.71 ERA and one homer allowed in 21 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay has been the real deal since he joined the Phillies. He is 5-1 with a 1.47 ERA. He has thrown three complete games, including two shutouts. He leads the Majors in wins, shutouts, complete games, innings (49) and strikeout-to-walk ratio (9.75). He is fourth in strikeouts (39). Halladay has delivered, but so far he has not rubbed off on the rest of the rotation. He can't help that, but he can continue to win. They hope he does that Thursday against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: If Lohse has really found something, an already good year may be about to get even better for the Cardinals. He's coming off his best start in nearly a year, seven excellent innings against the Reds with eight strikeouts. Lohse got ahead, threw strikes and kept the ball down, which is a pretty good plan for nearly anybody. He'll be returning to a park he briefly called home, but it's worth noting that pitching away from Busch Stadium has not suited Lohse well since he joined the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Duke has lost each of his past three starts, none of which have been reminiscent of his first three this season. After allowing five earned runs in his first three starts, Duke has given up 18 earned runs in his last 15 outings. His start on Saturday was a step forward -- there were more first-pitch strikes and better overall fastball command -- but Duke isn't as consistently sharp as he needs to be. He hung a slider that Andre Ethier sent over the wall for a three-run homer, and Duke skirted out of other trouble all night. Duke is 4-5 with a 3.73 ERA in 13 career starts against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter will look to stay unbeaten in his seventh start this season. In his six previous starts, Carpenter has been extremely consistent with four victories and two no-decisions. In 38 innings, Carpenter has only allowed 27 hits and 15 runs (12 earned). He has struck out 39 and walked 13, good for an impressive 3-to-1 ratio. A 17-game winner last season, Carpenter has continued to pitch well in 2010 thanks to terrific control. Plus, he has been locating all of his pitches with very few mistakes. That has added up to a terrific month of April and early May for the veteran right-hander.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens remains the fifth starter for now, though the rotation spot is likely to remain in flux from week to week. After a strong start against Milwaukee, Karstens came out a bit flat in his outing against Milwaukee on Sunday. Too many balls were elevated, and Karstens gave up six runs and 11 hits in five innings. The Pirates aren't expecting great things from the right-hander -- who is in the rotation largely because of a lack of other options -- but they would love to see Karstens provide some stability in the back of the rotation if he can. Karstens allowed three runs in six innings and took the loss in his only previous start against St. Louis.

Maholm picked up his second win of the season in a gutsy start against the Cubs on Tuesday. It was clear Maholm was having issues with his sinker from the start as Chicago teed off and hit a number of deep fly balls. But only two went out of the park -- both were solo shots -- and Maholm otherwise kept the Cubs off the scoreboard. As has become expected from the Pirates' most consistent pitcher, Maholm found a way to make the big pitches when he needed to most. He has given the Pirates at least six innings in five of his six starts, which is more than any other pitcher on the staff can say. In 10 career starts against St. Louis, Maholm is 3-3 with a 3.09 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The Cardinals wasted a signature outing by Wainwright in a 2-1, 10-inning loss to the Phillies on Wednesday. Wainwright received a no-decision, allowing one run, four hits and two walks in eight innings. Wainwright, entered the game with a 2.13 ERA that shrank to 1.96.

home_pitcher_note: Penny lost a 4-0 decision in Philadelphia his last time out on May 6. Penny left after needing only 75 pitches to clear six innings. Game situation rather than his performance dictated his removal from a 3-0 game. Penny has been sensational since hooking up with St. Louis pitching guru Dave Duncan, and it looks like he's headed for his best season in years.
away_pitcher_note: Myers helped Houston end its eight-game losing streak Wednesday when he pitched seven innings against Arizona, allowing six hits and two runs, in a game the Astros eventually won 4-2 in the bottom of the ninth. Myers has lasted at least six innings in all six starts this season. He won his only game April 25 vs. Pittsburgh at home. He has thrown 100 or more pitches in five of his six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse got roughed up at Philadelphia on May 6, surrendering five runs (three earned) off nine hits and one walk with three strikeouts over four innings. Lohse has been up and down through six starts. He's been shelled twice, had two decent outings and tossed two gems.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez's last start, Thursday at home against Arizona, was his worst of the season, as he gave up nine hits and five earned runs in 3 2/3 innings. He has gone at least six innings in all but one of his other starts, when he lasted just 4 1/3 innings April 12 at St. Louis. He has lost his last two starts after beating Pittsburgh April 24 at home, when he gave up just one earned run in 7 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter struck out eight and walked none in a no-decision against the Pirates on May 7. Carpenter allowed two earned runs on eight hits and his WHIP stands at a sparkling 1.07. He hasn't gone more than seven innings in any of his seven starts this season. Carpenter has yielded just four runs in 20 innings over his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Norris continues to baffle the Astros, if not opponents. He lost his third straight start Friday when he surrendered four earned runs in four innings vs. San Diego. He hasn't won since April 15 at St. Louis, his second start of the season and Houston's first win of the year. He hasn't lasted more than five innings in any of his six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Harang finally seems to be on a roll, with three straight quality starts. He was 0-3 with an 8.31 ERA over his first four starts but is 2-1 with a 3.37 ERA over his last three. In a 14-2 win over the Cubs on Saturday, he allowed two earned runs and seven hits with one walk and a season-high nine strikeouts. The key to Harang's recent success is a return to using his fastball, being aggressive and working inside.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia makes his fifth road start, and for the second time in three games he appears in a very tough ballpark on pitchers. Still, nothing has daunted the youngster so far: not top-flight opposing lineups, not Cy Young Award winners starting for the opponent, nothing. So there's no reason to think that Great American Ball Park will faze him, either. Garcia has gone at least six innings in all six of his starts this season, and he has yet to allow more than two earned runs. If he keeps that up, he won't just garner Rookie of the Year consideration, he'll be a Cy Young candidate.

home_pitcher_note: Leake took a no-hitter into the sixth inning and was a 5-3 winner over the Cubs with a sharp seven-inning performance on Sunday. All three runs scored in the seventh and overall he allowed four hits with one walk and struck out six. He threw 91 pitches, with 61 being strikes. It was the first time the rookie faced a lineup he had previously seen but it proved to be of little issue. He kept locating the sinker and induced 11 groundball outs.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright is typically considered among the second tier of pitchers in the National League: a true No. 1, but a notch below Cy Young Award-winners Roy Halladay and Tim Lincecum. And it's true that they have the hardware and he doesn't, but over the past year, Wainwright has been as good as anyone. Over the past 52 weeks, dating back to May 15 of last season, Wainwright has made 34 starts, going 21-8 with a 2.22 ERA, 243 2/3 innings pitched, 222 strikeouts, 57 walks and 13 home runs allowed.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Arroyo limited Pittsburgh to one run over seven-plus innings in his latest successful start against his former team as the Reds beat the Pirates, 2-1, on Monday. Arroyo couldn't have been much sharper, retiring the side in order four times while not allowing a runner past second base until Ronny Cedeno homered. The right-hander struck out two and walked one, throwing 72 of 103 pitches for strikes. He lasted at least six innings for the sixth time in seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Maybe one of these days Penny will get a little help. He's gotten the bare minimum of run support this season, and his last time out, his defense betrayed him, as well. Penny has pitched as well as just about any hurler in the NL so far on the season, but he's stuck with a 3-3 record that just doesn't tell the story. Penny has issued a grand total of eight walks in 47 2/3 innings on the year, which may tell you as much as any number could about the kind of year he's having.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse hasn't been the disaster this year that some fans seem to think he's been, but he also hasn't been as good as he or the club would like. He's had three solid starts out of seven, including two that were very good. It's just that when he's been off, he's been way off: including a nine-run performance his last time out. He's not in any jeopardy yet, if only because there are no really viable alternatives, but at some point if Lohse doesn't get straightened out, the Cardinals may have to begin to look at what else they can do. That time is not here yet, though, and probably won't arrive for a few more weeks if it does at all.
away_pitcher_note: Stammen picked up a no-decision this past Wednesday. He wasn't as effective as he was against the Marlins last week. He lasted five innings against the Mets, allowed four runs on seven hits, struck out two and walked two. However, Stammen had a great day at the plate, going 2-for-2 with three RBIs. The last pitcher in franchise history with three RBIs was right-hander Guillermo Mota against the Red Sox on June 9, 1999.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter is pleased with the way he's coming along, feeling better and feeling stronger. But he also grants that this year has been more laborious than some. He's been working to find a consistent delivery, and searching for reliability with his cut fastball, usually a signature pitch. And yet Carpenter still has an ERA in the low 3s, and he's averaging just slightly under a strikeout per inning. The results have been outstanding. If he can in fact get better, look out.
away_pitcher_note: A day after his left flexor tendon stiffened up against the Rockies on Thursday night, Lannan played catch from 100 feet without any problems and is scheduled to make his next scheduled start against the Cardinals on Tuesday. Lannan even had a successful bullpen session on Saturday to make sure he could make the start. On Thursday, Lannan made his first start since May 2. There was good news and bad news when it came to Lannan's outing against the Rockies. He cruised through the first four innings. However, after sitting on the bench for a while in the top of the fifth inning, Lannan's left flexor tendon started to stiffen up. Suddenly, he couldn't get his pitches down in the strike zone. It didn't help that Lannan pitched in rainy, cold weather.

home_pitcher_note: The Cardinals' young lefty doesn't pitch like a rookie. He's poised and doesn't get rattled, but more strikingly, he has four pitches that he throws with confidence in a wide variety of counts. The difference-maker seems to be his slider, which he used to get a slew of strikeouts his last time out. Garcia came through the Minors known for a sinker-curveball combination, but the addition of the slider (which he also sometimes throws smaller, like a cutter) has taken him a major step forward.
away_pitcher_note: A case can be made that Sanchez is coming off his best outing of the season. The right-hander beat the Mets on May 14, and it was his first win since April 22 at Houston. Sanchez matched his season high with seven strikeouts. The seven innings and 108 pitches also were season highs. Sanchez has made eight starts, and in seven of them he has thrown at least six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright is coming off an uncharacteristically forgettable performance, but he often seems to follow those games with some of his best showings. His last time out, he made far too many mistakes with his curveball. That was very unlike him, since the curve is Wainwright's out pitch and one of the finest breaking balls of any National League pitcher.  He's been especially dominant at home, posting a 2.03 ERA at Busch Stadium since the start of 2009.
away_pitcher_note: It's not always been pretty or crisp when Robertson pitches, but for the most part, the veteran left-hander has been getting the job done. Even though he was struck out 25 and walked 19 in 41 1/3 innings, he has been able to minimize damage. Robertson collected a win over the Mets in his last start, giving up three runs (two earned) in 5 2/3 innings. In an injury-plaged 2009 with the Tigers, Robertson logged 49 2/3 total innings. He is closing in on that number now.

home_pitcher_note: Very little went right for Penny his last time out. When he made bad pitches, they got hit hard. Even when he made good pitches, he had bad luck. Now he returns home to face his first Major League team, the Marlins. He's 2-1 with a 3.91 ERA in four career starts against Florida. Penny needs to get back to the efficient ways that marked his first seven starts, when he enjoyed quick outs and quick innings. In his loss to the Reds on Sunday, he needed more than 100 pitches to get through five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro returns to Busch Stadium to face his former teammates on the heels of his finest performance with the Angels, a shutout of the Athletics on Sunday at Angel Stadium. Pineiro yielded four hits and a walk, striking out five. Only two A's reached scoring position as Pineiro used his sinker to produce 14 ground-ball outs, needing only 98 pitches to record his sixth career shutout and first with the Angels. Pineiro is 1-1 with a 1.13 ERA and 0.88 WHIP in two career starts against the Cardinals. He's 13-8 with a 3.29 ERA in 29 appearances, 28 as a starter, at Busch Stadium.
summary: 2010-05-21 - Los Angeles Angels (5) @ St. Louis Cardinals (9) (Final)

away_pitcher_note: Kazmir logged a season-high seven innings Monday night against the Rangers, but lost his third consecutive start, 4-3. With the loss, Kazmir has allowed four or more runs for the fourth time in seven starts this season. So far this season, Kazmir is 0-3 with a 7.59 ERA in road starts. Against the National League, Kazmir owns a lifetime record of 5-3 with a 4.83 ERA in 13 starts. His only other career start against St. Louis came in 2005, when he allowed two runs in four innings and did not earn the decision in a 6-4 loss while with Tampa Bay.
summary: 2010-05-22 - Los Angeles Angels (10) @ St. Louis Cardinals (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter is coming off his longest start in terms of pitches since 2006, and he's pitching on regular rest. It will be intriguing to see how he fares, though he has said repeatedly this year that he feels stronger than he has in years. After handling Carpenter quite gently last year, the Cardinals seem to be pushing him a little more in 2010. If he responds well on regular rest after 118 pitches, it will be very good news for Carpenter and the team.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver matched his shortest outing of the season Tuesday night against the Rangers, lasting just 4 2/3 innings and picking up a no-decision in an 8-7 loss. He gave up seven runs on seven hits while striking out just one. Weaver is now 1-2 with a 4.56 ERA in his last four starts. He's only made one career start against St. Louis, when he pitched three innings while giving up three runs on five hits on June 10, 2007. He didn't factor into the decision in a 9-6 loss. Weaver is 6-3 with a 3.41 ERA in 11 starts against the National League.
summary: 2010-05-23 - Los Angeles Angels (5) @ St. Louis Cardinals (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Garland picked up his fifth victory of the season in his last start against the Dodgers, even though he labored through a season-high 117 pitches, 75 for strikes. Through the first two innings, after which the Dodgers led, 3-1, he had thrown 56 pitches. But the Padres rallied and made a winner of him against his former team. "They're definitely a hot team right now. You can tell by their at-bats; they're sitting on really good pitches, they're fouling off pitchers' pitches," Garland said of the Dodgers. "They're a tough team right now. It was a grind. I don't think they swung and missed one time. Pretty wild."
away_pitcher_note: With at least one and maybe two starters on the disabled list, the Cardinals need co-aces Wainwright and Chris Carpenter more than ever. For the time being, they'll pitch on an every-fifth-day pattern even with off-days on the schedule, because their services are required. Wainwright has never started in PETCO Park, with his only regular-season appearance there being a one-inning relief showing in May of 2006.
summary: 2010-05-25 - St. Louis Cardinals (0) @ San Diego Padres (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Correia took the loss in his previous start, against the Dodgers, allowing four runs on seven hits in six innings. Correia was on target for the first five innings, allowing the Dodgers just one run, the same number L.A. starter Clayton Kershaw allowed in his 7 1/3 innings. The Dodgers' sixth frame started with a single from Matt Kemp, who took second base on the first of the Padres' throwing mistakes. Correia's pickoff throw went well out of the reach of first baseman Adrian Gonzalez and rebounded off the side railing.  It was deja vu. In his last outing, on Saturday against the Dodgers, a Correia error on a pickoff throw resulted in two Dodgers runs.
away_pitcher_note: He's been as good as anybody in the National League, rookie or not. Garcia throws four pitches, but the most noteworthy this year has been a nasty slider. He can throw it for a strike and he can throw it for a chase pitch, and it's complemented his bread-and-butter sinker/curveball combination beautifully. Garcia also throws a changeup, giving him an impressively full arsenal for a rookie hurler. At some point he'll likely come to earth at least a little bit, but for now Garcia has been brilliant.
summary: 2010-05-26 - St. Louis Cardinals (1) @ San Diego Padres (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: LeBlanc, who had become one of the most reliable and consistent performers in the starting rotation, struggled from the outset of his last outing against the Mariners, allowing eight earned runs in three innings. "The life on his pitches isn't where we've seen it. It's a good learning experience for him that this can happen," Padres manager Bud Black said. LeBlanc, who had allowed six earned runs over his first six starts this season, surrendered seven runs in the second inning to Seattle, a team that has struggled mightily with scoring runs all season. LeBlanc said that in that pivotal second inning, he got away from being aggressive.
away_pitcher_note: Walters assumes the spot vacated by Brad Penny after Penny was placed on the 15-day disabled list with a right lat strain. In the corresponding roster move, Walters was recalled from Triple-A Memphis on Saturday and pitched four scoreless innings of relief in Anaheim.  Thursday will be Walters' second stint as a fill-in starter with the club. He made one start last season and allowed three runs over four innings at Chicago while appearing in nine games total and posting a 9.56 ERA.
summary: 2010-05-27 - St. Louis Cardinals (8) @ San Diego Padres (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note:
Wells did not get a decision in his last start against the Rangers but had a stellar outing. 
He gave up three runs on seven hits and went 8 1/3 innings, his longest outing of the year. 
Wells also struck out six. He's learning -- he was able to work quickly, get ahead of 
batters and the only mistakes were two pitches, which Vladimir Guerrero and Nelson Cruz both 
launched out of the Ballpark at Arlington.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter was let off the hook in his last start after allowing five runs, four earned, on eight hits over six innings against Anaheim. The team rallied for an extra-inning victory on a walk-off hit by Felipe Lopez, thus removing Carpenter from the decision. Two home runs spoiled Carpenter's outing, although he said afterward that his command felt good. He walked two and struck out four and has surrendered nine home runs so far this season after giving up only seven all of last year.

home_pitcher_note:
Silva is off to his best start ever at 6-0. He picked up his last win over the Rangers, 
giving up three runs on six hits in 5 1/3 innings. It was a short start, primarily because 
of the heat and humidity. The more Silva wins, the more confident he gets. He's already 
picked up more "W's" in his first nine starts than he did in 34 starts the last two years 
with Seattle.
away_pitcher_note: This is the spot that Kyle Lohse would normally occupy, but Lohse was placed on the 15-day disabled list on Thursday and will undergo forearm surgery on Friday in Los Angeles.  No timetable has been set for his return. Right-hander Adam Ottavino will be called up to make the start in Chicago. Ottavino last pitched on Monday for the Redbirds and picked up the victory after allowing one run over five innings. In eight starts with Memphis this season, Ottavino has gone 4-3 with a 4.17 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster will close the Cubs' six-game homestand and hopes to end the way he started it. Last Tuesday, he threw eight shutout innings and snapped a personal four-game losing streak in the Cubs' 3-0 win over the Dodgers. Dempster was able to avoid the one bad inning that has snuck up on him this season. Last year, he was 0-1 with a 3.33 ERA in four starts against the Cardinals. He's 6-6 with a 4.35 ERA in his career against St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: The Cardinals will be looking for a little justice for Wainwright, who was a very hard-luck loser his last time out. Three times this season, Wainwright has allowed one or two runs in a start and the Cardinals have lost. He hasn't always pitched well at Wrigley, but he also hasn't made many starts there. There's no reason to think he can't succeed just as much at the Friendly Confines as he has everywhere else.

home_pitcher_note: Monday brings an interesting challenge for Garcia: it will mark the first time this season that a team has seen him twice. That may not matter for the rookie lefty, who has an impressive array of pitches and confidence in all of them. But typically, the more that hitters see a pitcher, the more they benefit. It will be interesting to watch whether Garcia or the Reds adjust more successfully. Garcia held them to two runs in 6 1/3 innings at Great American Ball Park earlier this month.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo has won four starts in a row and hasn't lost since April 23 in San Diego. He's 5-0 in his last six starts with a 2.66 ERA. On May 16 against the Cardinals, he threw his first complete game of the season, allowing two runs and seven hits in a 7-2 Reds win. He has started more games (22) against the Cardinals than any other team and is 7-8 in those starts.

home_pitcher_note: Walters did enough to earn a second start when he tossed five shutout innings in San Diego. He doesn't overpower hitters, but he has a feel for what he's trying to do and he gets hitters to chase pitches out of the strike zone. He'll once again be pitching in a friendly ballpark, though the opponent will be a little more potent than the Padres. Walters recorded his first big league win in his previous start.
away_pitcher_note: Despite a blister that developed on his index finger in his start on May 22, Cueto continues to be one of the hottest pitchers in baseball. In his last outing on Thursday, he threw six scoreless innings to lead the Reds over the Pirates. The blister affected his slider, but he's expected to be fully ready in St. Louis. With that win, he's now 5-0 with a 1.85 ERA in his past six starts. After going 0-2 against the Cardinals in 2008, he's 3-0 in his last five starts against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Teammate Ryan Ludwick said it best after Carpenter shut down the Cubs at Wrigley Field on Friday: "When he's on, he's unhittable. When he's off, he's still pretty unhittable." Carpenter hasn't been really on that many times this season, but he's been extremely effective. And he feels like he's steadily getting better, refining his command and seeing improvement on his cut fastball. If there's another level for Carpenter to take his production, look out.
away_pitcher_note: Backed by an offensive outburst, LeCure allowed just two runs in six innings to pick up a win in his Major League debut on Friday against the Astros. The start in St. Louis will be his second appearance in place of the injured Homer Bailey. The 2005 fourth-round Draft pick spent the beginning of the season at Triple-A Louisville, where he compiled a 5-2 record with a 2.55 ERA in nine starts and was named International League Pitcher of the Week before getting called up.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright has yet to throw fewer then six innings in a start this season and is averaging just over seven frames per game. Good news for a stretched bullpen that could use the day off and a strong start from Wainwright to reset itself. With Wainwright striking out almost one batter per inning, there should be plenty of swings and misses for Milwaukee batters, currently in the bottom ten of the Majors for K's.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf has been struggling with his command all season, and now he's struggling to get on the same page with his catcher. Rookie Jonathan Lucroy has had a difficult time picking up Wolf's complicated set of signs with runners on base, leading to a series of mound visits during the pair's two games together. Manager Ken Macha would prefer to save his slightly more experienced catcher, George Kottaras, for his less-experienced pitchers, so Wolf and Lucroy will probably stay together for at least one more turn. More concerning is Wolf's uncharacteristically high walk count; he issued 2.4 free passes per nine innings for the Dodgers last season and has walked 4.5 batters per nine innings this year.

home_pitcher_note: Missing Kyle Lohse and Brad Penny from the rotation, the Cardinals need another starter to step up and help carry the load after Chris Carpenter, Adam Wainwright and Jaime Garcia. With rookie P.J. Walters scuffling to the tune of seven earned runs on Tuesday night, the burden falls on Ottavino to help spare the bullpen from covering five innings at a time. Walking six batters in his only start of the season, Ottavino must nail down his location against a tough Brewers offense.
away_pitcher_note: Narveson was humming along through five scoreless innings against the Marlins on Memorial Day, with eight strikeouts and only two singles against him. But things unraveled in a hurry for the lefty, who surrendered a game-tying three-run home run to Cody Ross amid a seven-run Florida rally, with five of those runs charged to Narveson. In the Cardinals, Narveson will be facing the team that drafted him (in 2000) and first brought him to the big leagues (in 2006). He's already made seven appearances against them for the Brewers, including two starts, and has a 2.25 ERA in those games.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia's remarkable start to the season came with one major caveat: how would he handle facing a team that has seen his stuff before? Garcia passed the first part of the challenge, limiting Cincinnati hitters in his second go-round with the Reds despite lacking his "A" game. Ranking No. 2 in the Majors in runs scored, Milwaukee's righty-dominated lineup will prove a sizeable test for Garcia's ability to adjust to hitters who are already making adjustments to him.
away_pitcher_note: Parra gets the nod over a surprised Dave Bush, who expressed some confusion after being informed this week that his turn was being skipped. The Brewers would like a look at Parra and it makes some sense to feature him against the Cardinals, who as of Thursday were batting .243 with a .674 OPS against left-handed pitchers and .272 with a .782 OPS against righties. Bush is 2-6 with a 6.45 ERA in nine career starts against St. Louis including 0-3 with a 10.57 ERA at Busch Stadium. Compare that to Parra, who is 2-1 with a 2.97 ERA in 12 games, including 10 starts, against the Cardinals and is 2-0 with a 2.86 ERA in five starts at Busch Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Monasterios' last outing Wednesday was cut short after five innings because of a finger blister, but he is still in line to start Monday in the opener of a three-game series against the Cardinals -- as long as his bullpen session on Saturday goes as planned. The rookie right-hander is 2-0 with a 1.87 ERA in 14 appearances, only three of which have been starts. He has yet to go more than five innings, but he's also yet to take a loss.
away_pitcher_note: The Cardinals have yet to announce whether Hawksworth or P.J. Walters will get this start, and in either case, manager Tony La Russa has said he will view it as a "bullpen game." It would appear that Hawksworth may have the edge, though, for one reason: Walters is the incumbent, having already made two starts. If he were getting the call for a third time, it doesn't seem that the club would hesitate to say as much. If Hawksworth is the choice, it will be his first big league start.
summary: 2010-06-07 - St. Louis Cardinals (4) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (12) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda's one career start against the Cardinals, on July 30, 2009, went well: he let up four hits and two runs in six innings, striking out five and walking none. Matt Holliday's 14 career at-bats against Kuroda? Those haven't gone as well. Holliday is 7-for-14 with two doubles, a home run and six RBIs against Kuroda lifetime and has struck out once. Kuroda rebounded in his last start on Thursday, going six and allowing four runs, three earned to the Braves. The start before, he had let up seven runs, five earned, in four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter recorded what may have been his finest outing of the season last Wednesday against the Reds. Pitching eight strong innings, allowing four hits to go with a solitary run, Carpenter effectively worked both sides of the plate to keep the Cincinnati hitters frustrated all game. With a career 2.20 ERA in six starts against the Dodgers and a perfect 5-0 record when facing L.A., Carpenter appears primed for another dominant outing.
summary: 2010-06-08 - St. Louis Cardinals (0) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Were it not for a five-inning start on May 30, Kershaw would have six consecutive quality starts in a row. He allowed three earned runs in 6 2/3 innings to the Braves in his last outing Friday, the first time he had allowed more than two runs in a start since May 4. Kershaw's walks and strikeouts have both been up over his last two starts: he's walked nine and struck out 17. None of the Cardinals have homered off Kershaw, but Matt Holliday is 4-for-10 and Albert Pujols is 4-for-7 with two doubles lifetime.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright returns to the site of some of his most memorable outings. Back in 2007, he got knocked around at Dodger Stadium in a game that he considered a major turning point in his career. Two years later, he pitched absolutely brilliantly in a playoff game at Chavez Ravine but came away with nothing to show for it after Los Angeles rallied in the ninth. This time around, the Cardinals mostly need innings, since two of their regular starters are on the disabled list.
summary: 2010-06-09 - St. Louis Cardinals (3) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Sunday against Ubaldo Jimenez and the Rockies, Lopez allowed three runs on nine hits over seven innings; he struck out six in defeat. If nothing else, the veteran right-hander has kept his team in ballgames. He posted his second consecutive quality start on Sunday. Part of the reason he hasn't won since May 15 is simply competition: Lopez has had to face with some of the game's best hurlers, including Jimenez, Tim Lincecum, Tommy Hanson and others. His likely Cardinals counterpart, Jaime Garcia, is no slouch either, so Lopez will have to be extra fine with his pitches to stay in contention. The veteran right-hander is 2-1 with a 5.25 ERA in four career starts versus St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia was solid yet again on Sunday when he limited the Brewers to just two earned runs over six innings. He did allow eight hits and two walks but was able to keep his composure and pitched out of a few jams. Friday will mark Garcia's first career start against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Haren wasn't quite as good Monday as he was in his previous start, when he shut out the Dodgers for eight innings, but he wasn't half-bad either. The D-backs' ace allowed three runs on nine hits over 5 2/3 innings, finishing his outing one out short of Arizona's eighth straight quality start. In his next start, Haren will be seeking his first second-straight win since proving victorious on April 20 and 26. Saturday, he faces the St. Louis Cardinals, which drafted him in the second round of the 2001 First-Year Player Draft. In three career starts against his former club, Haren is 3-0 with a 4.29 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Ottavino was effective against the Brewers on Saturday, allowing two runs on five hits over five innings but was stuck with a no-decision in just his second carer big league start. It marked an improvement over his first start, however, as he allowed four runs and six walks over 5 2/3 innings against the Cubs in his debut on May 29. The rookie right-hander has never faced the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: One start after dominating the Dodgers (nine shutout innings), Jackson was only so-so Tuesday night against the Braves. While he did keep the D-backs in the game, Arizona's No. 2 starter allowed four runs on nine hits over six innings. A sign of Jackson's endurance: He had pitched at least seven innings in four straight starts prior to Tuesday. The right-hander is also doing a better job of keeping the ball in the park: He hasn't allowed a home run in three consecutive outings after yielding seven June dingers. Jackson faces St. Louis next; he allowed four runs on seven hits over eight innings in an April 21 no-decision opposing the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter was in a groove against the Dodgers on Monday when he tossed seven scoreless innings but was stuck with a no-decision as the Cardinals were shut out for the sixth time this season. Carpenter, though, said his cutter is starting to come around and is feeling better than he did earlier in the season, and the stats certainly prove it as he is 2-0 with a 0.83 ERA dating back to May 28. He is 4-0 with a 2.09 ERA in nine career appearances (eight starts) against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright didn't have his best stuff against the Dodgers on Wednesday, when he allowed four runs on eight hits over six innings, along with a season-high five walks and six strikeouts. He uncharacteristically struggled with his control and needed 113 pitches to get through those six innings. Wainwright has never faced the Mariners in his six-year career with the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander acquired from the Tigers last season for Jarrod Washburn makes his first start of this season, mostly because of the ineffectiveness of right-hander Ian Snell, winless in five decisions. French started the season at Triple-A Tacoma, where he was used primarily as a starter.  He replaced Snell in the second inning against the Rangers last Wednesday and was impressive enough to get a shot in the Seattle rotation. He relies on location and changing speeds. This will be French's first career start against the Cardinals and the only player on the St. Louis roster he has faced is Matt Holiday, who walked. French also could get his first career at-bat.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan has to be activated first, but he will be, and then he'll get this start. He's struggled this year, but the bar is pretty low after some less-than-satisfying outings by fill-in Cardinals starters recently. His velocity has remained intact, so the question is location. Then again, with Suppan, the question is always location. If he can be even passable, giving the Cardinals six decent innings on a semi-regular basis, they'll be pleased.
away_pitcher_note: Perhaps a start against a National League team will help Rowland-Smith get his winless season turned around. Encouraged by a strong outing against the Angels on June 5, when he surrendered just one run over five innings, the lefty from Australia was rocked for 11 hits and eight runs (four earned) in a loss to the Rangers in Arlington. Two of the hits were home runs, the 11th and 12th off Rowland-Smith, this season. In 51 2/3 innings, Rowland-Smith has walked 22 and struck out 22, a ratio that has worked against him big-time. He has never faced the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia needs to regain the efficiency that marked his early starts. It's doubly important now with the club dealing with a battered back of the starting rotation. Every time Garcia runs his pitch count up in five innings, it puts strain on the bullpen. He can be a little more aggressive, but he's also finding hitters laying off his offspeed stuff more, so he'll need to adjust to that. He's still getting outs and putting up zeroes, so it's not a bad problem to have, but the Cards would still benefit from improvement from the rookie.
away_pitcher_note: The unsung left-hander continues to pitch well in his first injury-free season in several years. In 11 starts since being hit hard in his first outing of the campaign, Vargas has yielded three or fewer runs each time and given the team a chance to win. He's not overpowering, striking out 49 in 76 2/3 innings, but he works both sides of the plate and utilizes a superb changeup to keep hitters off-balance. He has pitched at least six innings in 10 of his 12 starts this season. Vargas has faced six Cardinals who are a combined 8-for-25 (.320) against him with no home runs.

home_pitcher_note: Through no fault of his own, the Cardinals have lost Carpenter's past two starts. He allowed three runs in 13 innings and struck out 13 over those two games, and didn't take the loss himself either time. But still, St. Louis must seize the opportunity whenever Carpenter pitches, since the back end of its rotation remains somewhat unsettled. Carpenter has a 2.16 ERA and has averaged more than seven innings per start at home this year.
away_pitcher_note: A's manager Bob Geren said he would like to keep Mazzaro on five days' rest as he gets acclimated to the starting rotation, moving Ben Sheets' scheduled start back to Saturday. Mazzaro made his second start since replacing the injured Brett Anderson on Sunday, in a 6-2 loss to the Giants. The 23-year-old righty tossed six innings, allowing four runs (three earned) on six hits and a walk while striking out one. He is now 0-4 with a 4.66 ERA in four career Interleague starts.

home_pitcher_note: After a somewhat uncharacteristic start at Dodger Stadium, Wainwright looked more like himself his last time out. Which is to say he looked like one of the National League's best pitchers.
