He's been absolutely brilliant at home this year, going 6-0 with a 1.96 ERA in six starts at Busch Stadium, and he's averaged 7 2/3 innings per game in those starts. Against the less-than-imposing A's offense, he should be in line for another excellent outing.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets will receive two extra days of rest this week before facing the Cardinals for the 27th time in his career. During his eight-year tenure with Milwaukee, Sheets struggled against St. Louis, the only team to hand him double-digit losing decisions. For his career, Sheets is 6-14 with a 4.05 ERA against the Cardinals. In his last start against the Giants on June 12, Sheets went six innings, allowing five runs (three earned) on eight hits and three walks while striking out two. He has now completed at least six innings in each of his last eight starts and in 11 of his 14 outings on the year.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan's second assignment as a Cardinal provides him another opportunity, as he'll again face one of the less-potent offenses in the game. He'll also again get to start at friendly Busch Stadium. If he can replicate his first start, in which he held Seattle to one run in four innings, but make it last a little bit longer, the Cardinals will be thrilled. They're not looking for him to be a world-beater, just to be a decent pitcher who eats up some innings. This start will give another indication whether he's ready to be that pitcher.
away_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old righty won his fifth straight decision on Tuesday, coming in a 9-5 win at Wrigley Field against the Cubs. Cahill went 5 2/3 innings, allowing four earned runs on six hits and two walks while striking out five. In his past six starts, Cahill is 5-0 with a 2.56 ERA. Over 38 2/3 innings of work in that span, Cahill has struck out 25 while allowing 30 hits and 15 walks. Cahill is 3-0 with a 1.75 ERA in four home starts this season, compared to 3-2 with a 4.29 ERA in six road outings.

home_pitcher_note: One pitch derailed an otherwise solid outing for Cecil on Tuesday in San Diego, sending the lefty to his first loss since May 8. Cecil logged six innings, during which he allowed seven hits and five runs, though four came on a second-inning grand slam from Padres outfielder Aaron Cunningham. Prior to that start, Cecil had gone 5-0 with a 1.49 ERA in his previous five starts. He is 0-1 with a 7.31 ERA in his career in Interleague Play but has never faced the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia got things sorted out his last time out, regaining the efficiency that marked his first few starts. When he throws his fastball for strikes early in the count, it sets up everything else he does -- particularly, it sets him up to use his slider as a put-away pitch. The interesting question will be whether Garcia can continue to keep the ball in the park. He's allowed two homers all year, while Toronto leads the Majors in long balls by a long way.
summary: 2010-06-22 - St. Louis Cardinals (9) @ Toronto Blue Jays (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Romero has bounced back nicely following his seven-run mishap against the Angels on May 25. In his four starts since that road start, the left-hander has gone 2-1 with a 2.25 ERA for the Jays, striking out 24 and walking 10 over 28 innings. On Wednesday in San Diego, Romero earned a win despite not featuring his best stuff. He allowed one run (none earned) on five hits over six innings. Romero has gone 3-1 with a 2.53 ERA in five career Interleague starts, compiling 32 strikeouts in 32 innings. He has never faced the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter returns to the city where he began his Major League career. It's also the place where he pitched possibly his best game as a Cardinal, a one-hit shutout in Interleague Play in June of 2005. The right-hander has been susceptible to the long ball at times this year, so he'll need to keep the ball down against a powerful Toronto lineup. Since joining the Cardinals, Carpenter is 3-3 with a 5.10 ERA in American League parks.
summary: 2010-06-23 - St. Louis Cardinals (1) @ Toronto Blue Jays (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Morrow has shown steady improvement since opening the season with a 6.80 ERA over his first nine starts. In five outings since then, the right-hander has gone 1-1 with a 2.32 ERA, limiting hitters to a .196 average along the way. Unfortunately, Morrow has also received an average of just 2.8 runs of support during that strong stretch. On Friday against the Giants, Morrow yielded two runs on five hits over six innings en route to no-decision. He is 0-3 with a 4.62 ERA in 19 career Interleague games, but has never faced the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright has been dominant at home, and merely excellent on the road. All four of his 2010 losses have come away from Busch Stadium, and his ERA on the road is more than a run higher than it is at home. Of course, that 2.78 road mark would still be one of the best in baseball, so it's not like he's struggled. Still, facing a designated hitter adds an extra challenge, though it's one Wainwright will likely meet with aplomb. He's allowed more than two earned runs only four times in 15 starts this year.
summary: 2010-06-24 - St. Louis Cardinals (0) @ Toronto Blue Jays (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Greinke's last outing wasn't quite up to his season best, on June 13 at Cincinnati (12 strikeouts, 7-3 complete-game victory) but he was pretty sharp again last Saturday at Atlanta. He went seven innings and gave up four runs (three earned) on six hits and had no decision in a 5-4 Royals loss. Greinke issued no walks for the second straight game, indicating he's regained his pinpoint control after some lapses earlier this season. He's still got some catching up to do in the victory column. Against St. Louis, Greinke is 2-2 in five games.
summary: 2010-06-25 - St. Louis Cardinals (2) @ Kansas City Royals (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Davies suffered a control breakdown in his last start, at Atlanta, walking three in the Braves' four-run first inning. He issued seven bases on balls in all but no more runs, adroitly dodging out of trouble as he pitched into the fifth inning before needing relief help. The Royals took him off the hook with a comeback but Davies' ERA went to its highest point this season. After seemingly conquering his control woes with just six walks in five starts, he's issued 14 in his last three outings. Davies is 1-3 in four starts against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: This is really a "bullpen game" for the Cardinals. Hawksworth has been stretched out enough that if things go well, he could go four innings or so. But if he struggles, the hook is likely to be quick, with Adam Ottavino at the ready to pitch several innings as well. This game highlights one issue facing the Cardinals right now: there's just not a clear choice as the fifth starter as long as Brad Penny remains out. Hawksworth and Ottavino will try to earn some of the staff's confidence.
summary: 2010-06-26 - St. Louis Cardinals (5) @ Kansas City Royals (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Chen pitched very well, giving up just three hits in six innings, but two of the blows were solo home runs that translated into a 2-1 loss to the Nationals on Monday night. His command wasn't real sharp in the early going, and he wound up with four walks, but none of them were converted into runs. Chen has given the Royals a real lift as the replacement for sore-shouldered Gil Meche. In five starts, Chen stands 2-2, carrying over the success he had in relief (1-0, one save, 2.89 ERA. Against the Cardinals, he's 0-3 with a 5.71 ERA in eight games.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia rebounded from a tough 2-1 loss to the Seattle Mariners despite equaling his career high of seven strikeouts on June 16 to beat the Toronto Blue Jays, 9-4, at Rogers Centre on June 22. In winning in his first career appearance against the Blue Jays, who lead the Majors in homers, the rookie allowed a home run to Jose Bautista on a 3-0 pitch in the second. He said he wasn't expecting a swing on that count and made his fastball too hittable. He allowed three earned runs for the first time this season. He hadn't allowed more than two earned runs in his previous 13 starts. The six-inning effort against the Blue Jays was his 12th quality start. Garcia allowed the Blue Jays six hits but no walks while striking out four in making 89 pitches. He has never faced the Royals and is 1-1 with a 3.46 ERA in two Interleague starts. Left-handers bat .183 against him and right-handers .231.
summary: 2010-06-27 - St. Louis Cardinals (3) @ Kansas City Royals (10) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter was again brilliant against the team that drafted him and developed him, the Toronto Blue Jays, when he faced them for the second time in his career on June 23. Carpenter who pitched a one-hit shutout against the Blue Jays at his first homecoming on June 14, 2005, earned a 1-0 victory with an eight-inning three-hitter. Carpenter had some trouble with his curveball early against Toronto, but survived admirably until the pitch came around for him. His only loss this year was to the Houston Astros on May 13. His two starts against Arizona this season were no-decisions, and he has a 4.15 ERA in those starts. He is 4-0 with a 2.36 ERA in his career against Arizona, which includes nine starts and one relief outing.
away_pitcher_note: Tuesday against the Yankees, Haren allowed three runs on six hits over seven innings. Despite pitching well, he suffered his second straight defeat. The D-backs' No. 1 pitcher continues to be a strike-thrower: In five June starts, he's whiffed 33 and walked six. Next, Haren will face St. Louis, his original team, for the third time this season. He is 2-0 versus the Cardinals this season despite the fact that he's allowed nine earned runs in 14 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright lasted four innings in taking the loss to the Jays on June 24. He had gone 51 starts in which he had lasted at least five innings. His shortest start before the one at Rogers Centre was also four innings -- Sept. 13, 2008, at Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Willis doesn't seem to be improving in a D-backs uniform; he seems to be declining. Wednesday against the Yankees, Willis lasted 2 1/3 innings. He threw 66 pitches; just 27 were strikes. He exited the game having allowed two runs on one hit and seven free passes.

home_pitcher_note: Little by little, Suppan gets closer to what the Cardinals are expecting. St. Louis is not asking the veteran right-hander to be a world-beater, just an innings-eater. In three games as a Cardinal, Suppan has done a decent job of keeping the ball on the ground.
away_pitcher_note: Enright will have his contracted selected from Double-A Mobile to make the start. A second-round pick in 2007, the right-hander was 4-1 with a 2.88 ERA in 14 starts for Mobile this season. Enright is known for having pinpoint command.

home_pitcher_note: Hawksworth wowed the Redbirds with an outstanding start on Saturday in a game that was considered more a "bullpen start" than a proper start by Hawksworth. He was good enough to pitch himself into another start, and this time the expectations will be higher.
away_pitcher_note: Last time out, the Brewers looked to veteran lefty Randy Wolf to help guide them to a sixth consecutive win. Unfortunately for Wolf and the Brewers, the lefty fell victim to the home run ball, giving up two, including the eventual game-winner in the 5-4 loss to Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off his rockiest start of the year, Garcia will be looking to regain his command. Last time out, he simply couldn't locate, and he didn't get a single swing-and-miss. If he gets ahead in counts against Milwaukee, the swings-and-misses should follow.
away_pitcher_note: Narveson simulated the first two batters he would face in the bullpen before his last start to shake the struggles that accounted for a 12.27 first-frame ERA this season. He responded by going out and turning in a career-best performance for his seventh win of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter's command may not be quite as pinpoint as it was a year ago. His velocity is down a tick from a year ago. But he simply doesn't lose. Over the last 12 months, a span of 34 starts, Carpenter is 21-2 with a 2.41 ERA. The Cardinals are 26-8 in those games.
away_pitcher_note: Parra said he hoped to go seven innings and give the team a chance to win every time out, but he came up short of a quality start again in his last start, by one inning and one run. He took a no-decision, however, as the bullpen had its worst performance in nearly a month.

home_pitcher_note: As expected, Wainwright's Toronto slipup was a one-time deal. He remains one of the best and most consistent pitchers in baseball, not to mention dominant at home. Even against a familiar foe, his stuff, command and home-field advantage should add up to another fine game.
away_pitcher_note: After a shutout five days earlier, Gallardo did not have his best stuff last time out, allowing four runs on seven hits over six innings with two walks and five strikeouts. It was just the fourth time in 17 starts in 2010 that Gallardo has given up four or more earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: Francis had one of the worst games of his career Wednesday against the Padres (8 ER, 7 H, 3 IP) because he lost the ability to throw inside to right-handed hitters, throw srikes at all on the outside of the plate or sink his changeup. He believes it's an aberration.
away_pitcher_note: The Cardinals have yet to announce a Tuesday starter, but after Hawksworth threw a bullpen on Saturday, he's the guess. It could be Hawksworth, and it could be Jeff Suppan. Whichever one doesn't get the nod on Tuesday likely won't start until the weekend.

home_pitcher_note: Cook is 7-for-7 in quality starts this year for the Rockies at Coors Field, where he'll meet the Cardinals. He has a 3-0 record in Denver, while posting an 0-5 mark on the road. In a 7-3 win against the Giants on Thursday, he allowed three runs in 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia rebounded beautifully from a rough start when he last pitched, but the thin air of Denver will be a new challenge for him. He's been solid on the road but not as good as he's been in St. Louis (1.20 home ERA, 2.92 road).

home_pitcher_note: After his historic start, Jimenez has been ordinary -- 17 runs in 17 2/3 innings but without lost -- in his last three outings. Falling behind early and walking four led to a seven-run third against the Giants.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter didn't look like himself last time out, but he and the team insisted he was physically fine. The question came up because five days earlier, he was hit in the right forearm by a line drive. Carpenter is undaunted by Coors Field, with a 0.63 ERA in two starts there.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse has still yet to put everything together, but there were more things to like last time out. He threw lots of strikes, and when he got in trouble, he usually got out. Now he just needs not to get in trouble quite so often.
away_pitcher_note: Latos, a 14-game winner, was roughed up in his last start, allowing five runs in four innings in a loss to the Giants. It snapped his Major League record streak of 15 consecutive starts with five or more innings and two or fewer runs.
summary: 2010-09-17 - San Diego Padres (4) @ St. Louis Cardinals (14) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Suppan gets a spot start that could become more. Jaime Garcia is being skipped for at least one start as the Cardinals try to make sure he gets to the end of the year healthy. Suppan has been effective at home, with a 2.67 ERA at Busch Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Young will make his second start of the season and his first since April 6. He's been on the disabled list since with a strained right shoulder. He's emerged healthy after three Minor League rehab starts.
summary: 2010-09-18 - San Diego Padres (8) @ St. Louis Cardinals (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright still has a chance at both 20 wins and a Cy Young Award, but he needs to get righted in order for that to happen. He's had an odd month, allowing 13 runs in three September starts but racking up 21 strikeouts against two walks.
away_pitcher_note: Garland was exceptional in his last start against the Rockies, allowing four hits over seven scoreless innings. He got 12 groundouts and won for the first time in four starts, a good sign for the Padres, who are in a pennant race.
summary: 2010-09-19 - San Diego Padres (1) @ St. Louis Cardinals (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Volstad is returning from a six-game suspension, and the right-hander will be making his 28th start. He has 153 1/3 total innings, which is approaching his career-most 159 in 2009. He is 4-4 with a 4.02 ERA at home this year.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter checked out just fine after his last start, and that was a relief to the Cardinals. He experienced cramping in his hamstring after he tumbled while backing up a play. But Carpenter was cleared and is on track to start the makeup game.

home_pitcher_note: For the sixth time this season, Maholm made a start that lasted fewer than four innings. This time, though, it wasn't his entire fault. Two errors behind him led to five unearned runs in seven-run fourth that knocked Maholm out.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook is coming off his best start as a Cardinal, and his best start for anyone in a long time. His peripherals have been strong throughout his St. Louis tenure, so it should be no surprise that he finally got more zeroes on the scoreboard.

home_pitcher_note: For Morton, progress is coming in baby steps. He lasted only five innings in his last start, but he did push his ERA to its lowest point of the season. Morton is hoping that some delivery tweaks will make his pitches more deception.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse appears to be rounding into form, and he's won back-to-back starts for the first time since his first two starts of the 2009 season. In his most recent, he allowed three runs on seven hits in five innings to down the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Burres has gone 3-for-3 in the quality start department since being reinserted into the rotation. He's walked just one in 20 innings and allowed four earned runs on 16 hits during that same span. He's become one of the club's most reliable arms.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan pitched well in his first start since Sept. 1 on Saturday, yielding one run in five innings to the Padres in a no-decision. He hurled 5 1/3 shutout innings in his only other start against the Pirates this year, on July 31.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny, hit on the left hand against the Pirates on Sept. 1, was recently cleared to rejoin the rotation. He originally was scheduled to pitch Wednesday against the Giants, but the club opted to give him more time.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright makes his first bid this year for win No. 20, and while he'd rather have a playoff bid, it's no secret that 20 is a meaningful number. Wainwright is 4-0 in four starts at Wrigley Field over the past three seasons.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Coleman's sixth start. In his last outing vs. the Marlins, he gave up three runs on five hits over six innings and earned the win. Coleman has gained confidence with every outing and is a candidate for next year's rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter had been breezing for much of the second half, but he's had some tough results of late. He's allowed 15 earned runs over his past three starts. More specifically, he's allowed an inning of at least four runs in each of those games.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Samardzija's third start, and so far he's 2-0, with both wins coming on the road, including one in St. Louis Sept. 13. The right-hander threw 5 2/3 shutout innings against the Cardinals then, mixing up his pitches well.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook will be looking to right the ship after a rocky start in Pittsburgh. He needs to get back to throwing strikes; he's walked 11 men in his past three starts, as opposed to eight in his first seven games as a Cardinal.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse had been showing signs of progress, but he got knocked around in Pittsburgh in his last start. He has at most two more games to secure some kind of good feeling going into the offseason as he tries to salvage a frustrating year.
away_pitcher_note: Morton picked up his first win since May 5 in his last start, finally putting a bright spot on a tumultuous season. He allowed a season-low two runs in six innings, but more importantly, he did so being aggressive and trusting his abilities.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan will try to end his season on a high note as makes his final start. Suppan has pitched well down the stretch, going 1-0 with a 2.38 ERA over his last three starts. Last time out, he beat the Pirates for just his second win of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Burres lasted 2 1/3 innings against the Cardinals in his last start. Little went right. He struggled locating pitches down, which was the result of his arm and body not being in sync. Burres had allowed just four runs in his previous 20 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Walters will make his second September appearance. In his last outing, he was cuffed around for seven hits and five runs in four innings during a loss to Pittsburgh on Sept. 22, though he did strike out a season-best six batters.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald was wild in his last start on Friday against Houston. He tossed 80 pitches in four innings of work, his shortest outing since joining the Pirates on July 31. He was tagged for three runs on five hits and received a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter will try to finish his 13th big league season on a high note after recent struggles. Carpenter is 0-4 with a 7.17 ERA over his last four outings, and lasted just four innings in his last outing against the Cubs on Saturday.
away_pitcher_note:
Battling "extreme dead-arm" Hammel had to grind through five innings, allowing four runs on eight hits against the Giants on Saturday.
Things could have been worse, as he gave up three homers, but they were all solo shots.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook makes his final start of the season against the club that drafted him. He allowed five runs in 5 1/3 innings in his last start, but he's got a 2.42 ERA in four starts at Busch Stadium and a 2.25 ERA in two career starts against Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa had little margin for error against Matt Cain and the Giants on Sunday, and a two-run homer in the first inning was critical. Still, he's allowed three runs or fewer in 12 of his past 13 outings.

Jimenez gets his last shot at win No. 20 against the Cards, whom he beat on July 8 in Denver. Jimenez has not been as strong as he was in the first half, but, still, six of his eight losses this season have come when he's allowed three runs or fewer.

Rogers gets the spot start in the place of lefty Jeff Francis. Rogers, who has thrown out of the pen and in the starting rotation this season, tossed four innings of relief on Wednesday, allowing one run and striking out six.

home_pitcher_note: As Carpenter prepares for his sixth Opening Day start (fifth with St. Louis), he's more important to the club than ever. With Adam Wainwright out for the year, Carpenter will need to be in top form for the Cards to make the postseason.
away_pitcher_note: Stauffer gets his first Opening Day start as he was clearly the best starting pitcher in camp. Since allowing five runs in his first spring start, Stauffer allowed five runs over his final four starts, spanning 18 innings.
summary: 2011-03-31 - San Diego Padres (5) @ St. Louis Cardinals (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: A year further away from surgery, Westbrook would seem to be in position for a big year. He thrived in the National League after a midseason trade. Westbrook started the spring a bit slow, but got stronger as March went on.
away_pitcher_note: Richard, a 14-game winner a year ago, allowed seven earned runs on 11 hits in his final spring start against the Angels. Richard's velocity, after a sore shoulder early in camp, is fine and he's getting ground balls.
summary: 2011-04-02 - San Diego Padres (11) @ St. Louis Cardinals (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Garcia was pleased with his pitches at times in the spring, but for most of March, the results never really matched. A fine last Grapefruit League start, though, bred optimism for the second-year lefty.
away_pitcher_note: Moseley, signed as a free agent in December, gets the start as the Padres move into the regular season with Mat Latos on the disabled list. He had a 6.38 ERA, but is versatile enough to start or pitch in long relief.
summary: 2011-04-03 - San Diego Padres (0) @ St. Louis Cardinals (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Lohse was one of the best stories of spring, going all of the Grapefruit League season without issuing a walk. If he's back in form after struggling due to injury for more than a year and a half, it will be an enormous boost for St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: Back in the rotation after a dismal 2010 season, Morton is eager to seize the second chance. He was the Pirates' best pitcher all spring and will bring a changed arm angle and revitalized sinker to the mound with him now.

home_pitcher_note: McClellan finally won the job he's coveted for years, earning a spot in the Cardinals rotation with a superb spring. It remains to be seen how he'll hold up over a full season, but he pitched lights-out in the Grapefruit League.
away_pitcher_note: A left side injury cost McDonald two weeks of spring games, but the right-hander still hopes to be ready for this first start. McDonald likely won't be able to throw more than 100 pitches given his light spring workload.

home_pitcher_note: The bell rang, and Carpenter came out looking like himself. Carpenter had some iffy results during Grapefruit League play, but was sharp on Opening Day. The Cardinals have won Carpenter's last 13 starts against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: In terrible conditions, Correia provided the Pirates a strong six-inning start in his club debut on Opening Day. The Cubs did not have an extra-base hit off the right-hander, who threw 61 of his 92 pitches for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez's appearance in the home opener is somewhat fitting, since he closed last year's regular season by contributing five innings to the Giants' 3-0 victory over San Diego that clinched the NL West title.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook followed up an uneven spring with a shaky first start. He's still trying to refine his location, but that's not all that unusual for a pitcher who has often been a slow starter.
summary: 2011-04-08 - St. Louis Cardinals (4) @ San Francisco Giants (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: San Francisco's most consistent pitcher a year ago, Cain picked up where he left off last Saturday by blanking the Dodgers on five hits through six innings. Cain, who has cut down on walks in each of the previous two seasons, issued no free passes.
away_pitcher_note: A rough first month of Spring Training is totally forgotten for the second-year lefty. He pitched the season's first shutout and now faces the team against which he tossed the other shutout in his big league career.
summary: 2011-04-09 - St. Louis Cardinals (2) @ San Francisco Giants (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Considering that an auto accident prevented Zito from performing his usual between-starts routine before his inaugural 2011 outing, he pitched capably. Zito surrendered three first-inning runs before retiring 15 consecutive Dodgers batters.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse fell victim to one rough inning in his first start, but then something very encouraging happened: he rebounded and finished strong. He's healthy, and that means there's considerable optimism for Lohse going forward.
summary: 2011-04-10 - St. Louis Cardinals (6) @ San Francisco Giants (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Enright makes his first home start of the season vs. the team he had faced in his big league debut last June 30. Enright made an immediate impression in that Busch Stadium debut, holding the Cards to a run and four hits in five innings for a 4-2 win.
away_pitcher_note: McClellan will have a hard time topping his first start, when he tossed six very strong innings. Arizona is a tough place for pitchers, and it's been especially tough on McClellan in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga beat out Aaron Heilman for the fifth spot in the rotation. He was acquired in January from the Tigers in exchange for two Minor Leaguers. Galarraga got the win against the Cubs on Wednesday allowing four runs in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter will be looking for a little luck. He's turned in two fine starts, allowing three earned runs, but he hasn't gotten any help. The Cardinals are 0-2 behind him, scoring four runs in two games for their ace.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy started both Opening Day and the home opener for the D-backs. He matched his career high by tossing eight innings against the Reds on Friday. He had a good breaking ball and fanned nine, while walking just one.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook isn't where he wants to be yet, but he got a little closer in his second start. He still needs to refine his command, though -- Westbrook has walked nine batters in 10 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda stepped up big with the bullpen tired in San Diego, coming up just one out short of a complete-game shutout. He pitched to contact, kept his pitch count down and was very aggressive going after hitters.
away_pitcher_note: Through two starts, Garcia has been as impressive as any pitcher in baseball so far in 2011. He's throwing strikes and keeping the ball down, while amassing strikeouts at a prodigious rate. A rough spring is long forgotten.
summary: 2011-04-14 - St. Louis Cardinals (9) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Garland makes his 2011 debut after returning from a strained oblique muscle and his first missed start with an injury in 10 years. Garland was signed to be the fifth starter because of his durability. He was not sharp in his one Class A rehab start.
away_pitcher_note: A healthy Lohse is a huge boon for the Cardinals. His first two games show that he has a chance to be just as effective as he was in 2008, when he contended for All-Star honors.
summary: 2011-04-15 - St. Louis Cardinals (11) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw threw another gem at the Giants with 6 2/3 more scoreless innings. He's proving to be a young ace, showing a gritty competitiveness along with almost untouchable stuff that is now augmented by a developing slider and changeup.
away_pitcher_note: McClellan's difficult second start may have been more impressive than his clean first one. For him to pitch six effective innings in Arizona, at a park that's given him fits, shows what he's capable of as a starter.
summary: 2011-04-16 - St. Louis Cardinals (9) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley comes off another uneven start. He couldn't protect a three-run lead against the Giants and Tim Lincecum after cruising through the lineup the first time and has let leads get away in each of his three starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off one of the worst starts of his career, Carpenter will look to rebound against a team that has never beaten him in the regular season. Carpenter felt fine against Arizona; he simply couldn't locate.
summary: 2011-04-17 - St. Louis Cardinals (1) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Behind a Cards offense that strung together 17 hits, Westbrook got his first win of the season, going 5 1/3 innings, while giving up five runs (two earned). The righty struck out three and walked two.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan didn't pitch badly on Wednesday in a 3-2 loss to the Phillies, allowing three runs, two earned, on six hits. His only bad inning came in the fifth, when Lannan allowed two runs.

home_pitcher_note: Behind a Cards offense that strung together 17 hits, Westbrook got his first win of the season, going 5 1/3 innings, while giving up five runs (two earned). The righty struck out three and walked two.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan didn't pitch badly on Wednesday in a 3-2 loss to the Phillies, allowing three runs, two earned, on six hits. His only bad inning came in the fifth, when Lannan allowed two runs.

home_pitcher_note: Getting another win under his belt, Garcia gritted out five innings of work, giving up eight hits on three runs (two earned) in his last start. However, the eight hits Garcia surrendered equaled the total from his first two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann pitched arguably his best game since having Tommy John surgery in his most recent start. He had a perfect game through five innings, but Phillies left-hander Cliff Lee was better, blanking the Nationals, 4-0, on Thursday night.

home_pitcher_note: Tallying his 1,000th career strikeout and second win of the season against the Dodgers on Friday, Lohse went 7 1/3 innings, surrendering six hits, while walking one and striking out six.
away_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny was solid on the mound Friday, pitching six innings and allowing two runs on five hits. He struck out four hitters and walked two others. He picked up his first no-decision of the season.

home_pitcher_note: McClellan's new gig has been a roaring success. Through three starts, he's been absolutely outstanding, throwing strikes even as he allows more balls in the air. He's been quite successful against the Reds in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez's first-inning woes remain a big issue. The right-hander has frequently put the team in an early hole, which means more work for the bullpen. His first inning ERA is now 29.25, compared to a 1.93 ERA after the first.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter's just fine, it turns out. Though there were some worries after a rocky start in Arizona, Carpenter dismissed them, saying he just had a bad game. His next start, against the Dodgers, proved him right.
away_pitcher_note: The 3 1/3 innings Wood worked in Monday's 9-3 loss to the Pirates accounted for the shortest outing of his career. A 42-pitch first inning with lots of foul balls created a tough challenge.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook will be starting on short rest thanks to a rainout earlier in the week. He has made two such starts in his career, going 1-1 with a 5.19 ERA, though those were both on three days' rest after a relief outing.
away_pitcher_note: Dusty Baker didn't announce his starter for the series finale vs. the Cardinals until Sunday afternoon, when he declared he'd go with Volquez instead of scheduled starter Sam LeCure. Volquez is 1-1 with a 4.98 ERA in four career starts vs. St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: Norris was often in trouble against the Mets on Wednesday, but continually got out of it despite giving up 10 hits. The 26-year-old gave up three runs in six innings and even notched an RBI single against knuckleballer R.A. Dickey.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia has been effective, but the only real issue from his 2010 season -- inefficiency -- has been popping up again lately. He averaged more than 19 pitches per inning over his past two starts, thus he's only gone five innings in each.

home_pitcher_note: The Astros have lost three of Happ's four starts, including the last two. Happ was beaten Thursday in New York, allowing six hits and six runs in 4 2/3 innings. He is 1-2 with a 5.64 ERA in four starts against St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: It looks like 2008 all over again for Lohse, who's off to a brilliant start. He's coming off his sixth career shutout, and he's consistently pounding the strike zone. He's gone at least seven innings in every start this year.

home_pitcher_note: Figueroa has struggled, allowing 19 earned runs and 31 hits in 20 innings while losing all three of his decisions. His only quality start came April 16, when he held the Padres to six hits and two earned runs in 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Nothing seems to faze McClellan, most especially having runners on base. He's done a superb job of limiting the damage when he's gotten in trouble, and it's been a big key to his success this year.

home_pitcher_note: Tim Hudson threw 113 pitches and came within an out of notching a complete game while beating the Giants Saturday. While snapping a two-game losing streak, he avoided the first-inning woes that plagued him in previous four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter has received no-decisions in his last two starts, pitching seven innings against the Dodgers and six last Saturday vs. Cincinnati. His last decision was an April 12 loss at Arizona. He has 26 K's in 30 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Beachy has produced two impressive starts since experiencing one of the least impressive outings of his career on April 14.  The 24-year-old right-hander's recent success has come while he has shown better command with his slider.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook beat Cincinnati on Sunday in his last start, giving up only three hits and no earned runs in six innings. He has received a decision in four of five starts. Control has been his biggest problem, surrendering 16 walks in 24 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe has allowed two earned runs or fewer in 10 of his past 11 starts dating back to last September.  No longer relying too heavily on his sinker, he has increased his strikeout totals with the help of his slider.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia worked 5 1/3 innings in his previous start, giving up six hits and three earned runs Tuesday night at Houston. He struck out six and walked two. Garcia allowed his first home run of the season in that game, to Hunter Pence.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse may actually be better right now than he was at any point in his outstanding 2008. He's throwing strikes and getting deep into games, having gone at least seven innings in all five starts.
away_pitcher_note: The last time Volstad faced the Cardinals, he tossed a shutout on Sept. 20, 2010. The 6-foot-8 right-hander is coming off his best outing of the '11 season, allowing two runs in seven innings vs. the Dodgers. He struck out five.

home_pitcher_note: Even after his first rocky start, McClellan is undefeated with an ERA in the low 3.00's, which tells you how well he's pitching. One disconcerting trend: He has 10 strikeouts against nine walks over his past four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hits have been hard to come by off Sanchez. He carried a no-hitter into the ninth vs. the Rockies on April 22. Then he kept the Dodgers hitless for 3 1/3 innings. But he ended up with a no-decision, allowing three runs in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Cardinals finally won a game started by Carpenter, but the ace doesn't have a win on his own ledger yet. It's not because he's pitched poorly, though. Carpenter has quality starts in five of his six games.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez allowed two home runs on Friday after not giving up a homer in his previous three starts. Homers by Jay Bruce and Jeremy Hermida accounted for the four earned runs Vazquez allowed in six innings. Vazquez also went 2-for-2 with a walk.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook has been getting sharper lately, and he'll need to be at his best on Thursday. His opposite number is maybe the hottest pitcher in the league. Westbrook's command could still get finer, but he's progressing.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson gave up just five hits in seven innings on Saturday but was the victim of a blown save, preventing him from earning his fourth victory. Johnson walked two and struck out six. The five hits allowed were a season high.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia won three of his first four starts when he allowed a total of four earned runs. But he has allowed six earned runs over 11 1/3 innings in his last two outings, both no-decisions. He is 2-2 with a 3.90 ERA in his career vs. the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf is 3-0 in his past four games, all quality starts. He got a no-decision at Houston on Friday, but allowed just four hits and an earned run in seven innings. he has allowed only four earned runs in 33 2/3 innings over his last five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse had won four straight starts before getting roughed up Monday against Florida, when he allowed five earned runs on six hits over six innings and walked a season-high three. He is 3-6 with a 5.36 ERA in his career against Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo had better command through five innings in his last start, giving up only a homer by the Braves' David Ross. But he allowed four runs without getting an out in the sixth inning.

home_pitcher_note: McClellan's unbeaten start to the season ended when he allowed four earned runs on six hits over five innings against Florida. He will be making his first start vs. the Brewers, but has a 2.82 ERA in 22 1/3 innings in his career against them.
away_pitcher_note: Narveson is winless in four starts since pitching seven scoreless innings against the Cubs in a home victory on April 9. After allowing nine hits and no earned runs in his first two starts, he has allowed 24 hits and 17 earned runs in his last two.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano picked up the win in his last outing against the Dodgers, his 10th straight win on the road. He has yet to win at home this season in three starts. Against the Cardinals last year, Zambrano was 2-0 with a 2.03 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter is off to a rocky start in 2011 and has yet to record a win through his first seven outings. He got hit hard in his last start, on Wednesday vs. Florida, when he allowed six runs (four earned) in six frames and made two errors.

home_pitcher_note: Garza finally got his first hit in his last start with a leadoff single in the sixth. But he didn't get a win as he gave up five runs on six hits over six innings against the Reds. This will be his second career start vs. the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook is coming on strong, with three straight quality starts after four rough ones to start the year. He's thrown more strikes the last two games and is, of course, getting plenty of ground-ball outs.

home_pitcher_note: Coleman notched his first quality start in his last outing against the Reds. The difference? Two side sessions with pitching coach Mark Riggins, who tweaked his mechanics a bit, plus the addition of a four-seam fastball.
away_pitcher_note: At his best, Garcia is as good as anybody -- as evidenced by his two shutouts already this year. He needs to maintain his command and efficiency from start to start. If he does that, he'll find himself among the elite.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo gave the Reds a quality start against the Cubs on Saturday, allowing one earned run on seven hits in 7 1/3 innings. He was in line for the win until Chicago mounted a ninth-inning comeback.
away_pitcher_note: If you're looking for one number to sum up what Lohse is doing this year, this one is as good as any: He's thrown 67 percent of his pitches for strikes. Keep doing that, and it's going to be a very nice year.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto was impressive in his season debut on Sunday. Cueto, who spent the season's first month recovering from irritation in his right bicep and triceps, pitched six shutout frames against Chicago, allowing five hits and one walk while fanning four.
away_pitcher_note: McClellan is coming off his best start to date, a nice rebound after a couple of so-so outings. His strikeout-to-walk ratio remains unimpressive, but it's not stopping him from being effective.

home_pitcher_note: Wood seems to thrive in May. Or vs. the Astros. The southpaw is 1-0 and has surrendered two earned runs in 12 2/3 innings over his last two starts -- both against Houston. In three previous starts, Wood allowed 16 earned runs in 13 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter finally got his first win, but it's still been an up and down year. His stuff remains outstanding, but his command has been iffy at times. He's sure to be fired up for a game against the rival Reds.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook is coming off a disconcerting start in which took a step back after it appeared he had banished his early funk. The Phillies will present a good challenge for Westbrook, who struggled against them last June.
away_pitcher_note: Lee has pitched fairly well other than one start in Atlanta, but the problem lately has been a lack of run support. The Phillies had not scored a run while Lee was pitching in 27 innings before snapping it Wednesday in Florida.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia keeps impressing. In his last start, he wasn't at his sharpest but still battled through seven strong innings. If he can have games like that, succeeding while not at his best, he's going to have a huge year.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt is expected to make his first start since landing on the 15-day disabled list with lower back inflammation. He made a rehab start Thursday with Class A Clearwater with the expectation he would rejoin the rotation if he felt OK.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse is winless in his past three starts, but will get a chance to get back on track against Houston. In his only start vs. the Astros this season, Lohse threw seven innings of four-hit ball and kept Houston off the board.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Mets, Norris took a no-decision after allowing four earned runs in 7 1/3 innings. Norris has a 5-1 record in seven career starts against the Cardinals to go along with a 1.97 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: McClellan surrendered three home runs in his last outing and lost his first game of the year after starting 5-0. The right-hander will look to redeem himself after allowing five earned runs to the Astros on April 28.

away_pitcher_note: If the Cardinals have a must-win game, Carpenter is the man they want pitching. He scuffled on short rest in Game 2, but on full rest, there's no reason to think he can't be his best. He'll be facing an old friend in Roy Halladay.

away_pitcher_note: Jackson never seems fazed by anything, a trait that should help him in the NLCS. He was hit hard in his first start against Milwaukee as a Cardinal, but bounced back with two more good games against the Brewers.

away_pitcher_note: He didn't earn the victory, but Gallardo held the D-backs to one run over six innings in a must-win Game 5 of the NLDS, helping the Brewers win a postseason series for the first time since 1982.

away_pitcher_note: Wilson takes the ball in opener, his third straight playoff Game 1 start. In his one previous World Series start, he went six innings in Game 2 in 2010, giving up two runs on three hits for the loss. He's looking for his first win this postseason.

home_pitcher_note: The Game 2 starter is the only one who would pitch twice at Busch Stadium, as he would also be in line to start Game 6. Garcia was much more effective at home than on the road this year and last year. He was 9-4 with a 2.55 ERA at Busch this season.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis had his first subpar playoff start in Game 3 of the ALCS against Detroit, giving up four earned runs in 5 2/3 innings. Lifetime against the Cardinals, he has pitched just a single scoreless inning.

home_pitcher_note: Harrison is 1-0 with a 4.22 ERA in two playoff starts and one relief appearance, and opponents are hitting .225 off him. He has walked six and struck out 12 in 10 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse has a 7.45 ERA this postseason. With an 0-4 record and 5.09 ERA over his first eight postseason appearances dating back to 2002, he has the second-most career regular-season starts (298) of any active pitcher without a playoff victory.

home_pitcher_note: Holland started the Rangers' Game 6 win, which clinched their spot in the World Series. In the playoffs, he is 1-0 with a 5.27 ERA in 13 2/3 innings. He has never faced the Cardinals in his career.
away_pitcher_note: This could be interesting. Jackson is a flyball pitcher who will be pitching in a park that punishes flyball tendencies. However, Jackson has been effective in Arlington, with a 3.25 lifetime ERA there.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson opened the World Series by taking a loss, giving up three runs in 5 2/3 innings. The biggest blow came in the fourth inning, when Lance Berkman drove in two with a single. Wilson is 0-3 with a 7.17 ERA this postseason.
away_pitcher_note: It's a different challenge for Carpenter, but there's no one the Cards would rather have in a big game. He's been better at home than away, but not drastically so, and he keeps the ball down, which is critical in Arlington.

home_pitcher_note: The Cardinals set up their rotation in order for Garcia to get two home starts in the World Series. Now they hope to reap the benefits. He was brilliant at home this year, and pitched seven shutout innings at Busch in Game 2.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis pitched Game 2 in St. Louis and took a no-decision, going 6 2/3 innings and allowing one run. He was matched zero for zero by Jaime Garcia, who went seven scoreless innings. Lifetime in the World Series, Lewis is 1-0 with a 1.88 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The Cardinals set up their rotation in order for Garcia to get two home starts in the World Series. Now they hope to reap the benefits. He was brilliant at home this year, and pitched seven shutout innings at Busch in Game 2.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis pitched Game 2 in St. Louis and took a no-decision, going 6 2/3 innings and allowing one run. He was matched zero for zero by Jaime Garcia, who went seven scoreless innings. Lifetime in the World Series, Lewis is 1-0 with a 1.88 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter, the Cardinals' ace, gets the call to start on three days of rest. His first short-rest start didn't go well (three innings, four runs in NLDS Game 2), but it was difficult to resist the chance to start the ace in a Game.
away_pitcher_note: Manager Ron Washington reiterated that if the World Series goes to a seventh game, he'll tab Harrison instead of starting Game 4 hero Derek Holland. Harrison couldn't make it out of the fourth in his one Series start.

home_pitcher_note: Set to make his third straight Opening Day start, Johnson will throw the very first pitch at Marlins Park. Regarded as a key to Miami's playoff hopes, Johnson is looking to bounce back from a shoulder injury that limited him to nine starts in 2011.
away_pitcher_note: Chris Carpenter's setback opened the door for Lohse to start the season opener. The Opening Night start will technically be the second of Lohse's career, though the first came only because of a rainout. Lohse led the rotation in wins and ERA in '11.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo will be the fourth Brewers pitcher to start three Opening Days, and is halfway to Ben Sheets' club-record six openers. The Cards have given Gallardo trouble; he's 1-7 with a 5.66 ERA in 11 regular season starts.
away_pitcher_note: Perhaps Garcia is poised for another big step forward as he prepares for his third full season as a big league starter. The sole lefty in the rotation, Garcia had an up-and-down spring, but he did so last year, too, and started the season strong.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke added a cutter this spring and was sensational before a stinker against the White Sox on Monday. He expressed "zero" concern that the outing would affect his season, and is poised for a big one as a free agent-to-be.
away_pitcher_note: After Tommy John surgery cancelled his 2011 season, Wainwright showed this spring that he is fully healthy. St. Louis will monitor his innings closely but that will be of little consequence early. Wainwright won 20 games in his last full season.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf is Mr. Steady for the Brewers, with 13 wins, 33-34 starts and more than 210 innings each of the past two seasons. He'll draw on a gem against the Cardinals in last year's NLCS, a win in which Wolf worked seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: After weeks of preparing to pitch in the bullpen, Lynn's role changed in mid-March when Chris Carpenter went down. Lynn adjusted to the move seamlessly, and he should have no issues with the workload given that he started in the Minors.

home_pitcher_note: Bailey did not have a good spring as he posted a 7.98 ERA in five Cactus League games. The positive side is that he is healthy. Bailey added weight and muscle with the hope he will be more durable this season.
away_pitcher_note: After dedicating himself to a new diet and fitness routine, Westbrook had terrific spring results. He's added more disguise into his delivery, which also includes a change in hand placement. Westbrook's goal is to log at least 200 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Leake had a 5.14 ERA during the spring but looked better in many games than the results showed. Leake is headed into his third big league season and is aiming to reach 200 innings for the first time.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse took a no-hitter into the seventh inning of his Opening Day start before settling for a two-hit, one-run performance in 7 1/3 innings. He should be able to extend himself out to a pitch count of 100 after hitting 90 on Wednesday.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto was stellar on Opening Day with seven shutout frames in a win vs. Miami. Picking up from 2011, Cueto had a quick tempo and kept the ball down to induce ground balls and speedy outs. He threw 95 pitches, but said he could've gone another inning.
away_pitcher_note: After allowing two first-inning runs, Garcia settled in to blank the Brewers over the next five innings of his first start. His success was largely the result of mixing pitches, finding a better rhythm and smoothing out his delivery.

home_pitcher_note: The Cards set their rotation so Wainwright, in his first season back from elbow surgery, would pitch the home opener. Wainwright extended himself to 88 pitches on Saturday, setting him up to be able to approach 100 next time.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija held the Nationals to four hits over 8 2/3 innings in an impressive first start. It was his longest career outing, and he set a personal best with eight strikeouts. He is 2-2 in 13 games, including two starts, against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn threw 100 pitches in a strong season debut. Relying heavily on his fastball and curveball, Lynn struck out eight and allowed only two hits against the Brewers. He proved he's more than capable to hold down Chris Carpenter's spot in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Volstad's fifth career start and second game ever at Busch Stadium. He did not get a decision in his Cubs debut vs. the Brewers, giving up three runs on five hits over five innings. Volstad fell behind in the count early in the game.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook, who waited nine days to make his regular-season debut on Monday, was a little erratic with four walks in two innings. But he settled down to pitch seven strong innings allowing just one unearned run on three hits in a 7-1 win vs. the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm struggled in his Cubs debut, giving up five runs in the first against the Brewers on Tuesday. The lefty needed 41 pitches to get through that inning. He's 4-6 in his career vs. Cardinals and 1-1 in three starts at Busch Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse, coming off his stellar outing on Opening Day, held the Reds to just one run on four hits in six innings on Tuesday. He walked one and struck out two. Lohse was in control throughout his stint, retiring eight in a row in one stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto lasted only five innings the last time vs. St. Louis on Wednesday. His biggest issue came in the third after it took 14 pitches to retire Erik Komatsu. Clearly worn down from the battle, three straight hits followed for three runs.

home_pitcher_note: This will be two straight starts against the Reds for Garcia, who labored without sharp command in his last outing. He allowed 11 hits in 4 2/3 innings. Garcia hasn't had ideal feel of his pitches in either of his starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Through two starts as a Red, Latos has not gone more than five frames. In his last start on Thursday in Washington, he had two strikes on a few batters and wasn't able to put them away. Still, he only gave up two runs and that was an improvement.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright endured one of the worst starts of his career on Friday, matching his career high with eight runs allowed. Speed bumps are to be expected this year, as Wainwright is in his first season back from Tommy John surgery.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo pitched brilliantly for 7 1/3 scoreless innings at Washington Friday but was burned by his own 'pen and a lack of run support. He changed speeds well and seemed to have high 80s mph velocity. He also notched his team's only run with a sac fly.

home_pitcher_note: Morton was workmanlike in first start of the season, on Saturday, needing 71 pitches to get through five innings against the Giants. He is 2-5 in nine starts vs. the Cards.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn has allowed one run in his two starts and has proven plenty capable of holding down Chris Carpenter's spot. There is room for Lynn to improve the quality of his offspeed pitches. Doing so would increase the effectiveness of his fastball.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett returns from the 15-day disabled list to replace Kevin Correia, who experienced discomfort in his left side.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook recorded 16 of his 21 outs Sunday via a ground ball, a terrific sign for the sinker-baller. He was more efficient in his second outing than his first, allowing him to finish seven frames. Westbrook is 2-0 for the first time since '06.

home_pitcher_note: Making his first career appearance against the Cardinals is an opportunity for Bedard to end his streak of tough-luck defeats, as the Cards are vulnerable vs. lefties.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse would have been the NL's second three-game winner had the bullpen not lost a lead in his start on Tuesday. Lohse showcased terrific fastball command in the outing and has pitched ahead in the count consistently all year.

home_pitcher_note: Garza served up a pair of two-run homers on Wednesday against the Marlins. He's 2-1 with a 5.32 ERA in his career against the Cardinals, his opponent on Monday. In two starts at home, he's given up two runs over 14 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: After two flat outings, Garcia showed much more life and movement on his pitches in his last outing, a win over the Reds. His sinker helped him get four double plays, and he needed only 89 pitches to finish seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija is coming off a loss to the Marlins in which he lasted 3 2/3 innings and he struggled to throw first-pitch strikes. That has to change. He picked up a W on April 13 in St. Louis, but did give up five runs in one inning.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright won't blame Tommy John surgery for his slow start, but that is having an effect. His velocity is down, and the righty has not had the same life on his pitches. He is at risk of not winning a game in April for the first time in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad is still looking for that first win; he doesn't have one since last July 10. In his last outing vs. the Reds, he gave up five earned runs over five innings. He lost April 14 to the Cardinals, serving up four runs over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn became the club's first three-game winner and has allowed only one run in each of his starts. He was efficient on Friday, and confused hitters by mixing up pitch sequences. Lynn is being aggressive, which should help him to keep pitching deep.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook was a hard-luck loser his last time out despite continuing his strong season start. He reached a season-high 113 pitches and recorded only two outfield outs. The latter is a sign that his sinker was effective. That is his key to success.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers altered their pitching plans so Gallardo will work on regular rest in the series opener. He's is 1-8 with a 6.17 ERA in 12 regular-season starts against the Cards, including an Opening Day loss.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse has thrown at least seven innings in three of his four starts and would have four wins if not for a blown save. He's walked only two, highlighting how well his command has been. Lohse has also not pitched from behind all year.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Estrada's second start for left-hander Chris Narveson, who is out for the year with a shoulder injury. Estrada struck out nine and limited the Rockies to one run Saturday in his first start in Narveson's spot.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia pitched 7 2/3 impressive innings against the Cubs but didn't factor in the decision in a walk-off win for Chicago. The lefty is 4-2 with a 3.24 ERA in nine games (eight starts) in his career against Milwaukee, including a win this year.
away_pitcher_note: The road has been tough on Greinke. He allowed eight runs in 3 2/3 innings at Wrigley Field earlier this month and has a career road ERA of 4.29.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright showed signs of getting back on track in his last outing. He allowed one run and struck out seven in six innings. Now he just needs run support. In Wainwright's four starts, the Cards have not scored a run while he's been on the mound.
away_pitcher_note: Morton's delayed season -- he remained in extended spring camp until April 14, recovering from hip surgery -- is in full swing largely due to the effectiveness of his breaking stuff, which he has been able to set up with inside fastballs.

home_pitcher_note: In the rotation because of an injury to Chris Carpenter, Lynn became the Majors' first four-game winner his last time out. He has fooled hitters with his use of three fastballs and two off-speed pitches. He maintains velocity deep into outings, too.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett will make his first Busch Stadium appearance since 2005. He owns a 2.08 ERA in three starts there. The Cards were foils for his stellar Bucs debut on April 21, when he blanked them on three hits through seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook, thriving with his sinker, has gone at least 6 2/3 innings in each of his first four starts for the first time in his career. Asked if Friday's win over Milwaukee was the best start he's ever had to date, Westbrook said, "Without a doubt."
away_pitcher_note: Getting some runs on Saturday in Atlanta turned Bedard into the best 1-4 pitcher in baseball. The veteran's moxie is beginning to show through, and his ability to vary his approach the second and third times through a lineup confounds batters.

home_pitcher_note: Harrell allowed six runs, five earned, and nine hits in six innings on Saturday. He walked one and struck out one over 86 pitches. A two-run double and a two-run home run by Jay Bruce spelled doom for Harrell.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse allowed as many runs in his last outing (three) as he had in his first four, but he still managed to become the National League's second four-game winner. Lohse had walked just two in 27 1/3 innings before issuing four free passes on Saturday.

home_pitcher_note: Norris will face the team he's had the most success against. He's 6-2 in his first three years in the Majors vs. the Cardinals. Norris was sharp for six innings in his last outing on April 30 against the Mets before faltering in the seventh.
away_pitcher_note: In a seven-inning start Sunday, Garcia allowed three runs, all immediately after he had a baserunning gaffe of his own. He also struck out a season-high six. Garcia has pitched at least seven innings in three of his five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Happ, who struggled last season with the Astros before being sent down to the Minors, has had four quality starts in his last five outings. The Astros are 3-2 in games started by Happ this season. Happ has 31 strikeouts in 29 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright won his last start, even though he did surrender two more homers. He's now given up seven, nearly half as many as he allowed in 33 starts in 2010. He continues to search for consistent command, though his last two starts have been better.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders had to battle in his start against the Nats in Washington. The left-hander allowed two runs on seven hits in 6 1/3 innings. Saunders made his lone career start against the Cards last season, and tossed five one-hit innings to get the win.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn became the NL's first five-game winner in his last start. He retired 15 straight at one point and continues to baffle hitters with his three fastballs and two offspeed pitches. Lynn has allowed more than one run in a game only once.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy felt like he had his best stuff of the year his last time out, but wound up dropping his first regular-season decision since Aug. 18, 2011, a span of 12 starts. He allowed two runs on four hits over seven innings vs. the Nats in a 2-1 loss.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook allowed as many earned runs in his last outing (four) as he had in his first four starts combined. That was largely due to elevated pitches and a so-so sinker. Westbrook is 3-0 this season against teams not from Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Miley will be making his fourth start since taking Daniel Hudson's spot in the rotation. In his last start against the Mets, he allowed four runs in six innings, with all of the runs coming in the third. Miley has also made three relief appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse was tagged with his first loss of the year at Houston, May 4. He lasted five frames giving up a season-high seven hits. For the second start in a row, Lohse allowed three earned runs. He'd allowed three total in his previous four starts starts.

home_pitcher_note: Walks hurt Garcia in his last outing. He issued four, which, along with a grand slam, loomed large as he allowed six runs in six innings. Garcia's results have been mixed this year, and when he has been hurt, it's been mostly by big innings.
away_pitcher_note: Minor's inability to consistently command his changeup has led to him allowing 15 runs and 18 hits in his past two starts. He has surrendered four home runs in the 11 1/3 innings he's pitched in this span.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright has won two straight and appears to have found his way. He has pitched at least six innings in each of his last three outings and limited Houston to one run in seven innings last weekend. Getting his delivery motion in sync has helped.
away_pitcher_note: Beachy allowed one hit and kept the Rockies scoreless before encountering a little seventh-inning trouble at Coors Field on Sunday. He has won three straight decisions and limited opponents to a .190 batting average.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn has won all six of his starts, though he did labor a bit his last time out. That prompted an exit after only five innings. The Cardinals want to avoid any overuse issues early, as this is Lynn's first full season as a Major League starter.
away_pitcher_note: Hanson bounced back from his worst start of the year by limiting the Cubs to two runs in six innings on Monday. His velocity has dipped since showing slight improvement two weeks ago.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook has won all four starts he's made against teams not from Pittsburgh and has pitched into the seventh in each of his six starts. He continues to thrive with his sinker and has received more run support than any other National League pitcher.
away_pitcher_note: It's only natural for Dempster to face the Brewers. He's 15-6 with a 2.75 ERA against them. However, he'll take a "W" against anybody. He has not won since Aug. 16, a span of 14 starts. All five of his starts this year have been quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse lasted only five innings on Wednesday, largely due to suffering a left hamstring strain while running the bases. Lohse became the third National League pitcher to win five games.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm is on a roll. He's won four straight, and given up three earned runs over 25 1/3 innings in that stretch. He's also holding teams to a .167 average. He lost to the Cardinals on April 15 right before starting his streak.

home_pitcher_note: Bumgarner saw his five-game winning streak snapped on Friday with a loss to the D-backs. His only other defeat this season also came against Arizona. In his five other starts, he has given up just six earned runs over 35 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia has allowed 11 runs in his last 11 2/3 innings and is especially getting knocked around early, as six of those runs have come in the first. He's having particular trouble locating his sinker, which has often forced him to pitch from behind.
summary: 2012-05-16 - St. Louis Cardinals (4) @ San Francisco Giants (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Cain ended the Giants' nine-game losing streak against the D-backs on Saturday night by throwing six innings of three-hit, one-run ball while striking out eight. He also helped his own cause with a 2-for-3 and two-RBI night at the plate.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright tied a career high with five walks Saturday. It was the first time he had walked more than two this year and just the second time he hadn't finished five innings. He had previously won all six of his career starts vs. Atlanta.
summary: 2012-05-17 - St. Louis Cardinals (5) @ San Francisco Giants (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: In six outings, Lilly has surrendered just nine earned runs, but he's coming off his worst start of the year. Lilly was hit hard for three in the first on Sunday but settled in for a victory in his eighth straight decision.
away_pitcher_note: After winning his first six starts, Lynn suffered his first loss Sunday. He was stung by walks (three), but did end his day by retiring nine straight. Lynn threw a season-high 121 pitches. He has struck out seven or more in four starts.
summary: 2012-05-18 - St. Louis Cardinals (5) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw is in Cy Young mode, coming off a duel when he out-pitched, and out-brushbacked, Ian Kennedy with seven scoreless innings. Kershaw complained a bit about his command against Arizona due to two walks, but he kept the ball in the park.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook endured his shortest start of the year on Monday, when he was chased after throwing 107 pitches in five innings. Westbrook goes as his sinker goes, and it wasn't sharp early in that outing. He allowed 11 hits and a season-high four runs.
summary: 2012-05-19 - St. Louis Cardinals (0) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley has given the Dodgers eight innings combined in his last two starts and is coming off a loss to Arizona when he allowed five consecutive hits, falling into the same pattern and hittable location that has gotten him into slumps before.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse was aggressive throughout his last start, though command issues cost him early. Still, he rebounded to pitch into the seventh. His left hamstring remains sore, but it's not affecting him on the mound.
summary: 2012-05-20 - St. Louis Cardinals (5) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Garcia put together one of his best efforts of the season in his last start against the Giants. He did not walk a batter for the first time all season and matched his career high with nine strikeouts. It resulted in his first win in nearly a month.
away_pitcher_note:
Richard pitched one of his best outings of the season in his last start. He allowed two runs, struck out six and walked none against the Dodgers. Both of his wins this season have been against the Dodgers.
Limiting walks is crucial for the lefty.
summary: 2012-05-21 - San Diego Padres (3) @ St. Louis Cardinals (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright lowered his ERA in his last start, allowing two earned runs over 5 2/3 innings, but his walk totals are becoming a little alarming. After walking a total of seven over his first six starts, he has walked nine over his past two.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez allowed a season-high five runs (three earned) in five innings in his last outing, a loss to the Dodgers. Walks continue to be an issue. He issued three walks against the Dodgers, giving him a team-high 27 walks in 53 1/3 innings this season.
summary: 2012-05-22 - San Diego Padres (0) @ St. Louis Cardinals (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: A winner in his first six starts this season, Lynn is now winless in his last two. He allowed season highs in runs (four) and hits (nine) Friday. Lynn needs to get back to pitching ahead in the count regularly, which will keep down his pitch count.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan wasn't at his sharpest in his last outing, walking five (one intentional) and allowing a season-high four runs in five innings against the Angels. The veteran struck out none and battled with his fastball command early.
summary: 2012-05-23 - San Diego Padres (3) @ St. Louis Cardinals (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook didn't pitch as poorly last time out as his line would suggest, as he was hurt by his defense. Still, he's now allowed at least three earned runs in three of his last four starts. He hadn't given up more than two in any of his first four.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton struggled in his shortest start of the season, allowing a career-high four home runs in just 4 1/3 innings in a loss to Boston. The defeat ended a four-game stretch in which Blanton went 3-0 with a 2.10 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The bullpen cost Lohse a win on Sunday, though the righty was also not his sharpest. He allowed 11 hits, a season high. Though Lohse has won just once in his last four starts, he has allowed more than three earned runs in only one of nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lee allowed nine hits and five runs in seven innings in his start Sunday against the Red Sox. Remarkably, Lee is winless this season after six starts, but that's mostly because of an uncooperative offense.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia was in line for the win on Monday before his bullpen lost the lead. The lefty has turned in two straight quality starts after allowing two runs in seven strong innings Monday. He has walked just three batters in his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick has a 2.25 ERA in his last four starts, but he has nothing to show for it with an 0-2 mark. That has everything to do with the Phillies' offense, which hasn't given him much support. He hopes for more against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright had far and away his best outing of the season on Tuesday, tossing a shutout over the Padres. The right-hander scattered four hits and struck out nine, and afterward said he had never been more satisfied after an outing.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay had one of his worst starts of the year, allowing five runs over six innings on Tuesday to the Nats. Halladay's 3.63 ERA is the highest it's been this late in a season since he finished with a 3.71 ERA in 2007.

home_pitcher_note: Hanson was solid in a no-decision against the Reds on Wednesday, allowing only one run in six innings of work on four hits to go with five strikeouts. At one point, Hanson retired 12 straight batters, lowering his season ERA to 3.12.
away_pitcher_note: After starting the season with six straight wins, Lynn has battled subpar command in each of his last three starts. It's part of the learning curve for the first-year starter, who has also shown a knack for getting stronger the deeper he pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Delgado has given up four runs in each of his last two starts, both losses. In his first start at Turner Field in two weeks, Delgado will try to continue his success at home, where his ERA is nearly 2.50 runs better than on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook lasted just 3 2/3 innings Thursday while allowing six runs on eight hits. He's struggled this month after going 3-1 in April. Westbrook is 1-2 in May, hasn't won a start since May 8 and has seen his ERA rise to 3.21 from 1.30 on April 7.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson was victimized by two big innings in his last start, perhaps his worst this year. He'll try to return to getting groundouts with his sharp sinker against the Cardinals, a team that has given him trouble in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse allowed three runs (two earned) on six hits over 6 1/3 innings Friday vs. Philadelphia and took a no-decision after the 'pen couldn't hold a one-run lead. In his previous two starts, he allowed eight earned runs on 20 hits over 12 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Santana needed only 96 pitches (74 strikes) for his first shutout since 2010. He struck out seven and never reached a three-ball count. Six times, a Padres inning lasted exactly nine pitches.
away_pitcher_note: After a shaky season start, Wainwright has settled in and has recently looked much more like the ace he was before elbow surgery. In his last 15 innings, Wainwright has allowed one earned run, 11 hits and one walk. He has struck out 11.
summary: 2012-06-01 - St. Louis Cardinals (0) @ New York Mets (8) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: R.A. Dickey has struck out 29 batters over his last three starts, the highest total of his career. Backed by improvements to his knuckleball, Dickey will look to continue his recent success, as he's only allowed one run in his last two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn was aggressive and around the strike zone with his fastball in Monday's seven-inning start. It got him back in the win column in a game where he threw 71 of 107 pitches for strikes. He threw a first-pitch strike to 18 of final 23 batters faced.
summary: 2012-06-02 - St. Louis Cardinals (0) @ New York Mets (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Niese didn't have his best stuff vs. the Phils on Monday, walking five and only throwing 64 of his 115 pitches for strikes. He'll look to regain the control he found in Pittsburgh, when he tossed 7 2/3 innings and only allowed one run on May 23.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook's last four starts have been nothing like his first six. With an unreliable sinker, Westbrook has gone more than five innings just once in that span. He has also allowed 31 hits, nine walks and 19 runs (17 earned) in 20 innings.
