home_pitcher_note: Kennedy was disappointed in his 2013 season, and it motivated him throughout the offseason. He has spent the spring making sure his breaking ball is ready in April. This will be his third straight Opening Day start.
away_pitcher_note: The Opening Day start will be Wainwright's third, but rain washed one out. With Chris Carpenter gone, Wainwright is the clear leader of this pitching staff. And another year from surgery, he expects to be more consistent.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill reported to Spring Training having lost around 15 pounds from last season, the result of some dietary changes. Last season, he faced the Cardinals once and allowed one run over six innings, but did not get a decision.
away_pitcher_note: Following a season in which he had shoulder problems, Garcia reported to Spring Training healthy and looked strong in six starts. He can be a formidable No. 2 starter but will need to pitch better away from home.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy will be making his first start in a D-backs uniform after signing a two-year deal as a free agent during the offseason. McCarthy has spent the past seven years in the American League and has never faced the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: An 18-game winner last season, Lynn is beginning his second full year in the Cardinals rotation. He has a different look this year, though, after shedding 40 pounds over the winter in an effort to improve his stamina.

home_pitcher_note: With the Giants trailing in the NLCS, 3-1, Zito pitched the biggest game of his career against these same Cardinals last Oct. 19 at St. Louis, lasting 7 2/3 innings in a 5-0 win. Zito will begin his quest to even his AT&T Park record, which is 30-35.
away_pitcher_note: Before his 2012 season ended prematurely with an oblique injury, Westbrook was the reliable veteran the Cardinals needed in the back end of the rotation. An effective sinker is the key for him to be efficient and effective.

home_pitcher_note: Overall, Vogelsong has a history of struggling at the start of a season. He's 2-4 with a 6.31 ERA lifetime in April. But last year he worked at least six innings in his first 21 starts, matching the third-longest streak in franchise history.
away_pitcher_note: Miller earns the start after beating out Trevor Rosenthal and Joe Kelly for the rotation's fifth spot. This will be his second Major League start. He limited the Reds to one hit in six innings in the team's final game of 2012.

away_pitcher_note: Wainwright went from dominant to hittable on Opening Day, struggling to finish his pitches in the middle innings in a loss to the D-backs. If he can correct that, there's no reason he shouldn't be able to pitch deeper and more effectively.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia will start a home opener for the first time in his career and will be coming off a solid 5 2/3-inning performance in Arizona. Garcia had a strong spring and has shown no residual effects from last year's shoulder problems.
away_pitcher_note: Latos had a bad April track record coming into this season but was mostly sharp on Wednesday vs. the Angels. At one point he fanned the side that included Albert Pujols and Josh Hamilton. But he allowed homers to Howie Kendrick and Alberto Callaspo.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn lasted four innings in his season debut, as elevated pitches and out-of-whack mechanics pushed his pitch count quickly up. He continues to adjust to a new body composition, which has led to necessary delivery changes.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo kept his roll going from Spring Training and took it into his first start vs. the Angels on Thursday. He threw strikes and limited trouble. "My command was there, I felt like I kept a good tempo of the game," Arroyo said.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook walked six Friday, due largely to delivery difficulties. Even still, he didn't allow an earned run in 6 2/3 innings and was strong enough late to push his pitch count to 116 for the first time since August 2011.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey wasn't sharp in his first start Friday vs. the Nats, but he relied on his fastball that reached 95 mph to log six shutout innings. He now has 19 consecutive regular-season scoreless frames, starting with his no-no last Sept. 28 in Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Miller picked up his first career win as a starter with a 5 1/3-inning outing Saturday. He relied heavily on a fastball-curveball mix and showed some conviction with the curve, not abandoning it when it didn't work early on.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse barely had a Spring Training, yet he was the only Brewer to deliver a quality start in the first turn through the five-man rotation. After an 87-pitch debut, he should be cleared to top 100 pitches in this game vs. his former team.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright has opened the season with a pair of quality starts, something the Cards expect with regularity from their ace. He had an especially effective curveball in his seven-inning start Sunday against the Giants.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo is off to a subpar start, and it gets no easier -- he is 1-9 with a 6.72 ERA in 14 regular-season starts against the Cardinals. At least the lone win was in St. Louis, an eight-inning, one-hit, no-run gem in 2011.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia was in line to move to 2-0 this season until a blown save cost him against the Reds on Monday. Garcia matched his career high with 10 strikeouts and pitched into the seventh for the first time this year.
away_pitcher_note: Estrada became the first Brewers starter to work past the sixth inning when he delivered seven innings of two-run ball to spoil the Cubs' home opener. He's not known as a hitter, but he has RBIs in each of his starts.

home_pitcher_note: Pitching at home against St. Louis is about as good as it gets for J-Mac. Last season alone, he was 6-2 at PNC Park with a 2.73 ERA -- less than half what it was on the road (5.95) -- and didn't allow a run to the Cards in two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn struck out 10 Reds batters en route to getting his first win on Tuesday. He corrected some delivery flaws between outings and likely could have pitched deeper had the strikeouts not pushed up his pitch count.

home_pitcher_note: Clint Hurdle was interested in Sanchez's follow-up start to a strong season debut, and he's even more curious to see his rebound from Wednesday's shellacking (nine runs in 3 1/3 innings). The lefty must pitch in to be effective.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook dazzled on Wednesday, pitching his first shutout in seven seasons and throwing just 111 pitches. He's yet to allow an earned run this season and is garnering ground balls with regularity, evidence of a strong sinker.

home_pitcher_note: As steady as he's been, Burnett has one win in his past 12 starts dating back to mid-August. The Cards gave him a hard time last season (16 runs in 15 1/3 innings). His second strikeout of the game will be No. 2,000 of his career.
away_pitcher_note: Miller was brilliant against the Brewers on Friday. Making his third career start, the 22-year-old rookie allowed one hit and struck out eight batters in seven shutout innings as part of a 2-0 win. He threw 113 pitches, with 87 going for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels showed improvement Saturday in Miami, albeit against a mediocre Marlins lineup, allowing one run in six innings. But he had a 10.47 ERA following his first two starts, so he will take any positives he can.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright shut out the Brewers in his last start and pushed his season strikeout total to 24 with 12 strikeouts. He's yet to walk a batter this season. He's allowed only two earned runs in his last 17 innings of work.

home_pitcher_note: It's a start. Halladay allowed five hits, one run, one walk and struck out two in eight innings Sunday in Miami. Did he turn a corner? Or did he face a weak lineup? He can answer those questions Friday against St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia tossed seven scoreless innings Sunday but for the second straight start, the bullpen cost him the win. Still, the lefty is pitching with clear confidence, and is riding groundball outs to success.
summary: 2013-04-19 - St. Louis Cardinals @ Philadelphia Phillies (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: Lee has dominated in his first three starts, posting a 1.52 ERA. He has allowed 15 hits, four earned runs, one walk, one home run and struck out 18 in 23 2/3 innings, leading the Phillies rotation to this point.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn has finished six innings only once in three starts and labored his last time out despite being staked to a nine-run lead. Pitch selection was largely the problem, as Lynn relied too heavily on his fastball.

home_pitcher_note: He allowed two hits, two walks and struck out four in seven scoreless innings Tuesday against the Reds. He had struggled against lefties, but held Shin-Soo Choo, Joey Votto, Jay Bruce and Xavier Paul hitless in 11 at-bats.
away_pitcher_note: The four runs Westbrook gave up to Pittsburgh on Tuesday were erased with a rainout, meaning he has still not allowed an earned run this season. Westbrook will need a sharper sinker to have better success next time out.

home_pitcher_note: Haren's rocky start continued on Tuesday in Miami, where he allowed seven runs (three earned) on seven hits in 4 1/3 innings. He was left searching for answers after that outing, and he'll have to find them vs. another tough lineup.
away_pitcher_note: Miller took the first loss of his career on Wednesday despite allowing only two runs in six innings. He's shown impressive poise so far in his young career and continues to give hitters fits with his sneaky fastball velocity.

home_pitcher_note: Detwiler pounded the strike zone with fastballs for seven strong innings Wednesday in Miami, allowing only one run on a career-high 107 pitches. The lefty has been dominant so far in 2013, giving up only three runs (two earned) in 20 innings.
away_pitcher_note: No other Major League pitcher in the modern era besides the Cardinals ace has struck out 25 or more batters without issuing a walk in his first four starts of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg had one clean inning and threw a lot of pitches [111] Friday. However, he lasted six innings, allowed four runs (two earned) and struck out six batters against the Mets. Strasburg allowed the first two runs in a 28-pitch first inning.
away_pitcher_note: Normally a master of movement, Garcia was up with numerous flat pitches and the Phillies banged away at him in his last start, his first bad one in four this season.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn shut out the Phillies on one hit in seven innings Saturday, his best start of the year. He did not have similar success in a start against the Pirates earlier in April. He gave up four runs in five innings on that night.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez allowed two runs in three innings against Atlanta in a 4-2 win his last time out. Sanchez has struggled over the past two weeks, during which he has allowed 11 runs and 12 hits in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook had a start against Pittsburgh rained out earlier this month, which gives him more time to solve that offense. The Pirates have always given Westbrook fits; he has only one win in 13 appearances against the Bucs.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett has allowed three earned runs or fewer in all five of his starts this season. He's struck out 42 batters in 29 innings. In his last start, against the Phillies on April 22, neither of the runs he allowed came on a hit.

home_pitcher_note: Miller allowed two runs in six innings against Pittsburgh earlier in April but was outpitched by A.J. Burnett. He's made three straight quality starts and continues to have hitters fooled by the late life on his fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Locke had the best outing of his career, throwing six scoreless innings in a 2-0 win over the Phillies. Locke impressed manager Clint Hurdle after the youngster battled through jams in both the second and fourth innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright fell two outs shy of a shutout on Tuesday, instead settling for 8 1/3 scoreless innings. He's riding a four-game winning streak and his curveball has been made better by his willingness to throw more high fastballs.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander is coming off a good effort in last Thursday's 1-0 victory over the Cubs. He threw seven shutout innings and gave up just four hits to earn his first win this season.

home_pitcher_note: After a strong road start, Garcia returns to Busch Stadium, where he has habitually pitched his best. He's allowed three earned runs in 13 2/3 home innings this year and has a career 2.45 ERA when pitching in St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo will try to recover after a shaky start against Washington last Thursday. The righty gave up six runs in six innings -- all runs coming before the fourth -- but still battled to get through six, making manager Dusty Baker happier.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn has allowed just one run in his last 16 innings pitched and is riding a personal four-game winning streak. He has won 23 of his first 31 career decisions and has more strikeouts (31) than innings pitched (29) this season.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander came up empty despite a great performance versus the Nationals last Friday. He gave up just one run on five hits in seven innings, but took the loss in a 1-0 defeat.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta appears to be building some confidence. He hit 96 mph with his second pitch against the Dodgers and 97 mph three pitches after that, and balanced that heat by throwing a higher-than-usual percentage of changeups.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook will be going for career win No. 100 for the third time after the bullpen blew a lead in his last start. The Cards have lost three of his four starts even though he has allowed an earned run in only one of them.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse has been great, but unlucky. The Brewers are 2-3 in his starts while scoring a total of one run in the losses, including 2-0 duels with the Dodgers' Clayton Kershaw on Sunday and the Cards' Shelby Miller on April 12.
away_pitcher_note: Miller's smooth April endured a laborious end on Sunday, when he needed 113 pitches to cover 5 2/3 innings. Fastball command continues to be key for Miller, who is still learning how best to incorporate his offspeed pitches.

home_pitcher_note: After a laborious first two frames last time out, Gallardo settled down and completed seven innings while giving up only one earned run and retiring the final 13 batters he faced. He is 1-10 with a 6.84 ERA in 15 starts vs. the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright had a dominant April, averaging 7.4 innings per start and posting a 43:3 strikeout-to-walk ratio. He has been every bit the ace the Cardinals hoped, and he continues to experiment with throwing more high fastballs.

home_pitcher_note: With the roof open and the baseballs flying Tuesday on the first warm night at Miller Park, Estrada picked a bad night to elevate some pitches against the Pirates. He surrendered three home runs, matching a dubious career high.
away_pitcher_note: Using the Reds' aggressiveness in his favor, Garcia was efficient (92 pitches) in an eight-inning win on Tuesday. He recorded 18 of his 24 outs via the ground ball, an indication of superb movement on his pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Wood took a perfect game into the fifth his last time out and allowed only two hits through the first seven frames. Defensive lapses in the eighth resulted in a loss, but he has six straight quality starts to open the season.
away_pitcher_note: Dating back to 2012, Lynn is on a personal 10-game winning streak, the longest active streak in the Majors. He's finished seven innings in his past three starts and has allowed eight hits and two runs during those 21 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Villanueva has given up four runs in his last two outings, and the problem has been elevation. He's had a tough time keeping the ball down when needed. In his last start, the Reds collected seven hits over 5 2/3 innings, his shortest start this year.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook wasn't as sharp in his last start, but the Brewers hit several liners right at the defense, and he came away with his 100th career win. "Made some mistakes and got away with some things," he said.

home_pitcher_note: Miller has not allowed more than three runs in any of his six outings. If he's had a deficiency, though, it's been in efficiency. High pitch counts have kept Miller from pitching deeper in games where he has dominated.
away_pitcher_note: Garland failed to pitch at least six innings last Saturday for the first time in six starts, but won as he gave up three runs in five innings to the Rays in Colorado's 9-3 win.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright has been every bit an ace this season, though he is coming off his shakiest performance of the year. The five runs he allowed in that start equaled his total from his previous four starts (31 1/3 innings) combined.
away_pitcher_note: After missing two starts while on the 15-day disabled list with a back strain, Chacin pitched a season-high seven innings Sunday against the Rays. He gave up three runs in a 23-pitch first and six runs total (five earned) in an 8-3 loss.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia has finished eight innings in back-to-back starts and has allowed a combined two runs in those outings. He is riding a three-game winning streak and has found success in riding an effective sinker as of late.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa rebounded from a tough start in Los Angeles to hold the Yankees scoreless on three singles over six innings in his last start, a home win. He's 2-2 with a 4.50 ERA in four games (two starts) at the current Busch Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn's 10-game winning streak ended in his last start, though he gave up only two runs on four hits in seven innings. Lynn entered the game leading the league in run support. He's finished the seventh in four straight outings.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off one of the best starts of his career, Hefner was noticeably less sharp last time out against the White Sox. He still kept the Mets within striking distance, which is all they can ask for in his debut meeting with the Cardinals.

away_pitcher_note: Miley has been struggling of late, going 0-4 with a 9.14 ERA over his last four starts. Last time out against the Cubs, he allowed two runs in the first inning and five in the third before tossing four scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: Buchanan scattered nine hits, two earned runs and one walk and struck out four in 6 2/3 innings Sunday against the Giants. It was his third consecutive quality start since replacing Cliff Lee in the rotation this month.
away_pitcher_note: Miller had five strong innings but one that sunk him in his last start. He allowed four hits and as many runs in a 38-pitch third that was the latest example of an inning imploding for him. Walks continue to be a problem for Miller, too.

away_pitcher_note: Masterson had a stretch of 11 straight scoreless innings end in the fifth his last time out when he allowed four runs. He continues to work through mechanical issues, the latest being a tendency to let his arm drag too far behind his body.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano, 3-0 against the Cards last season, tries to rebound from allowing nine runs in his last home start -- compared to the dozen he gave up all last season at home. In his previous six starts, he had not given up more than two runs.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey has allowed two earned runs in three of his four starts since joining the club and has stepped up as the workhorse the Cardinals hoped they were acquiring in a Trade Deadline deal. He struck out seven and walked one in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: Cole has a chance to build on his strong start off the DL, in which he held Atlanta to two runs in seven innings. This will be his third regular-season meeting with the Cardinals, whom he held to three runs in two NLDS starts in 2013.
away_pitcher_note: If not for a late rain delay, Lynn may have made a run at his second career complete game on Wednesday. As it was he pitched seven scoreless innings in his seventh start of such length this season. Lynn has a 1.84 ERA since the All-Star break.

allowing four earned runs in six innings, settling down after a four-run third. The veteran said he's made an adjustment that he hopes will fix the issues he's had over his last seven starts.

away_pitcher_note: Hendricks' streak of six consecutive quality starts ended due to a lengthy rain delay in his last outing. He's allowed just 10 runs in 50 2/3 innings since debuting on July 10.

home_pitcher_note: Masterson is pitching for his rotation spot, as he has allowed four-plus runs in four of five starts since joining the organization. Masterson has worked to simplify his mechanics, and success will continue to ride on the effectiveness of his sinker.
away_pitcher_note: In his last Minor League rehab outing with Double-A Tennessee, Doubront gave up three earned runs on five hits over 4 1/3 innings. He threw 95 pitches, 59 for strikes, striking out five. He's been on the DL since he was acquired by the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzales will be called up as the "26th man" to start the nightcap of the doubleheader. Gonzales went 4-1 with a 3.35 ERA in eight Triple-A starts after making three starts - none longer than five innings - with the Cards earlier this summer.
away_pitcher_note: Wada held the AL East-leading Orioles to one run on one hit over 6 1/3 innings in his last start, striking out eight. The 33-year-old lefty is making a case for staying with the Cubs next season. He doesn't overpower hitters but has late movement.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey has made five starts since joining the Cardinals and he has finished seven innings in three of them. He's been the workhorse the club wanted and he has allowed two or fewer earned runs in four of five appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Wood will be looking to win back-to-back starts for the first time since June 10-15. He's 1-6 with a 5.00 ERA in his last 13 starts. In his last outing, the lefty ended a 12-start winless streak with six shutout innings against the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn will face the Pirates for a second straight start, coming off a strong showing in Pittsburgh when he allowed two runs over six innings. Lynn has pitched through the sixth in 19 starts this year and finished August with a 1.99 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Cole will be making his third start since returning from injury. He was great in his first two games back, with a 2.77 ERA and 15 strikeouts in 13 innings -- nine of which came in his last start, when he took a no-hitter into the sixth vs. the Cards.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright lost to the Pirates in his last start when they tagged him for three runs in six innings. The Cardinals have won only three of Wainwright's eight second-half starts after going 15-4 behind him prior to the All-Star break.
away_pitcher_note: Locke had a 4-0 August, which he capped by allowing just one run over 7 1/3 innings against the Cardinals last Wednesday.

home_pitcher_note: Miller pitched well his last time out, allowing just two solo homers in a seven-inning no decision. He showed improved efficiency, though homers continue to sting Miller. He's allowed eight over his last seven starts and 20 this season.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez took a no-hitter into the seventh inning of his last start vs. the Reds and lasted 7 2/3 innings on 114 pitches. He was charged with one run and struck out six. In his last five starts, Volquez owns a 1.65 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta has turned in two lousy starts in a row, including a six-run, nine-hit outing against the Giants in which he lasted a season-low three innings.
away_pitcher_note: Recovered from a right shoulder stress reaction, Wacha will be making his first start since June 17. He threw 34 pitches in a rehab start on August 31 and will be limited to 50-60 in this outing. Marco Gonzales is expected to back him up.

home_pitcher_note: All five of Fiers' starts this season have met the definition of "quality," including a seven-inning, three-run outing against the Giants on Saturday. He was on the wrong side of Jake Peavy's 7 1/3-inning no-hit bid.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey had a troublesome start to his last outing, but kept the Cubs scoreless over his final four-plus innings to position the Cards for the win. He has allowed two or fewer earned runs in five of his six starts since joining the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse has not been particularly sharp since skipping a start with a sprained ankle and was blunt in assessing his last start against the Giants. "I'll just make it simple for you: It was terrible execution," he said.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn had a laborious afternoon on Monday, but he kept the Cards in the game by limiting the Pirates to three runs in six innings. He lasted that deep despite throwing 52 pitches through two innings, and he stranded eight runners.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson will make the 10th start of this particular tenure in the Brewers' rotation, with uncertainty to follow. The team will probably revert back to a five-man rotation, though manager Ron Roenicke has not revealed his plan.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright showed better overall command of his repertoire on Tuesday, though the Pirates hit three of his mistakes out of the park. He's allowed three-plus runs in five straight starts but has also finished at least six innings in each of those.

home_pitcher_note: Axelrod gave up five hits over six innings in his last start vs. the O's on Wednesday, but they were all hit very hard -- including three home runs that accounted for all four runs. He made mistakes in the strike zone and the homers were solidly hit.
away_pitcher_note: In one of his best starts of the season, Miller shut out the Pirates over seven scoreless innings on Wednesday. He has won just once since June 7 but has shown a heavier reliance on his curveball and a new sinker, and both have helped him recently.

home_pitcher_note: Leake wasn't sharp on Thursday vs. the Orioles, lasting a season-low four innings and tying a career high with three home runs allowed.
away_pitcher_note: Wacha made his first start since June 17 and threw 50 pitches over three innings against the Brewers. Wacha should be cleared to push to 65-70 pitches his next time out. His curveball was especially sharp in his return.

home_pitcher_note: Simon was roughed up for six runs over four innings in a loss to the Mets on Friday. After going 12-3 with a 2.70 ERA in the first half, he is 1-7 with a 5.27 ERA since. In 15 appearances (one start) against the Cardinals, he is 1-0 with a 3.54 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey had a string of four straight wins -- each with two or fewer earned runs allowed -- snapped against the Brewers on Friday. But he does continue to provide the Cardinals with length, having gone at least six innings in six of seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto is 2-0 with a 1.80 ERA over his last two starts. The All-Star right-hander lost a 1-0 duel to Adam Wainwright on Opening Day and was roughed up for four earned runs on seven hits over five innings in an Aug. 20 loss at St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn became a 15-game winner for the third straight season on Saturday and is riding a current winning streak of four. He's finished six innings in each of his last five starts and has not allowed more than three runs in a start since June.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright returned to form Sunday, as he pitched his fourth complete game of 2014 and limited the Brewers to one run on 100 pitches. The dominant outing comes after a month-long funk for Wainwright in which he had a 5.28 ERA in seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa labored through his first start following his contract extension but left in line for the win after allowing three runs on six hits to the Padres. It was only the second time in De La Rosa's last 14 starts that he didn't last at least six.

home_pitcher_note: Miller has a scoreless innings streak of 14 and is coming off a start in which he allowed three hits in seven innings. The addition of a sinker and the reprisal of his curveball have helped Miller become more efficient and less predictable.
away_pitcher_note: For the third time this season, Morales baffled the Padres, scattering four hits and two walks in six scoreless innings. It was a nice rebound performance after he surrendered a total of 13 runs in his previous two home starts.

home_pitcher_note: Cardinals manager Mike Matheny announced that Michael Wacha will not start as scheduled Sunday. Wacha "didn't feel right" in his recovery from a shoulder injury after his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles' six innings of one-run ball against the Mets on Monday was arguably his best start in months, but he didn't feel that way. He cited a lack of command and fastball velocity. The righty owns a 3.45 ERA and 1.20 WHIP on the road this season.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn was denied his 16th win on Thursday despite allowing one run while pitching his second career complete game. Lynn has allowed two or fewer earned runs in 11 of his last 13 starts and continues to be at his best deep in games.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta turned in a much-needed quality start in his last outing after the Brewers had lost 13 of 14, allowing one run on five hits in 6 2/3 innings in a 4-1 victory over Miami. Prior to that, however, the right-hander had lost three straight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright picked up his 18th win on Friday. In his last two starts, Wainwright has given up two runs in 17 innings. Wainwright didn't walk anybody Friday, a sign that his control appears to be back after a shaky August.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers is making his first start since hitting Marlins slugger Giancarlo Stanton with a pitch, resulting in facial fractures. In seven starts since being called up Aug. 9 to fill in for Matt Garza, Fiers is 6-1 with a 1.74 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Miller picked up his 10th win on Saturday, going six innings and giving up one run. Miller has given up just three runs in his last 27 innings, a streak that coincides with his ability to mix in his secondary pitches with his fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse appears to have recovered from an ankle injury that cost him one start in mid-August and limited his effectiveness in a couple others. In his last start last Friday against Cincinnati, he allowed two runs on five hits in 6 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Due to arm fatigue, Lackey had his scheduled start skipped on Tuesday and was given an extra three days' rest. He lasted only two innings in a start against the Reds on Sept. 10 due to an ejection stemming from complaints about balls/strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Holmberg earned his first big league win Saturday over the Brewers behind the strength of a good changeup. Despite not being overpowering, his 86-89 fastball was spotted well and looked tougher in conjunction with the offspeed pitch.

home_pitcher_note: Wacha will be pitching after a 10-day layoff that was built in after growing concerns about the lack of command he showed upon returning from a right shoulder injury. Wacha should be free to push toward 90 pitches if all goes right.
away_pitcher_note: Leake crossed the 200-inning mark for the first time in his career in a loss Sunday at Milwaukee. Citing the feeling of a dead arm, Leake struggled with command and location, yanking his pitches out of the strike zone.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn has allowed one run in each of his last three outings and will have a shot at eclipsing 200 innings this next time out. He has 22 quality starts and continues to pitch like a co-ace alongside Adam Wainwright.

home_pitcher_note: Wood scattered three hits over six scoreless innings in his last outing vs. the Reds, which was a big improvement after allowing seven runs over 1 2/3 innings in his previous start. He was miffed because he walked three.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright is eyeing a second 20-win season and will carry a four-start winning streak into this outing. He has allowed two runs over his last three starts, of which two were complete games.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks is going for his ninth quality start in 13 outings. He's allowed a combined three earned runs and 12 hits in 12 1/3 innings over two starts vs. the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Miller was hit in the right shin near the end of his last start, though he doesn't expect that to affect him on Tuesday. Miller has been sharp in September, allowing three runs (two earned) in 26 innings.

away_pitcher_note: After having his start pushed back three days while dealing with a dead arm issue, Lackey made his best start as a Cardinal on Friday. He was efficient through 7 2/3 innings and scattered six singles.

away_pitcher_note: This will be Wacha's final chance to prove himself ready to be a factor in October. He threw 78 pitches on Saturday (his most since returning from injury) but is still searching for crisp command, especially with his changeup.

away_pitcher_note: Wainwright draws the fifth Opening Day assignment of his career. A mid-February abdominal strain led Wainwright to have an abbreviated spring, but he still fit in three Grapefruit League starts. He built up to 93 pitches in the last one.

away_pitcher_note: Wacha's 2014 season was interrupted by injury (right shoulder stress reaction) and then ended with him serving up an NLCS-winning homer to Travis Ishikawa. He had an impressive and healthy spring and is hopeful of regaining his 2013 form.

home_pitcher_note: A Cuban defector who signed a seven-year, $32 million contract in June, the 25-year-old will be making his MLB debut. He had a smooth Arizona Fall League but ran into some consistency issues during six spring games (three starts).
away_pitcher_note: Martinez entered spring with the inside track on the fifth starter job and won it once Jaime Garcia bowed out with an injury. Martinez was electric in his final spring start, striking out five and allowing just three hits in six scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: By virtue of a rainout, Wainwright unexpectedly draws the fourth home opener of his career. He's 1-1 with a 5.51 ERA in the previous three. Wainwright threw six shutout innings in his Opening Night start against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies were so on top of Garza's pitches at Miller Park that he worried he was tipping, and switched up the signs. Now he'll face another proficient offense during the Cardinals' home opener.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn opened his season with a quality start, but also a loss, as he was undone by a hit batter and errant pickoff throw. It marked just the second April loss of his career, as his 12 April wins since 2012 are most in the Majors.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta looked sharp in his first start, allowing just two runs in seven innings in a loss to the Rockies. He was 3-1 with a 2.18 ERA in five starts against the Cardinals last year.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey worked six innings in his season debut April 10, allowing a pair of two-run Joey Votto homers in a 5-4 Cardinals loss. The 36-year-old right-hander ranks among the top 10 active pitchers in wins and strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers allowed five runs in five innings to the Pirates in his first start, giving up a homer and four doubles. He is 2-1 with a 1.30 ERA in six games, four starts, during his career against St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: Wacha became the first Cardinals pitcher to record an out in the seventh when he went 6 1/3 innings in his season debut against the Reds. He limited Cincinnati to five hits in that outing and flashed his improved curveball.
away_pitcher_note: Despite having strong performances in his first two starts, Cueto remains winless. Busch Stadium hasn't historically been one of his best venues to work -- with a 5.80 ERA over nine career starts in St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: Martinez exited in line for a win against the Reds last weekend before the bullpen blew the save behind him. Now a part of the permanent rotation, Martinez showed the sort of efficiency (100 pitches over six innings) the Cards need out of him.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey has had a setback-free rehab from flexor mass tendon surgery near his right elbow. It culminated in a 91-pitch, 5 2/3 innings start for Triple-A Louisville Sunday where there were no issues.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright been skirting around trouble all season. He has allowed the leadoff man to reach in eight of 13 innings, but he has limited damage by holding opponents to 1-for-23 with runners in scoring position.
away_pitcher_note: Leake settled down after a rocky first inning Monday against the Cubs, but not before he blew a 3-0 lead in the bottom of the first. He hasn't looked overly sharp in his first two outings. Lifetime at Busch Stadium, he has a 4.44 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Gonzalez was shaky against the Red Sox, pitching six innings and allowing five runs (four earned) and striking out six. He did manage to pick up his first victory of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Off-days gave Lynn a week between his first two starts of the season, and he has another week of rest leading up to this one. This will be his 100th career start, and he's allowed just one earned run in his first two of this year.

home_pitcher_note: Fister won his first game of the season after allowing two runs (one earned) in 6 2/3 innings vs. the Phillies on Thursday. Fister allowed four hits, four walks and struck out four.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey became the first Cardinals pitcher to finish seven innings when he did so against the Brewers on Thursday. He has shown notable efficiency early this season and has predictably come out of Spring Training pounding the strike zone.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer earned his first win of the season Friday after he held the Phillies to a run on four hits and no walks with nine strikeouts in eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: The two runs Wacha has allowed this season have been on solo homers, but he has otherwise been quite stingy. Wacha is flashing an improved curveball and has not yet had to rely too heavily on arguably his best pitch, the changeup.

home_pitcher_note: Garza emerged from Spring Training excited about his rediscovered slider, but he has struggled in the regular season and has a dissapointing ratio of strikeouts (nine) to walks (nine).
away_pitcher_note: Since winning a rotation job, Martinez has shown himself a more complete pitcher by complementing his fastball with a nice changeup-slider mix and also pulling back on velocity in order to improve command and stamina.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta is facing the Cardinals for the second time after allowing four runs on 10 hits in only five innings at Busch Stadium. His career ERA against the Cards is up to 4.58.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright finished eight innings in his most recent start, becoming the first Cards starter to go that far. He's still not pleased with the crispness of his pitches following a shortened spring, but he's still finding a way to get the results.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers has started three games and lost them all, most recently an outing against the Reds in which he surrendered two-out grand slams in consecutive innings. Asked what he needs to do better, Fiers said, "Everything."
away_pitcher_note: Lynn has allowed one earned run in each of his first three starts, even though his last two haven't been especially sharp. Lynn is looking forward to pitching on regular rest after making his last two starts following a week off.

summary: 2017-03-28 - St. Louis Cardinals @ New York Mets (Final: Tied)

home_pitcher_note: Martinez will be the first Dominican-born pitcher since Joaquin Andujar (1985) and the youngest since Joe Magrane (1989) to make an Opening Day start for the Cards. He led Cardinals pitchers with 20 quality starts, a 3.04 ERA and 5.4 WAR in 2016.
away_pitcher_note: Lester will be making his second Opening Day start with the Cubs. The lefty is coming off a stellar season in which he went 19-5 with a 2.44 ERA, and finished second in the NL Cy Young balloting. He even hit an RBI single in last spring game.

home_pitcher_note: This will be the first time since 2012 that Wainwright doesn't pitch the season opener. He's seeking a bounceback year after posting a career-worst 4.62 ERA and 1.404 WHIP in 2016. He leaves Spring Training confident that his curveball is back.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta followed his 2015 NL Cy Young season by winning 18 games. He went 11-3 on the road, so the right-hander won't mind pitching at Busch Stadium. Plus, he was 3-1 with a 2.38 ERA in four starts last year against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Recovered from Tommy John surgery, Lynn will be starting for the first time since Oct. 4, 2015, when he closes the Cards' season-opening set with the Cubs. Lynn was teammates with John Lackey, his counterpart on Thursday, in St. Louis from 2014-15.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey beat the Cardinals in his first start at Busch last year to become the 16th pitcher to beat all 30 big league teams. The right-hander is 12-4 with a 2.02 ERA in 24 career starts at Busch.

home_pitcher_note: Leake's back-of-the-baseball-card numbers weren't terrific last season, but he did post the lowest FIP of his career and should be better positioned for success with an improved defense behind him.
away_pitcher_note: Garrett, the Reds' No. 2 prospect according to MLBPipeline.com, is making his big league debut after he spent a half-season in Triple-A last year. The lefty can throw 96 mph but has three workable pitches that can produce strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Wacha entered camp fighting for a rotation spot, and he seized it by showcasing that his shoulder is strong again. Durability remains the biggest question for Wacha, but he'll begin the season on the heels of a strong spring.
away_pitcher_note: The Reds are keeping this spot clear for 40-year-old Bronson Arroyo to make his big league comeback after 2 1/2 years away with arm injuries. Arroyo threw 90 pitches Sunday in a simulated game without issue and the club believes he is ready to go.

home_pitcher_note: Martinez dazzled over 7 1/3 scoreless innings in his first Opening Day start. He leaned heavily on a fastball-changeup mix and induced 15 swing-and-misses on that changeup. Martinez allowed five runs in 13 innings against the Reds last season.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman used 99 pitches in 4 2/3 innings on his way to a 4-3 Opening Day loss to the Phillies. After a rocky beginning, including a leadoff homer, he deserved credit for settling down and keeping the game within reach after an early 3-0 deficit.

home_pitcher_note: Even though he received limited action this spring, Roark looked like his usual self by the end of his 2017 debut. He allowed two runs on three hits in six innings with six strikeouts and retired 13 of the final 14 batters he faced.
away_pitcher_note: A bloop and a bunt cost Wainwright two runs in his five-inning season debut, but he otherwise pitched well. He induced a high number of fly-ball outs and showed faith in the changeup that he worked on throughout spring.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez was efficient and in command of the strike zone in his rain-soaked season debut. In between two rain delays, he struck out seven in six shutout innings.
away_pitcher_note: After a 17-month layoff, Lynn made his return from Tommy John surgery with a 5 1/3-inning no decision. He will continue to rely heavily on the fastball but also hopes a refined changeup can help him versus left-handers.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer has completely shaken off the effects of a finger injury that hampered him throughout the offseason and Spring Training. In his season debut, he allowed two runs in 6 2/3 innings with seven strikeouts and two walks.
away_pitcher_note: Leake was a hard-luck loser in his season debut. He allowed one run over eight innings and needed only 92 pitches to get that deep. It was a continuation of a strong spring in which Leake showed improved command and benefited from a better defense.

home_pitcher_note: Tanaka has been disappointed by his performance thus far. After surrendering a career-high 7 earned runs in just 2 2/3 innings on Opening Day vs. the Rays, the O's touched him for three runs over five. Tanaka walked 4 and hit 2 batters in that start.
away_pitcher_note: Wacha threw 83 pitches while allowing one run over eight innings in his season debut. It was a strong first impression for a pitcher who has battled shoulder issues over the past three seasons. His fastball-changeup mix has been especially effective.

home_pitcher_note: The Yankees have won both of Sabathia's starts this year, as the left-hander was the first Bombers hurler to complete both five and six innings. He held the Orioles to three runs (two earned) and six hits over six frames last time out.
away_pitcher_note: He was outstanding in the season opener vs. the Cubs, fanning 10 with no walks in 7 1/3 scoreless innings, but struggled Sunday, when the Reds tagged him for six runs (five earned) on six hits over five. He looks to rebound in his first road start.

away_pitcher_note: Wainwright allowed 11 hits while collecting only 12 outs in his last outing. He's endured too many long innings in his first two starts and hasn't generated enough swing and misses. His 2.37 FIP suggests that the defense behind him has been lacking.

away_pitcher_note: Nova had one rough inning but otherwise pitched well enough to win Wednesday, allowing four runs (three earned) in six innings, throwing 82 pitches. The eight-year veteran has never pitched at Busch Stadium or even faced the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Leake has allowed one run over 15 innings and limited opponents to one barreled ball in his first two starts. The average exit velocity on balls in play against him is 87.2 mph, more than two mph lower than it was last season.

home_pitcher_note: Wacha threw too many pitches up in the zone in his last start, and two of those were tagged for home runs. His fastball velocity is up a bit, though, which is encouraging after seasons plagued by shoulder injuries.
away_pitcher_note: Cole continued to round into form Friday at Wrigley Field, holding the Cubs' deep lineup to two runs over six innings while throwing 114 pitches. He owns a 2-3 record and 3.13 ERA in five career starts at Busch Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: The good news for Davies is that he's been here before. His ERA after three starts is 8.79, nearly identical to his 8.78 after three starts in 2016 before the righty turned a corner. Davies went 11-4 with a 3.54 ERA in 25 starts the rest of the way.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez had a bizarre outing last Saturday in which he struck out 11 while walking eight. He had particular trouble commanding the sinker. He threw 118 pitches in the outing, so he may be limited in how deep he can go in this one.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta is coming off consecutive quality starts and has yet to surrender more than three earned runs in an outing. It's a continuation of his strong finish to 2016, when he posted a 2.92 ERA over his final 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: It's been a rough start for Adam Wainwright, who has logged just 13 2/3 innings over three starts. He's averaging 20 pitches per inning and has allowed 10 of 15 leadoff hitters to reach. He's allowed 21 hits over his last two starts (8 2/3 innings).

home_pitcher_note: Anderson is one Brewers pitcher who has had some success against St. Louis. In five starts, he owns a 2.42 ERA spanning 26 innings. Anderson surrendered one run in his first 13 innings this year before a five-inning, three-run start against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn threw seven scoreless innings to stop the team’s three-game losing streak in his last start. He continues to be a fastball-first pitcher, but he leaned more heavily on his cutter last time out than usual.

home_pitcher_note: Is this the year Nelson solves St. Louis? He is 0-7 with a 7.34 ERA in nine games, eight starts against the Brewers’ division rival. Cardinals batters have hit Nelson at a .316 clip.
away_pitcher_note: Leake had a 14 1/3-inning scoreless streak snapped last time out, but he continues to pitch brilliantly. With an expanded repertoire of pitches, Leake has allowed just two runs in 21 1/3 innings this season.

home_pitcher_note: Wacha has gotten off to a strong start as he tries to put a tough 2016 season behind him. The righty has worked at least six innings in his first three starts, allowing one earned run in two of those outings, including his last one (vs. Pittsburgh).
away_pitcher_note: In his past two starts, Estrada has combined to strike out 15 batters over 13 shutout innings. This lowered Estrada's ERA to 2.63 as he continues to disrupt his opponent's timing by mixing a great changeup with fastballs high in the zone.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright pitched into the seventh for the first time this season in a win last week. Inefficiency continues to be an issue, but Wainwright’s past two outings have been steps in the right direction.

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz has displayed dominant stuff as his slider and curveball have complimented his fastball in each of his past three starts. But the Braves believe he can be even more effective if he paces himself in the early innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn looked like his old self in his first month back from Tommy John surgery. He allowed two or fewer runs in four of five starts and allowed just one run over six innings in each of his last two.

home_pitcher_note: The 42-year-old veteran says he still hasn’t gotten through a start with his good knuckleball, but he’s still allowed three earned runs or fewer in each of his five starts. His left quad has bothered him in his past two outings.

home_pitcher_note: Conley bounced back from his worst career start (6-runs, 1 2/3 innings) to win at Tampa Bay. Too many base-runners is plaguing him. While opponents are batting .240, his 1.44 WHIP is above his career average of 1.37.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez shed the silver braids and got his first win in his last start. He went 7 1/3 strong innings, trading K's for early outs to help with efficiency. Martinez relied heavily on his two-sinker, a pitch he’d like to lean on more often.

home_pitcher_note: Straily is striking out more, but also walking more batters than a year ago. His Ks per nine is 9.29, but his walks per nine is 4.94. When in the zone, he's effective. His hits per nine is 5.81, and opponents BA is .179.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright still hasn't settled in this season, and his starts continue to end early. Wainwright has pitched past the fifth just once in six starts, and he has allowed double-digit hits three times. He enters this start with a 1.967 WHIP.

home_pitcher_note: Going deep into games has been an issue for Koehler, who has pitched as many as six innings just twice in six starts. However, he hasn't gone fewer than four innings. Home runs continue to hurt him, as he has allowed nine in 30 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn has been terrific over his last four starts, combining for just two runs allowed over 25 innings. Lynn has returned from Tommy John surgery looking like the workhorse he was before, and he has also seen a recent uptick in velocity.

home_pitcher_note: Leake had his 55-inning homerless streak snapped in his last start, but he’s 6-for-6 in the quality start department and continues to be the team’s most consistent starter. He’s pitched into the seventh in four of six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Fresh from Triple-A Iowa, Butler will make his first start as a Cub since being traded from Colorado in February. The righty has allowed nearly two home runs per nine innings over his previous 28 big league starts.

home_pitcher_note: Winless in his first five starts, Martinez has been victorious in his last two. He ranks fourth in the NL with 10.71 strikeouts per nine innings and has limited opponents to a .176 batting average with runners in scoring position.
away_pitcher_note: Lester’s solid start (three hits, one earned run) became a footnote Sunday in the Cubs’ 18-inning marathon against the Yankees, but the southpaw is the only National League pitcher to throw at least 100 pitches in every start.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright continues to be plagued by inefficiency and has finished six innings just once in seven starts. He’s given up at least four runs in five of his last six outings and has allowed double-digit hits in three of his appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta struggled mightily Tuesday in Colorado, collecting only two swinging strikes with a fastball that is still suffering from a downtick in velocity. The righty allowed nine runs (five earned) on nine hits in just 3 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: After allowing two runs in his previous four starts combined, Lynn was ambushed for four in his last outing. This will be his second career start against the Red Sox, and first since 2014. He allowed one run over seven innings in that previous start.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez has started 2017 strong, with a 2.80 ERA and 42 strikeouts in 35 1/3 innings. He has thrown a quality start in each of his past four outings, including a six-inning, one-run gem against Milwaukee his last time out.

away_pitcher_note: Hellickson allowed four hits, five runs (three earned runs), four walks, two home runs and struck out four in 5 1/3 innings Sunday against the Giants. He has a 6.75 ERA in his last seven starts, struggling with his fastball command.

away_pitcher_note: What does Burnes have in store for an encore? His season debut was a pitching duel for the ages with Minnesota's Jose Berrios, as both righties took perfect games into the fifth inning and no-hitters into the seventh.

away_pitcher_note: Strasburg battled Cardinals' starter Jack Flaherty in Game 3 of the 2019 National League Championship Series. He struck out 12 over seven innings that day in the Nationals' 8-1 victory.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright didn't have his best stuff, but he battled for five innings of one-run ball against the Brewers in the home opener his last time out. He'll face the Nationals, against whom he owns a 3.10 lifetime ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Ross is riding the momentum of throwing five scoreless innings in his first start of the season on Friday vs. the Dodgers. He has not pitched in St. Louis since April 30, 2016, nearly five years ago.

away_pitcher_note: Let down by his offense, Wainwright earned a no-decision Sunday despite eight shutout innings of one-hit ball vs. the Cubs. It was his second consecutive scoreless home start and a rebound from his previous outing, when he was tagged for six runs in four frames in San Diego.

home_pitcher_note: Peacock had been scheduled to start Thursday, but he was scratched that morning after becoming ill (non-COVID related) the previous night. Peacock has appeared in 10 games (two starts) for the D-backs this year.
away_pitcher_note: Kim was one pitch away from completing six innings for the first time this season on Monday, but a fateful changeup chased him after 5 2/3 frames and handed him his second straight loss. The lefty has issued six walks over his last two games.

home_pitcher_note: Bauer has been nearly unhittable at Dodger Stadium this season. He's 3-0 with a 0.90 ERA in three starts at Dodger Stadium and has struck out 28 over 20 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off his first loss of the season, Flaherty will make his fifth career start against the Dodgers. The Burbank, Calif., native is 1-1 with a 1.08 ERA and 36 strikeouts in his four previous outings against Los Angeles.
summary: 2021-05-31 - St. Louis Cardinals (4) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (9) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Price will once again be the starter for the Dodgers' bullpen game. The left-hander has been effective in the opener role, tossing 4 2/3 scoreless innings in two starts this season. Since returning from the IL on May 18, Price has thrown 6 2/3 scoreless frames.
away_pitcher_note: Gant will look to carry over his success from May, when he had a 1.37 ERA in four starts. The right-hander has gone six innings only once in nine outings, but he's coming off a start in which he tossed five scoreless frames in a win over the White Sox.
summary: 2021-06-01 - St. Louis Cardinals (3) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Buehler is the only Dodgers pitcher to complete at least six innings in every start this season. He has allowed one earned run or fewer in each of his last three outings.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Martínez took a no-hitter into the seventh inning against the D-backs, but he ended up allowing three runs on three hits and a walk in six-plus frames. The right-hander owns a 2.82 ERA over his past six outings.
summary: 2021-06-02 - St. Louis Cardinals (3) @ Los Angeles Dodgers (14) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright has endured an odd patch of late, alternating great starts with subpar ones. Most recently, he followed up eight scoreless innings vs. the Cubs on May 23 with five innings of four-run ball vs. the D-backs on Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: In his big league debut Friday, Gutierrez allowed just two hits and one run over five innings -- a fifth-inning solo homer -- for a hard-luck 1-0 loss to the Cubs. He was aggressive in the strike zone, especially with his fastball. Gutierrez earned a second start with his performance and is now filling in for the injured Jeff Hoffman.

home_pitcher_note: Kim was excellent facing the Reds on April 23, allowing one earned run in 5 2/3 innings while striking out a career-high eight batters. However, he has yet to complete six innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Castillo was getting weak contact and looked good for five innings in his last start. But he walked the first two batters of the sixth inning, and both wound up scoring. He and the Reds are badly in need of a win when the right-hander pitches. Castillo's lone victory this season came on April 7 vs. the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Oviedo's recent stretch has been indicative of the Cardinals' as a whole, with 11 free passes over his last two starts. The club's No. 9 prospect will look to right those woes when he faces the Reds for the second time in his career, still searching for his first win.
away_pitcher_note: Mahle has turned in back-to-back scoreless outings since allowing seven runs in just two innings in his May 20 start vs. the Giants. He'll be looking to improve upon his 7.23 ERA in four home starts this season (1.47 ERA in seven road outings).

home_pitcher_note: Gant turned in one of his best performances of the year on Tuesday with six scoreless innings against the Dodgers in Los Angeles. His ERA is the fourth lowest among National League starters with at least 40 innings pitched.
away_pitcher_note: In his return from the 10-day IL and a left foot sprain, Miley looked solid in Monday's 11-1 win over the Phillies. Over six innings, the lefty allowed one earned run, six hits and three walks with six strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Martínez will look to put Wednesday’s disastrous start -- 10 runs in two-thirds of an inning -- in Los Angeles behind him. A sign of encouragement is that he'll be rested, coming off an off-day and having tossed just 39 pitches on Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: Since Bieber's rougher stretch in the middle of May, he has turned in back-to-back seven-inning starts and will look to continue that trend in St. Louis. He has made one career start against the Cardinals, allowing one run in six innings with five K's.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright was the epitome of resilience in his last outing, tossing 50 pitches in his first two frames but bearing down for just 55 across his last five. The veteran’s role gained importance with injuries ravaging the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: The Indians are hoping that Mejía will be able to reach up to 65 pitches in his quest to get stretched back out as a starter after spending some time in Cleveland's bullpen. In his first start, he tossed three scoreless frames against the Orioles.

home_pitcher_note: Stewart last started on June 5, allowing three runs in 3 2/3 innings of a road loss to the Giants. He gave up no earned runs over five on May 31 vs. the Padres. Stewart was optioned to Triple-A, but recalled to fill in for the injured Adbert Alzolay.
away_pitcher_note: Oviedo was pitching as sharp as he had been all season last time out but was yanked early when the Reds were threatening at the plate. All told, control-wise, it was a step in the right direction for the club’s No. 9 prospect, after he offered 11 free passes in his two starts prior.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks beat the Cardinals on May 21 in St. Louis as part of his most recent seven-start stretch, in which he is 6-1 with a 3.13 ERA. On Sunday in San Francisco, the righty allowed three runs over 6 1/3 innings with five strikeouts and three walks.
away_pitcher_note: Gant will look to move past his toughest outing of the year, when he set a season-high in earned runs (seven) and tied a season-low in innings (four) vs. the Reds. Continuing to be of concern is the walks, with nine over his last three starts and an MLB-leading 37 overall.

home_pitcher_note: Davies logged six shutout innings to beat the Padres on the road on Tuesday, ending with four strikeouts, two walks and one hit allowed. The righty has a 2.16 ERA in his last eight turns, including five shutout frames in St. Louis on May 23.
away_pitcher_note: Martínez took a modest step forward his last time out, though he was still tagged for five runs over four innings. The right-hander has struggled as of late, with 18 earned runs over his last six innings across three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright will look to be the steadying force for a struggling rotation, with at least seven innings in each of his last two starts. Also comforting is that Wainwright is pitching at home, where he owns a 2.62 ERA this season vs. 8.20 on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Garrett allowed two runs on five hits across four innings in his first MLB start of 2021. Miami's No. 7 prospect didn't have his best command or stuff, walking three batters and striking out three.

home_pitcher_note: Kim (right lower back tightness) will be  activated off the IL for his first start since June 4. In the end, it will be just one missed start for the lefty, who endured his second bout with the back ailment after missing two weeks in Spring Training with a similar issue.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers has gone at least six innings in each of his last three starts. In his 2021 debut, he walked a season-high four batters in a loss to the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Recently graduated from prospect status and still in search of his first win, Oviedo was two outs away from qualifying for it his last outing, but a ruinous fifth inning dashed such hopes. The Havana native will make his first career start against the nearby Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Alcantara struck out a season-high 10 batters in a start vs. his former club in April. He has a 2.38 ERA in five starts since the worst outing of his career (8 ER, 1 1/3 IP) in L.A.

home_pitcher_note: Morton will attempt to bounce back after lasting just four innings against the Marlins on Friday. The veteran hurler has allowed at least three runs in an inning in seven of his 13 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gant will look to flush his past two starts, where he's struggled to get deep after serving as a reliable stopgap. Most concerning is that the walks have come back to bite the righty, with five in his last start (all in one inning) and eight over his last two.

home_pitcher_note: Fried allowed a pair of home runs during Saturday's loss in Miami. He had allowed just one homer over his past six starts combined.
away_pitcher_note: Martínez was sharp in his last start (two unearned runs over seven frames) following two clunkers (15 combined earned runs over 4 2/3). The righty has a 3.90 ERA in 11 games (four starts) against Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson will return to the Majors to take the turn previously reserved for the recently injured Tucker Davidson. The right-hander allowed three runs over 12 2/3 innings in the two starts he made for Atlanta in May.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright will make his 15th start (20th appearance) against the team that drafted him, with a 3.63 ERA in such contests. It'll be the righty's 12th career outing back in his home state and his first since May 2019.

home_pitcher_note: Smyly completed five innings for the first time in his past three starts and exited Sunday's start in Miami without allowing a home run. The long ball has consistently hurt the veteran lefty, who is looking to win consecutive starts for the second time this year.
away_pitcher_note: Kim will hope his second go on Sunday Night Baseball will be smoother than the first, when he was chased after allowing four runs (one earned) in 3 1/3 innings on May 16. His last time out on Tuesday, he tossed a quality start despite allowing a career-high five walks.

home_pitcher_note: Skubal is 3-0 with a 2.74 ERA in his last four starts, striking out 32 batters over 23 innings. His slider has a 36.6 percent swing-and-miss rate, but he used his fastball and changeup to strike out seven Royals over six innings in a win last week.
away_pitcher_note: Still searching for his first big league win, Oviedo couldn't have done much more last time out, with seven shutout frames -- a career high in innings. Most encoraging: the 23-year-old allowed no walks, an about-face after being hampered by free passes in May.

home_pitcher_note: Injuries to fellow Tigers starters Matthew Boyd and Spencer Turnbull mean the future is now for Manning, who will make his long-awaited Comerica Park debut after holding the Angels to two runs on four hits over five innings on the road last Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: Gant's last outing was a modest step in the right direction, with three earned runs across 5 1/3 frames after lasting 5 2/3 frames and allowing 12 earned runs during his two prior starts combined. The walks remain an issue, with a MLB-leading 44 offered (15.8 percent walk rate).
